items.title: AI Founding Engineer: RF Machine Learning (SIGINT) (f/m/d)
items.card: Your role You are the founding engineer for RF machine learning at Datacept. You take responsibility for the cognitive core of our systems. The layer that turns received I/Q data into detection, classification, and understanding of emitters for SIGINT and COMINT missions. We build the foundation model in a space where no foundation models exist. The domain of RF machine learning is just in its starting phase.
items.desc: Modern conflict runs on the electromagnetic spectrum. Every drone, every radio, every radar leaves a trace in it. Datacept builds cognitive electronic warfare systems that listen to that spectrum, understand what is in it, and act on it. At the centre of this sits one capability: models that learn directly from raw I/Q data. Not from decoded protocols, not from hand-built feature extractors, but from the signal as it arrives at the antenna. This is how we handle emitters no system has seen before, in environments where new frequencies, new protocols, and new platforms appear faster than any rulebook can follow. We are looking for engineers who have this capability. Tasks Your role You are the founding engineer for RF machine learning at Datacept. You take responsibility for the cognitive core of our systems. The layer that turns received I/Q data into detection, classification, and understanding of emitters for SIGINT and COMINT missions. We build the foundation model in a space where no foundation models exist. The domain of RF machine learning is just in its starting phase. Methods that work in audio and computer vision like self-supervised pretraining, learned representations, large pretrained backbones carry over to RF only if you understand why they work. Second, the models have to run in the field. Our systems are deployed at ports, stadiums, critical infrastructure, and military sites, on hardware with real limits on compute and power. Our cloud platform enables scalable processing of the largest RF datasets, here we can deploy the full power of the foundation model. We maintain one of the largest RF datasets in the world which is constantly growing. Besides being the integral part of the engineering team you will directly work with the founders. You set the direction for RFML at Datacept, you make the architectural decisions, and as we grow you build the team around you. What you will do Design and train models that learn from raw I/Q recordings: detection, classification, and more Research and implement ML methods from other domains to improve our data pipelines Define how we evaluate: test sets, metrics, and scenarios that reflect real conditions such as domain shift between sensors, sites, and interference environments Make models fit the hardware: Besides the foundation model we need expert models that are also compact and deployable on edge Continuous testing of all pipelines in real world conditions provides continuous feedback Integrate new data sources into our data platform How we work Fast learners over specific backgrounds. We care more about how quickly you pick up new skills than where you have worked before – the spectrum changes faster than any CV Intellectual honesty. The right answer matters more than being right. You challenge assumptions, test ideas against real recordings, and pivot when the data says so Adaptability. We are organised, but things change quickly – a new idea, a customer trial, a funding deadline. You find a way to make it work and balance short-term deliverables with the long-term architecture Ownership of outcomes. You optimise your own time, focus on what matters to deliver quickly, and cut out inefficiencies. Nobody manages your calendar for you Not building in a vacuum. You stay connected to hardware, to the founders, and to the customers at the sites we protect, so that all the pieces fit together in the field Requirements Skills You have built and shipped ML systems that people depend on, preferably on signal-like data: audio, time series, sensor streams, images, video or ideally RF You understand self-supervised learning well enough to explain why a given method works, and you can move ML ideas between domains with intent You have strong mathematical fundamentals and are comfortable when the problem first has to be formulated before it can be solved You go from idea to prototype to deployed model on your own, and you ask for help when it speeds things up rather than when you are stuck You work well with few fixed structures and changing priorities You are prepared for the intensity of a founding role: long and unconventional working hours, field trials, deployments You want to contribute to Europe's technological sovereignty in a domain where it is currently lacking Helpful, not required Prior work in RF or signal-centric ML: spectrum sensing, modulation recognition, SIGINT, EW. We are just as interested in people from adjacent domains who have shown they can reason about hard problems and are eager to learn Projects that you build yourself (in the software/hardware) space. We want people that can create things and not just implement a set of requirements. items.desc: ABOUT CFM Founded in 1991, we are a global quantitative and systematic asset management firm applying a scientific approach to finance to develop alternative investment strategies that create value for our clients. We value innovation, dedication, collaboration, and the ability to make an impact. Together, we create a stimulating environment for talented and passionate experts in research, technology, and business to explore new ideas and challenge existing assumptions. YOUR ROLE We’re hiring for a Machine learning researcher: a role that blends modern ML research, GPU-heavy experimentation, quantitative modelling, and production-quality engineering. You’ll join a newly formed quant research team whose goal is to build AI-based alpha models that are predictive, reliable and efficient. You will work at the intersection of research and engineering to design, implement, and scale the AI models and algorithms that power our predictive signals. You’ll collaborate closely with data teams, the ML platform team, portfolio teams, and quant researchers across the firm. YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES • You’ll be engaged as a core contributor to our AI-based alpha models, working across research and engineering. • Research: Iterate on data pipelines, target definitions, model architectures, and training recipes (optimization strategies and hyperparameters). You’ll be responsible for both getting things to work, and developing a deeper understanding, which we can bring to the next problem. • Engineering: Develop, optimize, and scale distributed training and evaluation workflows for large-scale foundation models, working closely with the ML platform team to efficiently leverage multi-GPU infrastructure. • Keep up with the latest DL research and collaborate with diverse teams, including other quant researchers, software engineers, and hardware architects. • Attend conferences and communicate research results to the rest of the firm. Where possible, there will be the opportunity to publish your research. YOUR SKILLS Required: • Proficiency in Python and at least one deep learning framework such as PyTorch. • PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning or other quantitative domains preferred. Open also to candidates with 2/3 years experience in a AI research role. • Experience with end-to-end model development, spanning dataset construction, training, evaluation, profiling, and monitoring. • Familiarity with modern model architectures, e.g. MoEs, long-context transformers, vision-language models, efficient attention mechanisms (e.g. GQA/MQA), and new techniques such as multi-token prediction. • Experience training and scaling models using distributed training frameworks such as PyTorch Distributed, DeepSpeed, FSDP, or Megatron-LM. • Strong engineering skills, ability to contribute performant & maintainable code, profile bottlenecks, debug training failures, and work with large codebases. • Initiative and appetite for helping shape the direction of a newly formed team. Preferred (we encourage you to apply even if you don’t satisfy all of the below): • Experience optimizing LLM inference (e.g. KV-cache management, continuous batching, quantization, speculative decoding) • Familiarity with distributed execution and orchestration tools such as Ray or Kubernetes. • Experience with RLHF, RLAIF, DPO, or reward modeling. • Experience with CUDA, including developing custom kernels or other GPU performance optimizations. items.desc:
Technician position for AI applied to Human Data and Ergonomics (EPIC Project) - IT | Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia 
 Technician position for AI applied to Human Data and Ergonomics (EPIC Project) 
 Italy 
 Commitment & contract: Technician level 2, 2 years (extendable) 
 Location: IIT CRIS – Via San Quirico 19D, Genova 
 Step into a world of endless possibilities, together let’s leave something for the future! 
 At IIT, we are committed to advancing human-centered Science and Technology to address the most urgent societal challenges of our era. We foster excellence in both fundamental and applied research, spanning fields such as neuroscience and cognition, humanoid technologies and robotics, artificial intelligence, nanotechnology, and material sciences, offering a truly interdisciplinary scientific experience. Our approach integrates cutting-edge tools and technology, empowering researchers to push the limits of knowledge and innovation. With us, your curiosity will know no bounds.
 We are dedicated to providing equal employment opportunities and fostering diversity in all its forms, creating an inclusive environment. We value the unique experiences, knowledge, backgrounds, cultures, and perspectives of our people. By embracing diversity, we believe science can achieve its fullest potential.
 THE ROLE 
 You will be working in a multi-disciplinary group, where people with different backgrounds collaborate, each with their own expertise, to support IIT research activity. The Human-Robot Interfaces and Interaction (HRI²) research line is coordinated by Dr. Arash Ajoudani. We develop intelligent robots that enable natural and human-centered interaction at both cognitive and physical levels, following a socio-physical interaction paradigm.
 Within this context, the EPIC project (Ergonomics of Physical and Cognitive Interaction in Collaboration) aims to redefine ergonomics by integrating human cognitive states and physical behavior using advanced sensing technologies and AI-driven analysis. The project involves the acquisition and interpretation of multimodal human data (e.g., motion, behavioral cues, wearable signals, and visual data) to assess cognitive load, attention, and ergonomic risk in real-world scenarios.
 This position focuses on the implementation and application of AI methods to human-centered data , supporting the development of data-driven models and assisting in experimental activities. The role is primarily technical, with opportunities to contribute to research and innovation in a highly interdisciplinary setting.
 Within the team, your main responsibilities will be:
 Supporting the collection, preprocessing, and management of multimodal human data (e.g., wearable sensors, video, motion tracking).
 Implementing and applying machine learning and AI techniques for human data analysis, including classification, regression, and pattern recognition tasks.
 Assisting in the development of pipelines for estimating cognitive states (e.g., attention, cognitive load) from behavioral and physiological signals.
 Collaborating with senior researchers to validate models and interpret results in the context of ergonomics and human–robot interaction.
 Contributing to the integration of AI modules into experimental platforms and robotic systems.
 Supporting experimental campaigns, including data acquisition, annotation, and quality assessment.
 Maintaining clear documentation of code, datasets, and experimental procedures.
 Assisting in the preparation of technical reports and project deliverables.
 ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS 
 A Master’s degree (MSc) in Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Biomedical Engineering, Robotics, Computer Engineering, or a related field.
 Basic experience in machine learning and data analysis, with hands-on implementation (e.g., Python, TensorFlow, PyTorch, or similar frameworks).
 Familiarity with data preprocessing, visualization, and statistical analysis techniques.
 Knowledge of handling sensor data, time-series signals, or image/video data.
 Good programming skills in Python.
 Good knowledge of the English language.
 Strong attention to detail and structured approach to data handling.
 ADDITIONAL SKILLS 
 E Experience with human-centered data analysis (e.g., physiological signals, motion capture, behavioral data).
 Basic understanding of human–robot interaction or cognitive ergonomics concepts.
 Familiarity with ROS, MATLAB, or data annotation tools.
 Experience with deep learning techniques for image or time-series data.
 Ability to work in a challenging and international environment.
 Capacity to work both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.
 Strong motivation to learn, a proactive attitude, and good problem-solving skills.

items.title: Founding Research Scientist / Engineer
items.card: responsibilities. We're looking for people who are excited by the opportunity to help build a new AI company and want their work to have a lasting impact. If that sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you.
items.desc: London, UK · Full-time · £120k–£300k base salary + 1.2–3% equity About us At Archemind (currently stealth), we’re working on one of the fundamental challenges in artificial intelligence: making AI systems genuinely adaptive. Foundation models have made extraordinary progress, yet they still struggle to adapt to new tasks, environments and changing requirements. We believe the next major advances in AI will come not only from making models more capable, but from enabling them to learn, adapt and improve through experience. Our research combines foundation models, reinforcement learning, post-training and adaptive learning, with the ambition of developing new approaches to machine intelligence with broad real-world impact. Our founding team brings together experience from Google DeepMind and Oxford , with deep expertise in machine learning, reinforcement learning, foundation models, adaptation and personalisation. At DeepMind, our team members worked on Gemini and led research on user adaptation, evaluation and model behaviour. Our scientific advisors are internationally recognised researchers in artificial intelligence: Michal Valko , co-founder of DeepMind’s Paris office and Professor Philip Torr , University of Oxford. We also collaborate with the University of Cambridge on computational models of cognition and human states. We’ve received early backing from venture capital investors and angels, and are now preparing for our first institutional funding round. The Opportunity You’ll join Archemind at a formative stage and help shape the research direction, core technology and engineering foundations of a new AI company. You’ll have substantial autonomy to identify important problems, develop novel methods, lead research initiatives and turn promising results into real-world systems. As the company grows, you’ll help shape its technical culture and strategy, and can take on research or engineering leadership. Depending on your expertise and interests, you'll contribute to areas including: Adaptive intelligence: new approaches that let AI systems adapt to changing tasks, environments and requirements. Reinforcement learning and post-training: algorithms that improve the capabilities, adaptability and behaviour of foundation models. Learning from experience: methods that let AI systems learn from interactions, feedback and outcomes. Evaluation and generalisation: rigorous methods for measuring adaptation, learning, robustness and generalisation. New learning paradigms: architectures, algorithms and training approaches built for continual adaptation. Research to production: turning fundamental research into scalable, real-world AI systems. Who We're Looking For We're particularly interested in people who combine strong machine learning expertise with an entrepreneurial mindset , and who thrive on difficult, open-ended problems. You should have: Excellent foundations in modern machine learning, with a strong understanding of model architectures, training methods and evaluation; Strong hands-on programming skills, particularly in Python and PyTorch, JAX or equivalent frameworks; Experience conducting ML research, building sophisticated ML systems, or both; The ability to work independently and solve difficult problems with limited direction; Scientific rigour and a willingness to challenge existing approaches; A genuine interest in building a company, not just contributing to an isolated research project. items.desc: Mission: As a Forward-Deployed AI Engineer, you will bring the full range of Data & AI expertise - data engineering, data analytics, data science and machine learning - directly into a UAV platform team. You will sit with the engineers and operators who design, test and fly our aircraft in Caldas da Rainha, understand their problems first-hand, and turn them into working data and AI solutions, fast. You will work with flight logs, telemetry, video and mission data; analyse them to answer engineering questions; build models where they add value; and package the results as internal tools, dashboards and integrations with our mission and ground control software. You will be the bridge between the platform team and Data & AI: bringing in Data & AI's platforms, models and specialists, and feeding the team's needs and domain knowledge back into Data & AI's roadmap. You will work AI-first, using AI-assisted development tools such as Claude to prototype quickly, validate with users, and harden what proves useful. We are looking for a deeply technical generalist - a data scientist, ML engineer or data engineer with strong software skills - who enjoys working close to the product and the people using it, and who would rather ship a useful solution this week than a perfect one next quarter. What will be your responsibilities: Data Analytics & Data Science: Analyse flight logs, telemetry and mission data to answer engineering questions - e.g. flight performance, anomaly detection, post-flight review, test and validation analysis; Machine Learning: Identify where ML adds value for the team, then build, evaluate and iterate on models - from quick baselines to production candidates - together with Data & AI's data science and ML engineering teams; Data Engineering: Help make the team's data easy to collect, find and trust - ingestion of logs and video, consistent mission identifiers, documented and queryable datasets; Internal Tooling: Design, build and maintain internal tools - scripts, CLIs, small web apps, dashboards and automations that remove manual work from engineering, testing and flight operations; Rapid Prototyping: Use AI-assisted development workflows (e.g. Claude, Claude Code or similar) to go from a problem to a working prototype in days, test it with users, then iterate or harden it; Systems Understanding & Integration: Build a working knowledge of how our software fits together - mission and ground control software, onboard and ground data flows - so you can integrate with it, debug across it and explain it to others; Bridge to Data & AI: Be the platform team's day-to-day point of contact for Data & AI. Translate needs into clear, scoped requirements, bring in the right Data & AI teams, and help the platform team adopt their products; Field & Test Support: Support ground and flight tests when needed, making sure tools, models and data pipelines work in real-world conditions; Documentation & Knowledge Sharing: Document analyses, tools and data flows, and share AI-assisted ways of working with the team; Agile Delivery: Work within the team's agile rituals, keep work visible in Jira and Confluence, and prioritise with the platform team's Product Owner. Profile and requirements: Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Aerospace or Electrical Engineering, or a related field. Experience: 3+ years of hands-on experience delivering data, analytics or ML solutions end to end, in a data science, ML engineering, data engineering or similar role - ideally including time spent working directly with end users or customers. Strong skills in exploratory data analysis, statistics and visualisation, especially on time-series, logs or sensor data. Strong SQL and Python data stack (pandas/Polars, NumPy, Jupyter). Hands-on experience training, evaluating and iterating on ML models (e.g. scikit-learn, PyTorch), including choosing the right metrics and validation approach. Good judgement on when a model is the right answer and when a simpler analysis or rule is enough. Strong Python; experience with at least one of C#, C++, TypeScript/JavaScript is a plus. Experience building internal tools end to end: scripts and CLIs, dashboards or simple web apps (e.g. Streamlit, Dash, React), REST APIs. Ability to read, understand and integrate with existing systems you did not write - APIs, file formats, message buses, databases. Comfortable with Git, Linux, Docker and basic CI/CD. AI-Assisted Development (essential): Hands-on experience using AI coding assistants and agents (e.g. Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) to prototype and ship quickly, with the judgement to review, test and verify what they produce. Additional training can be provided in-house, but affinity, some form of experience and strong openness to these new ways of working are essential. Domain Affinity: Interest in aviation, UAVs or robotics. Experience with flight data, telemetry, ground control software, autopilots …

items.desc: About Us Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces. Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected. As an ML Research Engineer in the Visual Navigation team , you will join us at an early stage to heavily influence our technical direction. Operating out of Paris, Lausanne or Zurich, you will focus on developing Machine Learning models to enable our drones to navigate on the battlefield, with responsibilities ranging from data curation and model architecture definition to onboard inference on our drones. Responsibilities DL Algorithm Development: Design deep learning models to analyze a drone's environment in multiple modalities and enable its localization through time and space. Edge AI Optimization: Embed models on heterogeneous platforms with limited shared compute. Optimize trade-offs between model speed and accuracy to minimize pipeline latency. Cross-Team Collaboration: Partner with the VIO, Navigation, and Embedded Software teams to build a robust, real-time localization pipeline, communicating trade-offs clearly to stakeholders. Research & Innovation: Stay at the absolute forefront of scientific trends in Deep Learning to introduce cutting-edge methodologies to the team. Pipeline Management & MLOps: Build, heavily modify, and manage training, evaluation, and MLOps pipelines while ensuring reproducibility, robust logging, and version control. Validation & Field Testing: Actively participate in real-world flight tests. Analyze in-field failures to continuously iterate and improve deployed models. Candidate Requirements Educational Background: Strong academic record with a STEM degree (e.g., Computer Science, Machine Learning, Robotics, Mathematics). Deep Learning & Computer Vision Expertise: Proven track record of researching and productizing Deep Learning models for Computer Vision in the industry (Drones, Robotics, Autonomous Vehicles, etc.) Technical Competence: Proficiency in Python and DL frameworks (PyTorch/Lightning). Experience with MLOps and edge deployment optimization. Professional Attributes: Highly structured, analytical, and research-oriented. Excellent communicator able to translate complex algorithmic benchmarking to downstream users and stakeholders. Thrives in a fast-paced environment with a hands-on, “no-task-is-too-small” mentality. Commitment: 100% dedication to Harmattan AI’s mission, vision, and growth plans, ready to go the extra mile for operational excellence. We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

items.desc: About InterDigital InterDigital is a global research and development company focused primarily on wireless, video, artificial intelligence (“AI”), and related technologies. We design and develop foundational technologies that enable connected, immersive experiences in a broad range of communications and entertainment products and services. We license our innovations worldwide to companies providing such products and services, including makers of wireless communications devices, consumer electronics, IoT devices, cars and other motor vehicles, and providers of cloud-based services such as video streaming. As a leader in wireless technology, our engineers have designed and developed a wide range of innovations that are used in wireless products and networks, from the earliest digital cellular systems to 5G and today’s most advanced Wi-Fi technologies. We are also a leader in video processing and video encoding/decoding technology, with a significant AI research effort that intersects with both wireless and video technologies. Founded in 1972, InterDigital is listed on Nasdaq. InterDigital is a registered trademark of InterDigital, Inc. The team InterDigital Video Lab brings together a team of highly motivated, fast-paced, and highly skilled researchers with strong backgrounds in video compression, video processing, machine learning, and standardization. We actively contribute to leading video standards organizations, including ISO/IEC MPEG, ITU-T SG16, JVET, IETF, SMPTE, ITU-R SG6, 3GPP, DVB, and ATSC, alongside mid- to long-term incubation activities. The Media Services research group at the InterDigital Video Lab has broad experience in energy efficient technologies in video streaming and high dynamic range imaging. The research group is dedicated to improving video industry technologies, creating authentic, energy-efficient, and high-quality streaming solutions. Energy-Aware Media project in the Media Services group is dedicated to making the entire video delivery chain more energy-efficient, from content creation through end-user display, while preserving the authentic, high-quality experience users expect. The team develops technologies, tools, and standards that reduce the energy footprint of streaming video at scale. What you'll work on This position focuses on the streaming segment of the energy-aware delivery pipeline. You will design algorithms and systems that make video streaming more energy-efficient end-to-end, including adaptive bitrate (ABR) ladder design, CDN and edge delivery strategies, network-adaptive streaming, and live streaming workflows. Concrete examples of problems you might tackle include energy-aware encoding ladder optimization, CDN cache and routing strategies that reduce end-to-end energy cost, and low-power live streaming architectures based on latest live streaming protocols. Job Summary InterDigital Research & Innovation seeks a qualified candidate to join the Video Lab as a Research Scientist focused on energy-aware video streaming. The candidate will join the Energy-Aware Media project and contribute to designing innovative algorithms, methods, and standards that improve the energy efficiency of video streaming workflows, with a particular emphasis on the streaming layer. The role spans both conventional and learning-based approaches and offers a clear path to taking ownership of dedicated research workstreams as the candidate grows into the role. Responsibilities Identify research opportunities in video streaming with a focus on energy efficiency, including ABR ladders, CDN and edge delivery, network adaptation, and live streaming. Research, develop, and implement new algorithms and prototypes in the identified areas. Contribute to existing research tracks within the team and grow into leadership of dedicated workstreams over time. Disseminate results through invention disclosures and technology reference implementations, tradeshows and exhibitions, and publications in peer-reviewed conferences and journals. Promote the team's research in standards organizations such as MPEG and 3GPP, as well as SVTA, DVB or ATSC Establish and maintain collaborations with external industrial partners and academic groups. Help supervise non-permanent team members, including interns, PhD candidates, and post-doctoral researchers. Minimum Qualifications PhD in computer science, electrical engineering, image processing, signal processing, applied mathematics, or a related field. Expertise in conventional and learning-based algorithm development applied to video streaming, image processing, signal processing, or networking. Publications in peer-reviewed conferences or journals in a related area. Software development skills in Python and C/C++. Strong communication skills and a collaborative mindset for working across the team and with external partners. Curious, creative, and motivated personality. Professional working proficiency in English, written and spoken. Nice to have Hands-on …

items.desc: About Niantic Spatial AI has learned from almost everything online, but it still struggles with the physical world, where 99.5% of economic activity happens. It doesn’t know where things are, how spaces fit together, or what changes over time. That’s one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it’s the one we’re solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are. In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That’s why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right. Our team built some of the world’s most widely used maps. Now we’re building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us. About The Role You'll help build the geometric foundation of the next-generation world map — joining our World Map Research Engineering team (Geospatial Alignment) as a Research Engineer or Senior Research Engineer. This is an end-to-end applied research role that spans from strong engineering and data-systems work to R&D in 3D deep learning, transformers, and foundation models. You'll develop new algorithms, produce the research data and evaluation assets needed to advance them, and engineer the resulting capabilities into dependable production systems. The World Map team works with heterogeneous captures from phones and handheld devices, aerial imagery, LiDAR, and 360 cameras, as well as external geographic and elevation data. The central challenge is to harmonize these data sources, quantify uncertainty, and maintain consistency as the map evolves. You'll work at the intersection of cutting-edge research and scalable engineering — developing new approaches to geospatial registration, correspondence, and geometric optimization, then productionizing these technologies to directly improve Niantic Spatial's world model. What You'll Do Geospatial Registration — Develop and advance algorithms for world-scale georeferencing and registration across imagery, 3D reconstructions, point clouds, and geographic reference data. 3D Geometry & Correspondence — Build and improve methods spanning multi-view geometry, SfM, SLAM, feature matching, learned correspondence, bundle adjustment, point-cloud registration, and ICP. Data & Evaluation — Create the data and evaluation flywheel for world-scale mapping — design and maintain large-scale datasets, pipelines, benchmarks, and evaluation methodologies that expose hard failure modes, accelerate research iteration, and support production. Learning-Based 3D Reasoning — Explore and develop learning-based approaches for geospatial understanding, combining transformers and 3D foundation models with geometric priors and uncertainty modeling. Production Robustness — Design robust solutions for challenging real-world conditions: sparse or noisy GPS, changing appearance, inconsistent reconstruction quality, large geographic extents, and imperfect reference maps. Cross-Functional Collaboration — Partner with leading researchers in visual localization, 3D computer vision, and mapping — as well as engineering and product teams — to identify high-impact problems and turn research breakthroughs into end-to-end production systems. Research Communication — Share results clearly through technical writing, design reviews, and internal presentations; contribute to publications and open research where appropriate. What You'll Bring Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, Photogrammetry, or a closely related field — or equivalent research or industry experience. Strong grounding in 3D computer vision, machine learning, robotics, photogrammetry, or a closely related area. Demonstrated experience with 3D geometry and several relevant areas — multi-view reconstruction, SfM, SLAM, camera pose estimation, point-cloud registration, image-based localization, georeferencing, or sensor fusion. The ability to formulate ambiguous real-world problems, choose the right mathematical or learning-based tools, and evaluate solutions rigorously. Strong Python skills and experience with modern ML and scientific-computing libraries (PyTorch, NumPy, SciPy). Strong software engineering skills — you can turn research prototypes into reliable, scalable, and maintainable systems. A track record of taking an algorithm from research idea and experimental prototype through evaluation, benchmarking, and deployment on real-world data. Clear written and verbal communication; able to collaborate effectively across research and engineering disciplines. …

Collaborate with leading companies, research labs, and experts to create transparent, efficient, high-performing models with novel capabilities that democratize access to AI. Apply now! Job Description Snapshot AI is reshaping our world. Now you get to shape AI. This large and ambitious project aims to develop a groundbreaking family of advanced, multilingual, open source foundation models based on solid research on model architecture, data quality, scaling, generalizability, finetuning, and safety. It combines the unique expertise of AI companies and top academic labs to create models with stronger generalization and finetuning capabilities, as well as enhanced transparency and safety. This will be an inclusive, community-driven project designed to and foster a new wave of innovation and scientific advancement. The team This position is hosted by the research group on Advanced Models by Open Research & Engineering (AMOR/e), providing an ideal environment for advanced AI research and collaboration. We are a team of scientists and engineers who aim to deeply understand, explain, and build AI systems. In addition to producing highly-cited research published at top academic venues, we build models and systems that are widely used by people every day. This work is also part of the OpenEuroLLM project, a large and talented team with world-class labs and experts across Europe, supported by well-known companies with advanced knowledge of LLM development. The role We are looking for an exceptional research engineer with a passion for AI and open-source development. In this role, you will design and build cutting-edge tools and software that will shape the future of foundation models, used by millions of people worldwide. We appreciate a strong empirical and theoretical understanding of deep learning. Key Responsibilities Contribute to one or more of the following tasks: Develop and implement scalable, efficient model architectures and fine-tuning techniques. Build robust data processing pipelines to enhance learning and generalization. Design and implement benchmarks and evaluation tools. Optimize (pre)training processes and contribute to the development of innovative LLM systems with real-world applications. Create tools for continuous evaluation, monitoring, and visualization of training progress. Collaborate with a team of researchers to tackle challenging technical problems and publish in top venues. What We’re Looking For A motivated and skilled software engineer passionate about open source development and building high-quality, highly scalable AI systems as part of a team. Experience with machine learning, MLOps, foundation models, or LLMs is a strong plus. Impact This is your chance to make a real-world impact by advancing open-source foundation models while collaborating with leading AI researchers and innovative AI companies. Gain invaluable new skills as you help democratize AI, develop cutting-edge models, and create more efficient fine-tuning techniques that empower responsible innovation and drive scientific progress. Job Requirements A master’s degree (or an equivalent university degree) in Computer Science or a related field. Strong programming skills in languages like Python and experience with ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow). A pragmatic, hands-on approach to creating efficient, scalable, and reliable software systems. Ability to communicate technical ideas effectively, e.g. through discussions, whiteboard sessions, written documentation. Proven experience with open source development and tools is a plus. A true passion for AI! Conditions of Employment An exciting position within an international yet personal university. You are right in the middle of the students, on a green campus within walking distance of the central station. Besides beautiful architecture, you will find varied workplaces and excellent sports facilities. We Also Offer You Full-time employment for 1 year, with possible extension to 2 years. Salary in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, scale 11, ranging from €4,925 to €6,685 gross base salary per month (full-time), depending on your knowledge and experience. In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary. items.desc: Mission As a Forward-Deployed AI Engineer, you will bring the full range of Data & AI expertise - data engineering, data analytics, data science and machine learning - directly into a UAV platform team. You will sit with the engineers and operators who design, test and fly our aircraft in Caldas da Rainha, understand their problems first-hand, and turn them into working data and AI solutions, fast. You will work with flight logs, telemetry, video and mission data; analyse them to answer engineering questions; build models where they add value; and package the results as internal tools, dashboards and integrations with our mission and ground control software. You will be the bridge between the platform team and Data & AI: bringing in Data & AI's platforms, models and specialists, and feeding the team's needs and domain knowledge back into Data & AI's roadmap. You will work AI-first, using AI-assisted development tools such as Claude to prototype quickly, validate with users, and harden what proves useful. We are looking for a deeply technical generalist - a data scientist, ML engineer or data engineer with strong software skills - who enjoys working close to the product and the people using it, and who would rather ship a useful solution this week than a perfect one next quarter. What Will Be Your Responsibilities Data Analytics & Data Science: Analyse flight logs, telemetry and mission data to answer engineering questions - e.g. flight performance, anomaly detection, post-flight review, test and validation analysis; Machine Learning: Identify where ML adds value for the team, then build, evaluate and iterate on models - from quick baselines to production candidates - together with Data & AI's data science and ML engineering teams; Data Engineering: Help make the team's data easy to collect, find and trust - ingestion of logs and video, consistent mission identifiers, documented and queryable datasets; Internal Tooling: Design, build and maintain internal tools - scripts, CLIs, small web apps, dashboards and automations that remove manual work from engineering, testing and flight operations; Rapid Prototyping: Use AI-assisted development workflows (e.g. Claude, Claude Code or similar) to go from a problem to a working prototype in days, test it with users, then iterate or harden it; Systems Understanding & Integration: Build a working knowledge of how our software fits together - mission and ground control software, onboard and ground data flows - so you can integrate with it, debug across it and explain it to others; Bridge to Data & AI: Be the platform team's day-to-day point of contact for Data & AI. items.desc: About Us Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces. Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected. About The Role Harmattan AI is heavily pushing the boundaries of autonomous systems, where the perception of the surrounding world through visual cues is a vital component. To make sense of incoming visual data and enable mission-critical downstream decisions, we have developed custom detection models. As our product and project portfolio expands, we are diversifying our efforts in this space across multiple embedded platforms. As an ML Research Engineer in the Detect & Track Distillation team, you will join us at a very early stage, giving you a unique opportunity to heavily influence the technical direction of the team. Operating out of Lausanne, Paris, or Zurich , you will focus on taking large foundation models and distilling them into highly optimized, task-specific components. Your work will span target detection, classification, and target re-identification across time, directly tackling the hardware inference constraints of diverse edge and embedded systems. Responsibilities Model Distillation & Finetuning: Take large foundation models and compress/distill them into highly specific, efficient components optimized for smaller tasks and target detection. Edge AI Optimization: Optimize neural networks for constrained embedded systems using techniques such as quantization (PTQ vs. QAT), pruning, and LoRA. Pipeline Management & MLOps: Build, heavily modify, and manage training, evaluation, and MLOps pipelines while ensuring reproducibility, robust logging, and version control. Data Curation: Collaborate on data curation and the creation of task-specific datasets to constantly improve model accuracy. Benchmarking & Evaluation: Framework-level benchmarking of newly distilled models to evaluate performance and latency, ensuring results are fully aligned with real-world operational deployments. Research & Innovation: Stay at the absolute forefront of scientific trends in computer vision and quantization research to introduce cutting-edge methodologies to the team. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with the Detect&Track Foundation team, downstream System Engineers, Project Teams, and Mission Intelligence to deliver robust solutions. Mentorship: Depending on seniority, support the team by managing or mentoring junior engineers. Candidate Requirements Educational Background: A strong academic record with a degree in a STEM field (e.g., Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics). Deep Learning & Computer Vision: Proven experience running vision neural networks, developing target detection architectures, or managing re-identification tasks. Model Compression & Edge AI: Hands-on expertise in knowledge distillation, model compression, and deploying networks onto highly constrained embedded systems or edge hardware (e.g., Jetson, custom NPUs, wearables). Technical Competence & Infrastructure: Proficiency in MLOps, GPU compute, and building infrastructure (such as training pipeline templates and loggers). Professional Attributes: Highly structured, analytical, task-aligned, and research-oriented. Excellent communication and influence skills, with the ability to effectively translate and present complex benchmarking data to downstream users and senior stakeholders. Thrives under pressure in a fast-paced environment with a “no-task-is-too-small” mentality toward building foundational team infrastructure. Commitment: 100% dedication to Harmattan AI’s mission, vision, and ambitious growth plans, ready to go the extra mile to ensure operational excellence We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

items.desc: Machine Learning Engineers at IMC play a pivotal role in building the systems that drive training and deployment of large-scale ML models across IMC's global operations. They collaborate with quantitative researchers, hardware specialists and software engineers to build robust systems that get the most out of GPU acceleration, distributed computing and the broader open-source ML ecosystem. ML Engineers' work directly shapes how fast we can experiment, iterate and deploy - accelerating the cycle that turns a research idea into a live trading strategy. This is a unique opportunity to solve problems at the intersection of advanced machine learning and trading, where your contributions will shape the future of IMC's technology and trading capabilities. As a team, our Machine Learning Engineers broadly work across two areas: ML Research Engineering , focused on the systems and frameworks researchers use to train, evaluate and iterate on models at scale; and ML Performance Engineering , focused on making ML workloads execute as efficiently as possible, typically through GPU and low-level systems optimisation. These aren't rigid tracks, and there is overlap between them. You will bring depth of expertise in at least one of these focus areas and collaborate closely with global team members. Your Core Responsibilities The responsibilities below are representative of the role — the exact mix depends on your team, area of expertise and location. ML Research Engineering Develop large-scale distributed training pipelines that manage complex datasets and models. Partner with quantitative researchers to automate ML experiments, hyperparameter tuning and model retraining. Work with HPC specialists to optimise workflows, improve training speed and reduce compute cost. ML Performance Engineering Build and optimise low-latency inference pipelines, ensuring models deliver real-time predictions in production systems. Maximise performance in training and inference using GPU hardware and acceleration libraries. Across Both Areas Extend and improve the internals of machine learning frameworks and open-source tools to raise their performance for our workloads. Design scalable model infrastructure capable of handling high-volume trading data and delivering real-time, high-accuracy predictions. Evaluate and roll out third-party tools that enhance model development, training and inference capabilities. Your Skills And Experience Core, regardless of focus area: 3+ years' experience in machine learning, with a focus on training or inference systems. Production software engineering — Python, testing discipline and genuine ownership of systems once they ship. Machine learning fundamentals — you understand modern ML workloads beyond high-level APIs and can reason about model behaviour, correctness and performance at the level relevant to your area of expertise. A systems mindset — you reach for measurement before opinion on performance, scale or reliability issues, and can make sound build-versus-buy decisions. Strong collaboration — comfortable explaining the reasoning behind your technical decisions, working through differing perspectives with researchers and adapting your approach when the evidence supports it. Depth In One Or More Of The Following Distributed training and large-scale systems — parallelism strategy, data pipelines and checkpointing; frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow or JAX. GPU performance and low-level optimisation — reasoning about memory, compute and latency at the device level, and optimising performance across kernels, compilers and hardware (e.g. CUDA, Triton or equivalent). Production inference systems — hands-on experience building and hardening real-time, low-latency prediction pipelines in high-performance environments. Numerics and correctness at scale — low-precision effects, KV caching, batching, and knowing which optimisations stay bit-exact. Technologies listed above are examples rather than requirements; equivalent depth developed using other stacks or hardware platforms is equally relevant. Also a Plus Exposure to cloud platforms and orchestration tools. A track record of contributing to open-source projects in machine learning, data science or distributed systems. Not sure this is the one? If your strength is mainly in modelling and research direction, our QR / Modeller roles are likely a closer fit. A stabilizing force in markets since 1989, we provide liquidity across trading venues, delivering the best outcome in value and risk management to investors. Using our own technology and capital, we build proprietary systems and algorithms that operate across global markets. items.desc: TL;DR: Lovable lets over 2 million people build software using plain language, and the models behind it need to be exceptional. We're hiring an engineer who has gotten their hands dirty with post-training at scale and wants to do it again for one of the fastest-growing AI products in the world. You'll own our full post-training pipeline: translating the latest research into production training recipes, adapting them for code generation and agent workloads, and putting improved models in front of users fast. The goal is to get promising research into production within days or weeks, not months. This isn't an academic research position - you'll spend as much time in production infrastructure as in training configs, and your success is measured by what ships. Why Lovable? Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started. We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world. Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software. What We’re Looking For You've personally run post-training jobs on large language models - RFT/RLVR, preference optimization, or similar. Not just called APIs or written prompts, but actually trained and iterated on models You can write solid production code. The systems you build need to run reliably, not just produce interesting research artifacts You're fluent in at least one major ML framework (PyTorch, JAX) and comfortable working with distributed training setups and GPU clusters You understand the math behind preference optimization, reward modeling, and alignment techniques - and can reason about when each approach fits You've built or significantly contributed to evaluation systems that capture real-world quality, not just benchmark scores You can trace a model quality regression from user-facing symptoms back through serving, inference, and training - and you enjoy doing it You want to ship. Research taste matters, but at Lovable the question is always "how fast can we get this to users?" Preferred: You've worked on code generation or agentic use cases specifically You've put post-trained models into the hands of real users and seen how they hold up at scale You've owned the full loop: curating data, running training, evaluating results, deploying, and monitoring in production You have a habit of reading a paper on Monday and having a prototype running by Friday You've experimented with speculative decoding or similar techniques to improve model efficiency You have strong views on evaluation methodology and have built evals that actually predict user satisfaction You've published or contributed meaningfully to the open-source ML ecosystem What You’ll Do Own the full lifecycle of Lovable's post-training pipeline - from data curation and training runs through evaluation and deployment Apply and adapt reinforcement learning, preference optimization, and supervised fine-tuning methods to make our models better at generating code, reasoning about user intent, and acting as reliable agents Build the evaluation and experimentation infrastructure that tells us whether a model change actually helps users - covering helpfulness, safety, latency, and reliability Develop and operate the production systems that run training jobs at scale, including GPU orchestration and data pipelines Work across team boundaries with our agent, product, and infrastructure engineers to turn model gains into product improvements users can feel Investigate and resolve failures end-to-end - whether the root cause is in a training recipe, a data issue, or a serving regression Read papers, run experiments, and move fast: the goal is to get promising research into production within days or weeks, not months About Your Application Please submit your application in English. It’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join. We treat all candidates equally - if you’re interested, please apply through our careers portal.

items.desc: About this opportunity This role is being recruited by Calyptus on behalf of one of our clients. Calyptus is a specialist recruitment partner helping startups and high-growth technology companies hire across engineering, product and design. What to expect We’ll review your application and, if your experience is a strong match, one of our team will be in touch We’ll support you throughout the interview process and keep you updated at each stage If this particular role isn’t the right fit, we may consider you for other relevant opportunities with our clients ____________________________________________________________ What you will do The decision-making algorithm Design and build the core algorithm that turns live sensor data into decisions: which setpoints to change, by how much and when. Frame the problem properly. Decide whether it is best treated as prediction plus optimisation, model predictive control, Bayesian optimisation, contextual bandits, offline reinforcement learning or a combination, and justify the choice with evidence. Build process models that link settings and operating conditions to quality, scrap, throughput and energy, and that respect the dynamics of the process, including time delays, dead time and variation in raw material. Learn from historical data in which settings were rarely varied deliberately. Deal with confounding, operator interventions and changes of regime, and design safe experiments on live lines to fill the gaps. Quantify uncertainty and build in the ability to make no recommendation when conditions fall outside what the model has seen. Evaluate decisions properly: offline policy evaluation before anything goes live, and controlled trials against real production outcomes afterwards. Sensor data and features Build the pipeline from raw sensor data to model-ready features, covering synchronisation, resampling, lag alignment, filtering, missing data and faulty sensors. Develop soft sensors for quality measures that are only taken occasionally or offline. Link process data to production context such as product, recipe, material batch and shift. Detect anomalies, sensor faults and model drift, and retrain as lines, materials and products change. From recommendation to setpoint change Work out, for each adjustable variable, when a recommendation can safely be applied, taking account of process state, operating envelope, rate of change, interaction with other variables and the time the process needs to settle. Design the supervisory layer that sits above the line's existing PLC control loops, adjusting their setpoints while those loops continue to regulate the process, and make sure it never works against them. Define the conditions under which the system must hold or hand control back to the operator, such as start-up, product changeovers, alarms, sensor faults or unfamiliar material, and make handover between manual and automatic operation smooth. Monitor the effect of every change and reverse it automatically if the process does not respond as expected. Design the staged route from advisory to closed-loop operation, with clear, measurable criteria for when a line, or an individual variable, is ready for the next stage. Specify how setpoints are written back to the PLC (range checks, rate limits, reversibility and fallback to the last known good state), working with our integration partner and the customer's engineers. Machine safety functions stay in the PLC's safety layer and are never overridden by our software. Present recommendations with the reasoning behind them, in a form operators can check quickly and trust. Engineering and product Set the technical architecture for version one and make the build-or-buy decisions. Put proper machine learning operations in place: versioned data and models, testing, monitoring, deployment on edge hardware and in the cloud, and rollback. Spend time on customer sites to understand the process and earn the confidence of plant engineers. Help recruit and lead the engineers who join after you. What you will bring Essential At least six years in applied machine learning or data science, including substantial work on sensor or time-series data from physical systems such as manufacturing, energy, process industries, robotics or automotive. At least one model you took into production where its outputs drove real operational decisions. Strong time-series modelling, statistics and probabilistic methods, including uncertainty quantification. Experience with optimisation or sequential decision-making, such as model predictive control, Bayesian optimisation, bandits, reinforcement learning or constrained optimisation, and the judgement to know when something simpler will do. A good grasp of causal reasoning and of the pitfalls of learning decisions from observational data. items.desc: Machine Learning Engineers at IMC play a pivotal role in building the systems that drive training and deployment of large-scale ML models across IMC's global operations. They collaborate with quantitative researchers, hardware specialists and software engineers to build robust systems that get the most out of GPU acceleration, distributed computing and the broader open-source ML ecosystem. ML Engineers' work directly shapes how fast we can experiment, iterate and deploy - accelerating the cycle that turns a research idea into a live trading strategy. This is a unique opportunity to solve problems at the intersection of advanced machine learning and trading, where your contributions will shape the future of IMC's technology and trading capabilities. As a team, our Machine Learning Engineers broadly work across two areas: ML Research Engineering , focused on the systems and frameworks researchers use to train, evaluate and iterate on models at scale; and ML Performance Engineering , focused on making ML workloads execute as efficiently as possible, typically through GPU and low-level systems optimisation. These aren't rigid tracks, and there is overlap between them. You will bring depth of expertise in at least one of these focus areas and collaborate closely with global team members. Your Core Responsibilities The responsibilities below are representative of the role — the exact mix depends on your team, area of expertise and location. ML Research Engineering Develop large-scale distributed training pipelines that manage complex datasets and models. Partner with quantitative researchers to automate ML experiments, hyperparameter tuning and model retraining. Work with HPC specialists to optimise workflows, improve training speed and reduce compute cost. ML Performance Engineering Build and optimise low-latency inference pipelines, ensuring models deliver real-time predictions in production systems. Maximise performance in training and inference using GPU hardware and acceleration libraries. Across Both Areas Extend and improve the internals of machine learning frameworks and open-source tools to raise their performance for our workloads. Design scalable model infrastructure capable of handling high-volume trading data and delivering real-time, high-accuracy predictions. Evaluate and roll out third-party tools that enhance model development, training and inference capabilities. Your Skills And Experience Core, regardless of focus area: 3+ years' experience in machine learning, with a focus on training or inference systems. Production software engineering — Python, testing discipline and genuine ownership of systems once they ship. Machine learning fundamentals — you understand modern ML workloads beyond high-level APIs and can reason about model behaviour, correctness and performance at the level relevant to your area of expertise. A systems mindset — you reach for measurement before opinion on performance, scale or reliability issues, and can make sound build-versus-buy decisions. Strong collaboration — comfortable explaining the reasoning behind your technical decisions, working through differing perspectives with researchers and adapting your approach when the evidence supports it. Depth In One Or More Of The Following Distributed training and large-scale systems — parallelism strategy, data pipelines and checkpointing; frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow or JAX. GPU performance and low-level optimisation — reasoning about memory, compute and latency at the device level, and optimising performance across kernels, compilers and hardware (e.g. CUDA, Triton or equivalent). Production inference systems — hands-on experience building and hardening real-time, low-latency prediction pipelines in high-performance environments. Numerics and correctness at scale — low-precision effects, KV caching, batching, and knowing which optimisations stay bit-exact. Technologies listed above are examples rather than requirements; equivalent depth developed using other stacks or hardware platforms is equally relevant. Also a Plus Exposure to cloud platforms and orchestration tools. A track record of contributing to open-source projects in machine learning, data science or distributed systems. Not sure this is the one? If your strength is mainly in modelling and research direction, our QR / Modeller roles are likely a closer fit. A stabilizing force in markets since 1989, we provide liquidity across trading venues, delivering the best outcome in value and risk management to investors. Using our own technology and capital, we build proprietary systems and algorithms that operate across global markets. Our researchers, traders, and engineers work as a collective, combining rapid experimentation, advanced infrastructure, and real-time feedback to turn insight into execution and …

items.desc: At Marso, as an AI Engineer , you will own the full lifecycle of the robot’s embedded AI models: data quality, training, production reliability, and tooling that speeds up the path from development to deployment. Responsibilities Contribute to the development, training, and evaluation of embedded models that control the Marso robot. Make sure models stay reliable through every deployment stage: PoCs, field tests, and production rollout in general. Help define and assess data quality. Automate dataset extraction for model training. Cut the time-to-value between AI model development and production deployment. Build internal tools to visualize and debug data and model performance. Profile 3 to 5 years of experience in AI/ML engineering, ideally with an embedded or robotics component. Strong command of Python and deep learning frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, or equivalent). Hands-on experience deploying models to production, including under hardware constraints (edge, quantization, optimization). Solid understanding of data pipelines: collection, cleaning, labeling, and quality measurement. Rigorous and autonomous, and you enjoy testing in real-world conditions, not just in simulation. Nice to have: experience with mobile robotics, ROS/ROS2, computer vision, or sensors (lidar, cameras, IMU). We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team and encourage all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of background. Chez Marso, en tant qu’ AI Engineer , vous prendrez en charge le cycle complet des modèles d'IA embarqués du robot : qualité de la donnée, entraînement, fiabilité en production et outillage pour accélérer le passage du développement à la mise en service. Missions Participer au développement, à l'entraînement et à l'évaluation de modèles embarqués pour le pilotage du robot Marso. Garantir la fiabilité des modèles lors des déploiements : PoC, tests terrain et, plus généralement, mise en production. Participer à la définition et à l'évaluation de la qualité de la donnée. Automatiser l'extraction de datasets pour l'entraînement des modèles. Réduire le time-to-value entre le développement des modèles d'IA et leur mise en production. Développer des outils internes de visualisation et de debugging des performances des données et des modèles. Profil 3 à 5 ans d'expérience en ingénierie IA/ML, idéalement avec une composante embarquée ou robotique. Maîtrise de Python et des frameworks de deep learning (PyTorch, TensorFlow ou équivalent). Expérience concrète du déploiement de modèles en production, y compris sous contraintes hardware (edge, quantization, optimisation). Bonne compréhension des pipelines de données : collecte, nettoyage, labellisation, mesure de qualité. Rigueur, autonomie et goût pour le test en conditions réelles, au-delà du travail en simulation. Un plus : expérience en robotique mobile, ROS/ROS2, vision par ordinateur, ou capteurs (lidar, caméras, IMU). Nous sommes engagés dans la construction d’une équipe diverse et inclusive. Toutes les candidatures qualifiées sont les bienvenues et nous accordons une attention particulière aux compétences, à l’impact et à la capacité à contribuer au projet. Compensation Range: €45K - €75K

items.desc: Welcome to the Fraunhofer Institute for Integrated Circuits IIS! As the largest institute within the Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft, we have been conducting research for over 30 years in diverse fields such as artificial intelligence, microelectronics, sensor systems, data acquisition, signal processing, and signal transmission. Talented individuals from various engineering and natural science disciplines will find a wide range of exciting research topics under one roof. A few highlights that reflect our innovative strength include 5G/6G mobile communication technologies, generative AI in speech and signal processing, neuromorphic computing and X-ray imaging for e-mobility that’s just the beginning! What sustainable solution will you find with us? Be part of change The group »AI-Based Communication Systems« within the Wireless Systems and Standardization (WSS) department in the Communication Systems division at Erlangen focuses on research, implementation and demonstrations of AI-enabled wireless communication systems. The group investigates machine learning and mathematical optimization techniques for sensing and communication applications to optimize radio link, end-to-end network performance, and edge inference across terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks. Our activities span a wide range of methodologies, from link/system-level simulation and data-driven experimentation to real-time evaluation with hardware-aware training and deployment. Wireless Algorithms: Implement and optimize communication and signal processing algorithms for real-time wireless and sensing systems. Project Support: Contribute to technical documentation, proposal preparation, and customer demonstrations. You’ll work closely with researchers and engineers to integrate state-of-the-art computational chemistry methods with machine learning approaches, driving
items.desc: This an Atlantic portfolio venture. About the Venture This early-stage venture is building a discovery engine for chemistry, comprising a platform for running end-to-end simulations of chemical reaction systems, and a world model + agent stack that uses the simulation platform to discover new chemistry. Their goal is to build backend scientific data infrastructure to meet the demands of AI systems that can truly accelerate and automate the discovery layer of chemistry. Both founders hold PhDs in Chemistry from the University of Oxford, and the venture has already secured pre-seed funding. They are now building out their founding team. The Role As a Computational Chemist, you will play a central role in shaping the scientific foundations of the venture's technology, helping develop the computational methods and workflows that underpin its end-to-end chemical reaction simulation platform. You’ll work closely with researchers and engineers to integrate state-of-the-art computational chemistry methods with machine learning approaches, driving progress towards the venture's strategic and scientific objectives. You’ll take ownership of developing, validating and optimising the computational chemistry components of the platform, with a particular focus on reaction mechanisms, reaction kinetics, molecular dynamics and the modelling of complex chemical environments. You will design, implement and refine scalable scientific workflows for generating, processing and analysing chemical reaction data, improving the accuracy, reliability and computational efficiency of simulations. Beyond your core scientific responsibilities, the team is looking for someone who can contribute to strategic research decisions, bring strong independent scientific judgement, and help shape the interdisciplinary research culture of the company at an early stage. What You'll Work On Foundation models for chemical reactivity: The team is building and training foundation models for chemical reactivity with a variety of data modalities. You'll help curate this foundational data corpus by developing cheminformatics and computational chemistry workflows for generating data from combinatorial enumeration, as well as robust data filtering, clustering and validation routines. Computational methods: The team is working on efficient computational methods from which foundational data is generated and the platform is validated. You'll be responsible for developing protocols for estimating solvation and entropy factors in chemical reaction steps. This involves keeping up to date with published literature for ideas and inspiration. Generative models: The venture is expanding its foundational data corpus beyond combinatorial workflows. You'll help design, validate and benchmark the generative model architectures that accomplish this. Chemical reaction simulation: The team is building out an end-to-end chemical reaction simulation platform. You'll be involved in designing the architecture and assembling the platform, as well as developing benchmarks and validation protocols against computational and experimental methods. World models and agents: The venture will be developing an agent + world model stack that operates on the simulation platform. You'll be responsible for formulating the action space in which the world model is trained and the agent explores new chemical reaction space. What They're Looking For The team is looking for someone who enjoys being given a blank canvas and the chance to create something spectacular with it. In particular, someone who brings: A PhD in Computational Chemistry, Machine Learning, or a related field. Intellectual curiosity: Someone who enjoys venturing outside their comfort zone, exploring new ideas and applying their knowledge and experience to unfamiliar domains. An entrepreneurial mindset: Someone who thrives in an early-stage environment, enjoys building things from scratch and is excited to grow beyond the traditional boundaries of their role. Independent thinking and scientific judgement: Someone who can take ownership of complex challenges, contribute new ideas and help shape the scientific direction of the venture. A collaborative approach: Someone who can build strong relationships across the team and actively contribute to shaping and nurturing the company culture as it grows. An instinct for building great working environments: Someone who understands the importance of the right tools, systems and ways of working to help themselves and the wider team do their best work.

We develop intelligent robots that enable natural and human-centered interaction at both cognitive and physical levels, while leveraging advanced interfaces and AI-based algorithms to allow robots to perceive, interpret, and better understand the environment in which they operate.

Specifically, the project aims to analyze images acquired through standard RGB cameras to estimate the usage and degradation state of PPE, providing a more objective and quantitative evaluation of their condition.

Activities include the design and implementation of a controlled camera-based acquisition setup, dataset generation and management, and the development of computer vision and machine learning models for PPE condition assessment.
 Within the team, your main responsibilities will be:
 Designing and implementing a controlled camera-based acquisition setup for collecting image data related to PPE condition.
 Supporting the acquisition, annotation, and management of image datasets.
 Developing computer vision and machine learning algorithms for the analysis of PPE usage and degradation.
 Contributing to the development and validation of data processing and model training pipelines.
 Collaborating with senior researchers in the experimental evaluation of the developed methods.
 Maintaining clear documentation of datasets, code, and experimental procedures.

 Good programming skills in Python.
 Good knowledge of the English language.
 Strong attention to detail and structured approach to data handling.
 ADDITIONAL SKILLS 
 Knowledge of data-driven approaches for visual inspection and condition assessment.

We design and develop foundational technologies that enable connected, immersive experiences in a broad range of communications and entertainment products and services. We license our innovations worldwide to companies providing such products and services, including makers of wireless communications devices, consumer electronics, IoT devices, cars and other motor vehicles, and providers of cloud-based services such as video streaming. A position built for a curious mind who
items.desc: How do you predict a material's properties when the number of possible atomic configurations exceeds 2^2500? That is the bottleneck our IRESNE (nuclear fuel physics) and LIST (AI) teams have just cracked with PULSE, a generative (VAE) method published in Nature Scientific Reports, already cutting computational cost by more than two orders of magnitude (22,282 CPU hours down to 85 on a test case). With no known equivalent in the international literature, PULSE positions CEA as a pioneer in generative sampling of the configuration space of chemically disordered materials. This 24-month postdoc gives you the opportunity to drive this method toward its next generation, leading three ambitious, parallel research axes: pushing model accuracy on systems of several thousand atoms with an IWAE architecture; equipping it with the ability to quantify its own uncertainty — a prerequisite for any use in nuclear safety; and, in the second year, tackling a high-value exploratory axis — generalizing PULSE to a continuous latent space, opening the door to any disordered crystal or alloy. You will work at the heart of an all-CEA consortium bringing together two complementary strengths — atomistic nuclear fuel physics at IRESNE and state-of-the-art generative AI at LIST — with access to CEA supercomputers, the freedom to publish in top-tier journals, and the prospect of seeing your results feed directly into reactor safety analyses through the PLEIADES platform. A position built for a curious mind who wants to combine cutting-edge generative AI research with concrete impact on a strategic nuclear-energy challenge. #CEA-List ; #Research Engineer Profil du candidat You hold a PhD in Physics, Applied Mathematics, or Computer Science, with experience in deep generative models (VAE, diffusion) and Python/PyTorch. Applications from statistical physicists are welcome. STILL HESITATING? Remote work options to reduce commuting time and improve your quality of life. A rich employee benefits committee (CE) with social, cultural, and sports activities. A dynamic workplace at the heart of a vibrant hub, surrounded by schools and tech companies. Interested? Apply—this position is perfect for you!
