items.desc: Informations Générales Nom Chargé de contrôle des coûts, du plan de charge et de l’IA Junior F/H Ref # 16854 Date de publication Lundi, octobre 19, 2026 Pays France Region Île-de-France Ville Châtillon Business Unit (BU) ADF Type de Contrat CDI Date de début souhaitée 01-12-2026 Horaire de travail Horaire Normal Télétravail Télétravail possible Métier G - GESTION DE PROJET Métier Orano Projets 023 - Contrôle des Coûts Description Description Depuis plus de 50 ans, Orano recycle sur le site de La Hague les combustibles usés issus des centrales nucléaires. Aujourd'hui, avec le projet Aval du Futur, Orano relève un nouveau défi : concevoir et construire les installations industrielles qui accompagneront la filière jusqu'à l'horizon 2120, dans une perspective de performance durable, de sûreté renforcée et d'excellence technologique. Par son ampleur financière (40 à 50 milliards d'euros), sa technicité et son intensité, le projet Aval du Futur (AdF) figure parmi les plus grands programmes industriels d'Europe. Rejoignez-nous en tant que Chargé de contrôle des coûts, du plan de charge et de l'IA ! Au sein de la Direction Performance et Contrôle de Projet (DPCP) du Projet Aval du Futur (AdF), vous contribuez : Au processus de contrôle des coûts et au pilotage financier du projet (consolidation budgétaire, reporting mensuel des coûts et fiabilisation des coûts à terminaison) A l'élaboration et au suivi du plan de charge du Projet A la transformation digitale et au déploiement d'outils d'intelligence artificielle (IA) En appui aux responsables « Contrôle des coûts » et « Outils, données et méthodes » de l'équipe Cost Control de la DPCP, vos missions principales seront : 1. Élaboration et suivi du plan de charge Contribuer à la structuration du plan de charge et à la consolidation des données de l'ensemble du Projet en appui aux exercices semestriels d'analyse capacitaire des métiers de l'ingénierie Collecter les hypothèses et en assurer la traçabilité Assurer le suivi et l'analyse des écarts par rapport aux prévisions Contribuer à l'amélioration et au développement d'outils intégrés pour le suivi du plan de charge, des transferts de ressources et du plan de recrutement 2. Appui au contrôle des coûts Consolider les données et analyser les écarts par rapport aux prévisions concernant la répartition des ressources et la part de sous-traitance des études Réaliser des contrôles trimestriels des pointages afin de vérifier leur cohérence avec le plan prévisionnel de transfert des ressources 3. Reporting, Power BI et déploiement de l'IA Contribuer à l'intégration des données entre ECOSYS et Power BI, ainsi qu'au développement de tableaux de bord Power BI intégrés à ECOSYS Contribuer à l'identification, au test et au déploiement de cas d'usage de l'IA sur les activités de contrôle des coûts du Projet Profil souhaité Profil recherché : Formation supérieure Bac+5 (école d'ingénieurs ou université) en contrôle de gestion, finance, gestion de projet, gestion des données ou dans un domaine technique pertinent pour l'ingénierie industrielle. Première expérience en contrôle des coûts, contrôle de gestion, gestion de projet ou PMO, acquise dans un environnement industriel, d'ingénierie ou d'énergie, ou sur un grand projet. Compétences techniques : Bonne compréhension des principes de contrôle des coûts d'un projet industriel et des métiers de l'ingénierie. Maîtrise avancée d'Excel et bonne connaissance de Power BI. items.desc: Share page Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology : Chair of Learning Technical Systems In order to fill a fixed-term position in full-time (39.83 hours/week = 100%) at the earliest possible date , we are looking for a Research associate (m/f/x) The group conducts core research in artificial intelligence and machine learning, with a primary focus on online decision-making under uncertainty. Our work spans areas such as (inverse, deep, and causal) reinforcement learning, multiarmed bandits, and learning in multi-agent systems involving cooperation, competition, and coordination. We are particularly interested in how intelligent systems can adapt across changing domains and recover from suboptimal or biased decisions through principled approaches to domain adaptation and algorithmic recourse. While our methods are generic and applicable across diverse fields—including medicine, education, and finance—we primarily apply them to engineering and technical systems, such as the Internet of Things, nextgeneration communication networks, and robotics. The researcher will work on the development of robust and efficient collective algorithmic recourse methods to enhance the resilience of mission-critical networked systems. The project lies at the intersection of machine learning, optimization, and multi-agent systems, addressing challenges arising from resource volatility and uncertainty in dynamic environments. The work will include both theoretical analysis—covering efficiency, scalability, and convergence—as well as the application of the proposed methods to optimize networked systems. Scope: full-time Duration: fixed-term, 36 months Start: at the earliest possible date Apply by: 2026-11-02 Your tasks: The main task is to conduct high-quality and independent research in the area of collective algorithmic recourse, with a particular focus on its application to networked systems, and to publish the results in leading scientific venues. Your profile: An excellent, recently completed Ph.D. or M.Sc. degree with a strong publication record in Computer Science (Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence), Mathematics (pure or applied, including Operations Research), Electrical Engineering (Signal Processing, Information Theory), or related fields such as Theoretical Physics. A solid mathematical background. Strong programming skills. Excellent command of English, both written and spoken. We offer: We offer a cooperative and friendly working environment that encourages collaboration, creativity, and professional growth. The position is part of a DFG Priority Programme (SPP) , which provides excellent opportunities for scientific exchange and networking . The successful candidate will have the chance to participate in project meetings, workshops, and joint events within the programme to further develop their expertise and build research connections. items.desc: Turn complex energy questions into clear, data-driven decisions Are you analytical, curious and motivated by solving challenging problems? Join Axpo Polska as a Junior Data Scientist and help turn commercial and trading questions from the Polish energy and gas business into robust analyses, models and data products. You’ll work with colleagues across the business to strengthen decision-making through high-quality data science. You bring critical thinking, a constructive, questioning mindset and the determination to work through complex issues—not just produce numbers, but understand what they mean and communicate the insight clearly. What you’ll do Develop, maintain and improve predictive machine-learning models, including time-series, regression and classification models. Translate commercial and trading questions into analyses, models and practical data products. Work with large-scale data and use tools such as SQL, Python, GCP and Snowflake to deliver reliable analytical solutions. Explore and visualise results, including with Power BI, and explain findings to technical and business stakeholders. Check data quality, validate analytical outputs and critically review code and model results. Document your work clearly so that analyses and models can be understood, maintained and handed over effectively. Contribute to improving processes, performance and efficiency across the business. What you’ll bring A bachelor’s degree in data science, mathematics, IT, economics, finance, energy or a related field. At least one year of experience in data science or a similar analytical role. Strong SQL skills, including practical knowledge of query optimisation. Practical Python skills and a sound understanding of data science and machine-learning concepts, such as model evaluation, clustering and common model types. An analytical approach, strong critical-thinking skills and confidence working through complex, ambiguous problems. A challenging mindset: you question assumptions, investigate root causes and look for better ways to solve problems. A proactive, self-sufficient and entrepreneurial approach, with a can-do attitude and the ability to work well with multiple stakeholders. Good spoken and written English. Polish is relevant for the local business context; knowledge of the Polish energy and gas industry is an advantage. What we offer Full-time employment contract. Development in an international company that is shaping the face of the energy market. A progressive medical care package that takes care of your health and well-being. Co-financing of the Multisport card, enabling the use of various forms of physical activity. Foreign language classes during working hours. Flexible working hours and the possibility to work in hybrid mode. An office with a beautiful view, located in the city center. A motivated team, ready to guide you through your daily challenges. Details about the salary range for this position and other components of the compensation package will be provided in the following stages of the recruitment process. items.desc: Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world. We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today. Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development. We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation. About the Role We're building highly automated laboratory systems that combine robotics, scientific instruments, custom hardware, and software to run biological experiments at scale. You'll help design, prototype, and build the mechanical and mechatronic systems that connect and support our laboratory automation infrastructure. This includes developing custom components, integrating sensors and actuators, improving existing systems, and solving practical engineering challenges that arise as we scale. This is a highly hands-on role. You'll work alongside our automation engineers on projects from initial concept and CAD through prototyping, testing and deployment in the lab, and take on more ownership as you grow. You'll work closely with our automation, software, and biology teams to develop reliable hardware that can operate continuously with minimal human intervention. We're looking for someone who enjoys building things, learning quickly and solving practical technical problems, and turning ideas into working systems. If you've spent your studies building robots, rockets, race cars or 3D-printed contraptions and want to do that full-time on real problems, we'd love to hear from you. Location: Lausanne, Switzerland (on-site) · Type: Full-time · Experience: 0–3 years (recent graduates welcome) What You'll Do Design, prototype, and build custom mechanical and mechatronic components for laboratory automation. Develop fixtures, mounts, enclosures, robotic interfaces, and other custom hardware. Integrate sensors, actuators, motors, and control electronics with guidance from senior engineers, improving automation capabilities and system monitoring. Take designs from CAD through fabrication, assembly, testing and deployment. Help integrate new hardware and scientific instruments into automated workflows. Troubleshoot mechanical, electrical and integration issues, learning to find root causes and build robust fixes. Contribute to improving existing hardware for reliability and maintainability. Help source components and work with suppliers on custom parts. What We're Looking For A degree (BSc or MSc) in mechanical engineering, mechatronics, robotics or a related field. Hands-on experience designing and building physical things, whether from internships, a thesis, student teams (e.g. Formula Student, EPFL Xplore/Rocket Team, robotics competitions) or personal projects. Comfortable with CAD (SolidWorks, Fusion 360, Onshape or similar). Experience with 3D printing, basic machining or mechanical assembly. Comfortable working safely in a workshop with hand and power tools (e.g. drills, saws, grinders). Some exposure to sensors, motors or basic electronics (Arduino-level is great). Curious, eager to learn, and happy to get your hands dirty. You ask good questions and take initiative. Nice to Have None of these are required. They're things you'll pick up here. Exposure to laboratory automation, scientific instrumentation, or robotic systems. Experience with data acquisition or sensor integration. Familiarity with PCB design, embedded electronics, microcontrollers, or control systems. Experience with fluidics, pneumatics, or vacuum systems. Experience operating workshop machinery such as a lathe, milling machine, CNC or laser cutter. Programming experience in Python, C/C++, or similar languages. A solid grounding in mechanical design principles, materials and tolerances. Membership of a student competition team, or open-source hardware or maker projects. Application deadline We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis.

items.desc: Salary Starting salary is £41,064 per annum Basis Full time Job category/type Academic Job reference R6358 The University of South Wales seeks a highly motivated Research Fellow for a full-time position in Civil or Materials Engineering. This role is funded by the Switch to Net Zero Buildings (SNZB) PBIAA grant via UKRI EPSRC for the project: "Accelerating Net-Zero Construction in the Swansea Bay City Region: Validation and Industrial Scale-up of Low-Carbon Building Components Using Local Waste-Derived Materials". The post holder will bridge the "translation gap" between laboratory innovation and industrial adoption. Working closely with industrial partner Carapace Slate Ltd, you will investigate ultra low-carbon roofing and façade products using regionally relevant waste materials, such as waste derived aggregates. The Post holder will investigate the rheological and curing behaviour of low-carbon formulations, assess the impact of waste aggregate variability, and establish validated processing envelopes for repeatable automated manufacturing. Responsibilities include producing demonstrator components, adoption-ready datasets, high-quality publications and grant proposals. The post holder should hold a PhD in Civil Engineering, Materials Engineering or a related discipline, with resin, cement and concrete knowledge and experience desirable, alongside good communication and networking skills for collaboration with partners. This is a full-time, fixed-term position based at the Pontypridd Campus. We welcome applications from the UK and worldwide; consideration is subject to relevant UK Visas & Immigration permissions. items.desc: Au cœur de l’innovation de Dassault Systèmes, vous rejoindrez une équipe du département 3D MODSIM & AI Technologies, dédiée à l’exploration et au développement de nouvelles technologies de modélisation et de simulation 3D. Notre ambition : inventer les futures technologies permettant de rendre la conception 3D plus intuitive, automatisée et intelligente. Pour concevoir un objet manufacturé, les designers utilisent des logiciels de Conception Assistée par Ordinateur (CAO), tels que CATIA. Ces outils permettent de construire précisément une géométrie à partir d’opérations et de fonctions géométriques combinées entre elles. Dans ce contexte, notre équipe travaille notamment sur un projet visant à générer automatiquement des arbres de spécifications CAO à partir de maillages, en s’appuyant sur des techniques d’optimisation et de géométrie algorithmique. Nous explorons également, dans le cadre plus large des Industry World Models, l’application de l’IA générative à la création de modèles 3D exacts. L’objectif est de pouvoir générer des modèles 3D à partir de données provenant de différentes modalités — texte, image, critères de style, contraintes d’assemblage, simulation physique, pratiques de design, etc. — afin de guider et de contrôler la génération. Vous rejoindrez ainsi un environnement de R&D à la croisée de l’IA générative, de la géométrie algorithmique, de la modélisation 3D et de la simulation numérique, avec l’opportunité de contribuer à des technologies de rupture pour la conception industrielle. Vos missions Dans le cadre de ce projet, vous participerez à la conception et au développement de nouvelles solutions permettant de générer et piloter automatiquement des modèles CAO exacts. Vos missions seront les suivantes : Concevoir et développer des modèles et approches génératifs pour la génération de modèles CAO, pouvant s’appuyer sur des pipelines agentiques pour piloter et orchestrer les différentes étapes de génération ; Concevoir et développer en Python des composants permettant de guider la génération de modèles 3D à partir de contraintes issues notamment de la simulation physique ; Explorer différentes méthodes permettant d’intégrer des contraintes géométriques, physiques ou de conception dans les processus de génération ; Réaliser une veille technologique sur les avancées en IA générative, modélisation 3D, géométrie algorithmique et simulation numérique ; Évaluer et valider les performances des approches développées en termes de précision, efficacité, robustesse et scalabilité ; Collaborer avec les équipes R&D de Dassault Systèmes afin d'intégrer les technologies développées dans des solutions concrètes de conception et de simulation 3D. Vos Qualifications Vous êtes titulaire d’un diplôme d’ingénieur ou d’un Master universitaire, avec une spécialisation en informatique, mathématiques appliquées ou domaine connexe ; Vous disposez de solides compétences en mathématiques appliquées, notamment en simulation numérique et/ou optimisation ; Vous possédez une bonne maîtrise du développement logiciel, ainsi qu’une solide culture en informatique, algorithmique et conception d’algorithmes ; Vous maîtrisez Python et disposez d’une expérience avec au moins un framework de Deep Learning, tel que PyTorch ou TensorFlow ; Une expérience ou un intérêt pour l’IA générative, les modèles de Deep Learning, la géométrie algorithmique, la modélisation 3D ou la simulation numérique sera particulièrement apprécié ; Vous êtes à l’aise pour évoluer dans un environnement de R&D et d’innovation, à la frontière entre recherche et développement logiciel ; Vous maîtrisez parfaitement l’anglais, à l’écrit comme à l’oral. Nous rejoindre c'est aussi Intégrer une entreprise scientifique au cœur de l’innovation technologique, portée par une forte croissance depuis plus de 40 ans Principaux avantages et bénéfices : Environnement multiculturel Cadre de travail convivial axé sur le bien-être et la santé (salles de sport & de musique, conciergerie…) Engagement en faveur de la diversité et de l’inclusion Politique dynamique de développement de carrière : plan de formation, mobilités internes, etc Inclusion statement As a game-changer in sustainable technology and innovation, Dassault Systèmes is striving to build more inclusive and diverse teams across the globe. We believe that our people are our number one asset and we want all employees to feel empowered to bring their whole selves to work every day. It is our goal that our people feel a sense of pride and a passion for belonging. As a company leading change, it’s our responsibility to foster opportunities for all people to participate in a harmonized Workforce of the Future.

items.desc: The AIT Austrian Institute of Technology is Austria’s largest Research and Technology Organisation (RTO) . We aim to transform scientific excellence into innovation with impact. Together with our partners, we develop technologies and solutions for a sustainable, resilient, and digitalised future, strengthening Europe’s competitiveness and technological sovereignty. Our international teams combine cutting-edge research with strong implementation expertise to create measurable value for industry and society. Our Center for Digital Safety and Security is looking for new Ingenious Partners for our location in Vienna (Giefinggasse, 1210). In the Reliable Wireless Communication and Sensing research team , we develop energy efficient solutions for reliable wireless 5G/6G communication and sensing. We are enthusiastically researching integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) methods in mobile indoor and outdoor scenarios using 5G/6G physical layer technologies. CENTER FOR DIGITAL SAFETY & SECURITY You will investigate cooperative positioning and advanced localisation algorithms for wireless communication networks in complex outdoor scenarios, using AIT’s Radio-Frequency lab and an optical tracking system to obtain accurate ground-truth position measurements. You will validate the algorithms through numerical simulations and empirical measurements, while contributing to the development and deployment of a distributed wireless network using state-of-the-art hardware and software-defined radio (SDR) technology. You will publish your research results at conferences and in international journals. You will gain expertise in a research field with a wide range of applications, spanning construction, logistics, aviation, railways, agriculture, robotics, and defence. You will work alongside an international team of scientists and expand your professional network through European-wide research projects. Among other initiatives, we are committed to increasing the proportion of women in our company and therefore particularly welcome applications from female applicants. items.desc: About NestAI NestAI is a European AI lab for defence delivering the adaptive operating system for modern battlefield operations. We develop adaptive intelligence for unmanned and command systems: AI that continuously learns from operational data and adapts to changing conditions. NestOS is our open, modular and interoperable platform that enables this at scale and keeps capability evolution under sovereign European control. Founded in 2025 by Peter Sarlin, whose previous company Silo AI became Europe's largest AI acquisition, NestAI brings together over 200 engineers and scientists and partners with leading European defence forces and industry. Role Description Europe builds the drones and the platforms. It does not build the models that fly and command them. The intelligence inside Europe’s defences runs on models trained elsewhere, and access to the best models can be cut off overnight. NestAI is building sovereign AI models for defence to change this . We are initially focusing on models for battlefield autonomy and orchestration, bringing together real operational data, simulation and synthetic data to build models that can continuously adapt as the battlefield changes. We're hiring a Model Developer to join the initiative. This is a senior developer role where you’ll join the team developing models for battlefield autonomy and orchestration. In order to succeed, you need deep technical competence in model development, including pre-training, fine-tuning, evaluation, multimodal learning, long-context reasoning, model compression, and understanding of deployment trade-offs. What you'll do Build and iterate on model prototypes across both tracks: from early proof-of-life experiments to benchmarking against existing C2/Edge functionality. Work hands-on with multimodal and geospatial reasoning problems: LLMs currently fall short on spatial/geospatial reasoning, and closing that gap is core to the effort (e.g. representing maps and terrain as something a model can actually reason over, not just look at). Help stand up early evaluation harnesses and benchmarks so progress is measurable against a real baseline, not just a demo. Work against simulated/synthetic data in the near term, coordinating with whoever owns the data owners on what's usable and what needs to be built. Contribute technical judgment upward: flag when a direction isn't working rather than quietly grinding on it, making sure we fail fast. What we're looking for Solid hands-on experience training, fine-tuning, and evaluating ML models - ideally including multimodal or large-scale model work. You understand trade-offs in where to use single-task models and where large models. Comfort working in a still-forming, under-specified environment: this project doesn't have settled tooling, data, or team structure yet, and the ability to make progress without waiting for all of that to exist is more valuable than following an established playbook. Genuine curiosity about geospatial/spatial reasoning, simulation, or embodied AI problems - these show up constantly in this domain and current foundation models handle them poorly. Nice to have: a PhD in a relevant quantitative field; prior exposure to autonomous systems, simulation, or edge-constrained systems; experience or interest in defence, dual-use, or other regulated/sovereign-technology environments. Why join NestAI At NestAI, you’ll build meaningful, real-world technology as part of a world-class team of engineers, scientists, and experienced professionals. You’ll work on systems where reliability genuinely matters, contribute to Europe’s security and resilience, and solve problems that demand depth, trust, and craftsmanship. If you want to build with purpose - and with leading experts in the field - you’ve come to the right place. Perks & Benefits We offer a growing set of practical benefits to support your work and wellbeing, day to day: Occupational healthcare (currently provided by Mehiläinen) Epassi Flex benefit (sports, culture, commuting, wellbeing) Lunch benefit (25% tax-free coverage) Regular team lunches and all-hands events Your choice of Mac or PC Holiday allowance (50% of holiday salary) Phone benefit according to company policy (subscription and device) We are continuously developing and expanding our benefits as we grow. Practicalities Employment is subject to applicable security screening (including SUPO, where required). NestAI is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all applicants based on their skills, experience, and potential.

items.desc: CVEDIA · Remote, anywhere (with overlap with European afternoons) · Full-time ﻿(This job requires Advanced English (C1) proficiency - with the ability to communicate fluently and handle complex, fast-paced technical and professional tasks.) About CVEDIA CVEDIA builds computer vision models and applications that run in real products on server and edge hardware around the world. We train our models on synthetic data, and much of our model work already runs through AI agents. We have made the full move to this way of working across the whole company, and we are looking for people who want to push it further. About the role We are hiring an engineer who builds systems out of AI agents and knows enough about training neural networks to point those agents at the right problems. You are not just a software developer and not just a data scientist. You may have spent your evenings building your own agent harnesses, fine-tuning open-source models and running them on your own GPU, and getting groups of agents to finish real work. If so, you probably already know what this job is. You will start by learning our automated model pipeline, and then take on your first model. After that, the work widens to new research, new customer problems, and our software. You will design the harness, and the agents will do much of the work. What you will do Learn, maintain, and improve our synthetic data pipeline and automated training system. Take over a model as your first project, and improve it with an agent loop that generates its own data as it goes. Build closed loops in which agents train detectors and classifiers, test them against validation sets, and improve them with little human input. Design systems that handle false positives from the field, flagging only uncertain detections and fixing the rest automatically. Lead our research on vision-language models, fine-tuning them for specific tasks and using agents to track the latest techniques. Solve new detection and classification problems for customers and partners by building new models or extending existing ones. Apply agents beyond models, for example to QA automation and to code bases that find and fix their own bugs. Share what works with the team, and present results to customers when a project needs it. You may be a good fit if You have built your own agent harnesses or agentic workflows, and you can show us the work. You have run many agents at once, and you have dealt with the usual problems: communication between agents, token use, and checking that tasks are really finished. You have a background in professional software engineering on both Windows and Linux, including Git and an issue tracker. You have fine-tuned or quantized open-source models, for example by training LoRAs, and you have run them locally. You know the model landscape from the early GPT models to today's open-source ones, including where each one is strong and where it fails. You communicate clearly, both within the team and with customers. You have a real passion for AI and agents, and you try new tools and ideas without being asked. It would be great if you Have trained object detectors or classifiers for computer vision. Own a GPU capable of running local models because you wanted to experiment. Have served models with engines such as vLLM or SGLang, or take part in their communities. Have a background or a strong interest in data science. You do not need to tick every box. If you have the mindset, we will teach you the computer vision and research side. Why CVEDIA Agents as your everyday tools. You will use Claude, Codex and self-hosted models every day, with no limits on applying them to your work. Work that ships. Our models already run in production on edge boxes around the world, and your systems decide how fast they improve. Real influence. We are a small team. You will work directly with all of us and help shape how the whole company works with AI. People who think like you. We discuss agent behaviour, harness design, and model quirks every day. You will have people to compare notes with. Where and how you work The role is fully remote. You need to overlap with European afternoons, which is when most of our meetings happen. Pay depends on your experience. We will discuss it with you early in the process. How to apply (please submit your resume/CV in English only) Send us links to things you have built, such as repositories, harnesses, write-ups or side projects. Tell us about one problem you hit with agents and how you solved it. We care more about this than about your CV. The interview is one conversation with our technical leads about your own experience with agents and models. We will ask what you have tried, what broke, and what you learned. These are questions that only hands-on experience can answer. CVEDIA welcomes applicants from every background and country. We judge your work, not your title or your path to it.

Build and validate models for forecasting, risk stratification, personalisation, resource allocation and decision support. Design and analyse experiments, and apply causal inference methods to understand what works, for whom and under which conditions. Evaluate results carefully, accounting for uncertainty, bias, missing data and the limitations of available evidence. Develop reproducible analyses and clearly documented code in Python and SQL. Collaborate with ML engineers, data engineers and domain experts to turn analytical findings and models into practical solutions. Communicate methods, findings and limitations clearly to technical colleagues and partner teams. Use Causal Foundry products in your work and help improve its analytical capabilities, data quality and usability through feedback to Engineering. Contribute analyses and technical writing to scientific papers and other research outputs. Your projects may include work with public-sector and health partners in Rwanda. Some partner collaboration may involve travel. What we are looking for A PhD in statistics, computer science, mathematics, physics or a closely related quantitative field. A strong foundation in statistical modelling and machine learning, with depth in one or more relevant methods. Experience applying quantitative methods to data through your PhD research or other academic projects. Strong Python skills and the ability to work with data using SQL. Experience using AI agents and coding tools such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor for data exploration, analysis, modelling and research workflows, with careful validation of generated code and results. Experience gained during your PhD or personal projects is sufficient An understanding of sound model evaluation, experimental design and the principles of causal inference. Care for reproducibility, clear documentation and version control. The ability to work through ambiguous questions, explain methodological choices and recognise the limitations of an analysis. Curiosity, initiative and a collaborative approach to solving problems. Experience with contextual bandits or reinforcement learning, time-series forecasting, survival analysis, Bayesian methods, optimisation or recommender systems. Publications, open-source contributions or other examples of rigorous, reproducible research. Why Causal Foundry Apply your research skills to real operational decisions and problems with social impact. Explore advanced methods and see how they perform when applied, deployed and measured in practice. Work closely with colleagues across data science, engineering and domain disciplines. Build experience across the full data science process, from defining a question to evaluating the impact of a solution. Collaborate with people and partners across cultures and geographies. This is an on-site role in our Barcelona office. Working hours are 10 am to 7 pm.

items.title: Bioinformatics Research Associate
items.card: About the role Are you an ambitious bioinformatician looking to apply cutting-edge computational biology to one of the most exciting challenges in global health? As a Bioinformatics Research Associate in this specially created position by Imperial College to support the success of the £7.5 million ARIA-funded M2M (Mechanism to Medicine) programme, you will play a central role in helping to uncover the innate immune
items.desc: Job number: MED06012 Salary or Salary range: £50,733 - £59,484 per annum Posting End Date: 10 Nov 2026 About the role Are you an ambitious bioinformatician looking to apply cutting-edge computational biology to one of the most exciting challenges in global health? As a Bioinformatics Research Associate in this specially created position by Imperial College to support the success of the £7.5 million ARIA-funded M2M (Mechanism to Medicine) programme, you will play a central role in helping to uncover the innate immune mechanisms that protect individuals from respiratory viral infections and accelerate the development of a new generation of preventative medicines. Working alongside Professor Ajit Lalvani and a multidisciplinary consortium of leading academic and industry partners (including Prof Marko Nikolic at UCL, Dr Adrian Grzybowski at AnuBio inc., and Dr Sarah Teichman at University of Cambridge among others), you will integrate and analyse complex multi-omics datasets, generate novel biological insights, and directly support AI-driven approaches to therapeutic discovery. What you would be doing Lead the harmonisation, integration and analysis of large-scale multi-omics datasets, including single-cell transcriptomics, epigenomics and proteomics data. Develop, maintain and document robust computational pipelines for processing and quality control of next-generation sequencing and proteomics datasets. Identify innate immune correlates of protection through advanced bioinformatics analyses across clinical and laboratory-derived datasets. Work closely with AI and mathematical modelling teams to ensure bioinformatics outputs support downstream predictive modelling and therapeutic development. Collaborate with researchers across Imperial, UCL, industry partners and international collaborators to deliver key project milestones. Present findings to collaborators, funding bodies and at scientific conferences, while contributing to high-impact publications and future grant applications. Support implementation of FAIR data principles and open science practices across the programme What we are looking for We are looking for a highly motivated and collaborative scientist with: A PhD in bioinformatics, computational biology, computer science, genetics, statistics or a closely related discipline (or equivalent experience). *Candidates who have not yet been officially awarded their PhD will be appointed as a Research Assistant within the salary range £45,399 - £48,876 per annum. Strong programming skills in Python, R, Bash and/or Perl and experience working in Unix/Linux environments. Hands-on experience analysing genomics and multi-omics datasets, including scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, bulk RNA-seq and proteomics data. Experience developing reproducible computational workflows using tools such as Nextflow, Snakemake or equivalent workflow management systems. Experience working with HPC or cloud computing infrastructure and modern reproducible research practices. Excellent analytical, communication and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team. A passion for translating complex biological data into impactful scientific discoveries. What we can offer you The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity. Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression. As a member of research staff, you have 10 development days to use to develop your skills and explore your career prospects Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes). Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing . The opportunity to work on a pioneering £7.5 million ARIA-funded programme with the potential to transform protection against respiratory viral diseases. A unique position at the interface of bioinformatics, immunology, artificial intelligence and translational medicine. Collaboration with leading researchers and partners from Imperial College London, UCL, industry and international institutions. Genuine opportunities to contribute to high-impact publications, establish scientific independence and support future funding applications. Further information This is a full-time post (35 hours per week), fixed-term (48 months). If you require any further details about the role, please contact: Sofia Koletsi s.koletsi@imperial.ac.uk

items.desc: Jobbeskrivning Vill du arbeta med datorseende och AI där millisekunder kan göra skillnad? Nu söker vi en junior Computer Vision Engineer till ett teknikbolag i Lund som utvecklar intelligenta sensorsystem för att upptäcka och förstå vad som händer i omgivningen. Tekniken kombinerar eventbaserade kameror med AI för att identifiera objekt och analysera deras rörelse med mycket låg fördröjning. Tillämpningarna finns inom bland annat autonom mobilitet, robotik och industriell automation – med målet att göra fordon och maskiner säkrare och mer responsiva. Svenskt medborgarskap är ett krav för tjänsten. Om rollen Du arbetar i gränslandet mellan mjukvara, sensorer och maskininlärning. Här får du möjlighet att omsätta teori i praktiken, arbeta med verkliga sensordata och följa hur algoritmer presterar i fysiska miljöer. Dina arbetsuppgifter kan bland annat innebära att: Utveckla och utvärdera algoritmer för objektdetektering, klassificering och rörelseanalys. Bearbeta, visualisera och analysera data från kameror och sensorer. Bidra till träning och utvärdering av modeller för datorseende. Testa algoritmer och analysera precision, robusthet och svarstider. Samarbeta med kollegor inom mjukvara och hårdvara för att integrera och verifiera lösningar. #SIE Grundläggande kvalifikationer Vem är du? Du är i början av din karriär och har en relevant högskole- eller civilingenjörsutbildning inom exempelvis datateknik, elektroteknik, teknisk fysik eller motsvarande. Du kan vara nyexaminerad eller ha något års erfarenhet. Vi tror att du har: Kunskaper i Python och/eller C++. Grundläggande förståelse för bildbehandling, datorseende och maskininlärning. Arbetat med relevanta projekt under utbildningen, genom examensarbete eller på egen hand. Förmåga att kommunicera tekniska resonemang på engelska. Erfarenhet av OpenCV, PyTorch, TensorFlow, kamerakalibrering, 3D-geometri eller eventbaserade kameror är meriterande. Du behöver inte kunna allt från start – vi värdesätter din tekniska nyfikenhet, problemlösningsförmåga och vilja att utvecklas. Därför är rollen spännande Du får arbeta nära teknik där algoritmer möter den fysiska världen. Rollen passar dig som vill förstå hela kedjan från sensordata till detektering och respons, och som motiveras av att utveckla lösningar med tydlig praktisk betydelse. Meriterande färdigheter, egenskaper och erfarenheter Vi erbjuder Mer information Ivan Kertan +46761287807 Ivan.Kertan@sigma.se Tjänst Junior Computer Vision Engineer Kompetensområde Systemdesign, Systemutveckling, Software development Plats Lund Svar senast 2026-11-08

items.desc: About the role We are looking for an engineer to help build the knowledge graph and AI services behind a SaaS platform. The work involves turning documents and records into structured information, connecting related data and supporting search and matching with clear supporting evidence. This role is open to both seniors and mid-level engineers with relevant practical experience. You will work with the AI lead, application developers and platform engineer, taking responsibility for agreed components as the product develops. Hands-on experience building knowledge graphs and working with ontologies is essential. What you will work on You will develop RDF models and ontology modules for candidate and vacancy data, including skills, qualifications and employment history. The models need to preserve source evidence, record changes and represent conflicting information. You will write SPARQL queries, maintain taxonomy mappings and use SHACL to validate graph data. You will build Python services and repeatable processes to map structured records and extracted information into the graph. This includes incremental updates, duplicate handling and checks before data is published. Working with the wider team, you will ensure corrections and approved deletions reach the graph and search indexes, with tenant boundaries and access permissions respected. You will help develop information extraction services for documents, messages and transcripts, using FastAPI and schema validation. Extracted information should retain its source location and the model version used, with uncertain or unsupported results available for review. You will also contribute to entity resolution, using identifiers and similarity methods to find related records without losing the evidence behind a match. You will contribute to semantic and hybrid search, using embeddings, metadata filters and graph queries where appropriate. Search and matching results should be evaluated against representative examples, with explanations grounded in source evidence. You will write tests and maintain evaluation examples for the components you build. Alongside quality, you will consider latency, processing cost and failure handling. You will work with colleagues on service integration, investigate issues and document the decisions needed to maintain your work. What you need We are interested in what you have built and can explain, rather than a fixed number of years in the role. You should have professional software or data engineering experience and be comfortable delivering tested components within a team. You must have personally implemented an RDF knowledge graph and designed or extended an ontology in a working system. This includes writing SPARQL queries, defining classes and relationships, modelling taxonomies and applying SHACL constraints. You should be able to explain your modelling choices and show how you handled data quality or query problems. Familiarity with graph terminology or querying an existing graph alone is not sufficient. Practical experience with at least one RDF graph store, such as GraphDB, Stardog, Apache Jena or Amazon Neptune, is required. You should understand stable identifiers, named graphs and provenance, and be comfortable using or learning relevant standards such as SKOS, PROV-O and JSON-LD. You need good Python and SQL skills, experience building APIs with FastAPI or a similar framework, and a working knowledge of schema validation and automated testing. You should be able to integrate services with application data and handle errors, retries and timeouts sensibly. You should have practical experience in some of the following areas: information extraction, entity resolution, embeddings, semantic search or retrieval evaluation. You do not need to have delivered every part of the AI stack, but you should be able to assess the quality and limitations of the methods you use. You will need to communicate technical decisions clearly and work closely with other engineers. An understanding of data privacy, access controls and the risks of sending sensitive information to model providers is expected. AI outputs must preserve uncertainty and follow the product’s agreed human review controls. Useful additional experience Experience with Azure, model evaluation tools such as MLflow, or search platforms such as Azure AI Search or OpenSearch would be useful. Other relevant experience includes document processing, ontology versioning, graph query optimisation, event-driven processing and deploying AI services. These are areas you can develop further in the role. What we would like to hear about Please describe a knowledge graph or ontology you have worked on, your personal contribution and the tools you used. We would like to understand a modelling or implementation problem you encountered, how you approached it and what you learned from the result.

MLFlow, Nvidia Triton, etc.). Collaborer activement à l'intégration des solutions au sein de systèmes complexes et à fort enjeu technologique. Tes qualités et compétences techniques sont les suivantes : Maîtrise approfondie et expertise en PyTorch, JAX ou frameworks/librairies similaires. Maîtrise des concepts et outils MLOps ainsi que de l'écosystème associé (outils type MLFlow, Nvidia Triton, etc.). Solide appétence et compétences en Architecture IT et Infrastructure. Formation et/ou expérience probante sur des environnements HPC (High-Performance Computing) très appréciée. (Note : Nous recherchons un profil purement ML Engineer avec une culture MLOps/Infra, et non un profil ciblé Data Scientist ou AI Engineer). Communication : Aptitude à communiquer clairement et efficacement avec des interlocuteurs techniques et fonctionnels. Travail en équipe : Capacité à collaborer au sein d'équipes pluridisciplinaires. Autonomie et proactivité : Capacité à prendre des initiatives et à être force de proposition sur la partie technique et infrastructure. Curiosité technique : Intérêt poussé pour l'optimisation des performances et les innovations MLOps/HPC. Informations supplémentaires Pourquoi choisir NEXTON ? Nous te proposons des avantages et des opportunités pour enrichir ton expérience professionnelle et personnelle tout au long de l'année : ▶ Des communautés dynamiques pour t'accompagner dans ton parcours. ▶ Des Meet Up pour développer tes compétences. ▶ Des formations pour te réinventer et progresser. ▶ Des événements sportifs et festifs pour t'épanouir. ▶ Un forfait mobilité durable pour faciliter ton quotidien et encourager la mobilité douce. ▶ Un téléphone de dernière génération pour rester connecté. From Marketing, to Treasury and Fraud teams - there are lots! Don’t worry, we’ll help you get acquainted Understand the tech culture, the detail of the tech stack and how we build stuff. And any of these would be great, but aren’t essential: Experience in applying machine learning methods to real-world problems Familiarity with supervised ML Familiarity with Time Series Forecasting Familiarity with supervised LLM chat and workflow automation Familiarity with Computer Vision Familiarity with Bayesian Learning Familiarity with Causal Inference Familiarity with Recommender Systems Familiarity with Graphs and GNNs Familiarity with Reinforcement Learning Familiarity with Apache Spark or other distributed processing frameworks Experience in software development Additional Information What You Get Back (London) Stock options in one of the fastest growing European FinTechs An annual self-development budget Pet friendly offices Salary of £58,000 / year ‍♀️Lots of team activities ️ A paid 6-week sabbatical leave after four years For everyone, everywhere. We're people building money without borders — without judgement or prejudice, too. We believe teams are strongest when they are diverse, equitable and inclusive. We're proud to have a truly international team, and we celebrate our differences. Inclusive teams help us live our values and make sure every Wiser feels respected, empowered to contribute towards our mission and able to progress in their careers. If you want to find out more about what it's like to work at Wise visit Wise.Jobs. Keep up to date with life at Wise by following us on LinkedIn and Instagram.

items.desc: ¿Quiénes somos? Somos una compañía tecnológica especializada en Inteligencia Artificial, IA Generativa, Analytics, Gobierno del Dato, Cloud y arquitecturas Event Driven, pero sobre todo somos un equipo con conocimiento, criterio y muchas ganas de hacer las cosas bien. Nos mueve la excelencia tecnológica , la orientación a negocio y el sentido común, pero también el entusiasmo, la creatividad y la convicción de que la tecnología necesita alma, propósito y personas capaces de convertir la complejidad en soluciones reales. ¿Qué buscamos? Buscamos a un/a Data Scientist enfocado en forecasting de series temporales para el área de Finanzas con 2-3 años de experiencia en responsabilidades similares. Perfil con base técnica sólida —escribe buen código y se maneja con soltura en el desarrollo, aunque la productivización final se aborde en colaboración con Data Engineers—, que trabaja de forma autónoma : gestiona su propio tiempo, toma la iniciativa sin dirección constante y da visibilidad proactiva de su avance. Comunica resultados e implicaciones de negocio por sí mismo/a , sin necesidad de supervisión constante. Imprescindibles: Grado en Data Science, Informática, Ingeniería, Matemáticas, Estadística, Finanzas cuantitativas o afín (MS/PhD valorable). Python sólido, con buenas prácticas de desarrollo (código limpio, testeado, versionado). PySpark para procesamiento distribuido de datos a gran escala. Experiencia demostrable en forecasting de series temporales (clásico y/o ML). Aplicación de técnicas de ML sobre datasets grandes (clustering, clasificación, regresión, detección de anomalías). Mentalidad de optimización y rendimiento : diseña con el rendimiento en mente y propone mejoras que impactan en métricas (tiempos de procesamiento, consumo de recursos). SQL para acceso y transformación de datos. Comprensión sólida de metodologías ágiles. Inglés profesional. Será un PLUS: Dominio financiero (planificación, riesgo, FP&A, tesorería). Tecnologías de bases de datos en cloud (p. ej. AWS) y despliegue en infraestructura cloud de datos/analítica. Contenedores y pipelines/microservicios (Docker, Kubernetes). Herramientas de dashboarding (Dash, Tableau). ¿Qué ofrecemos? Pertenecer a una empresa a la vanguardia tecnológica y centrada en las Personas, ponemos al trabajador en el centro de todo lo que hacemos. Creemos en una cultura horizontal, sin egos, en un entorno donde se valoran tanto las ideas como las personas. Contrato indefinido y salario entre los 30.000 y 36.000 euros brutos/año de entrada, ajustado según tu experiencia (nuestro plan de carrera incluye 2 revisiones anuales). También tendrás a tu disposición un plan de formación especializado, participación en la propiedad y los beneficios de Mática: Wetaca gratuito en la oficina dos días a la semana, horario flexible con facilidades para trabajar desde donde quieras, seguro de salud, retribución flexible con Cobee, además de las vacaciones habituales, ofrecemos una semana extra en Navidad y tres días adicionales en Semana Santa. También recibirás un divertido Welcome Kit con portátil (podrás escoger entre varios modelos Mac o Windows), móvil, botella personalizada, auriculares bluetooth y golosinas. Cuando estés en nuestra oficina, en el centro de Barcelona o Madrid , la fruta, los cafés y los refrescos corren a cuenta de Mática. ¡Ah! Y si eres amante de los animales, te gustará saber esto: ¡nuestras oficinas son Pet-friendly! items.desc: Turn complex energy questions into clear, data-driven decisions Are you analytical, curious and motivated by solving challenging problems? Join Axpo Polska as a Junior Data Scientist and help turn commercial and trading questions from the Polish energy and gas business into robust analyses, models and data products. You’ll work with colleagues across the business to strengthen decision-making through high-quality data science. You bring critical thinking, a constructive, questioning mindset and the determination to work through complex issues—not just produce numbers, but understand what they mean and communicate the insight clearly. What you’ll do Develop, maintain and improve predictive machine-learning models, including time-series, regression and classification models. Translate commercial and trading questions into analyses, models and practical data products. Work with large-scale data and use tools such as SQL, Python, GCP and Snowflake to deliver reliable analytical solutions. items.desc: Horario de 8:00 a 15:00 · Presencial en el Hospital Clínico San Carlos (Madrid) · 34.000 € brutos anuales Plazo: el anuncio se cerrará el domingo 25 de octubre. ¿Te imaginas que el software que despliegas esta semana cambie el mes que viene cómo se trata a los pacientes con un infarto? En el IA Lab de CardioRed1 eso pasa. Somos el equipo de inteligencia artificial de la red cardiovascular que coordina el Hospital Clínico San Carlos, uno de los grandes hospitales universitarios de Madrid. Trabajamos dentro del hospital, en el Servicio de Cardiología, junto a los cardiólogos que usan lo que construimos. Buscamos a un/a ingeniero/a informático/a que también sea ingeniero/a de datos: alguien que sepa construir software que funcione en producción, mover y modelar datos clínicos reales y aplicarles IA, y que quiera hacerlo en un problema que importa. Dónde trabajarás En el Hospital Clínico San Carlos (Madrid, Moncloa), dentro del Servicio de Cardiología. En un equipo joven y multidisciplinar de ingenieros, científicos de datos y cardiólogos, con mucha autonomía y poca burocracia. Con datos clínicos reales: informes de miles de pacientes, resultados de laboratorio y registros de hemodinámica y del Código Infarto. Qué harás Construir y mantener pipelines de datos (ETL) que extraen información de los sistemas del hospital (historia clínica, laboratorio, mensajería HL7, bases de datos) y la dejan limpia y modelada. Desarrollar aplicaciones y servicios internos (backend en Python, APIs, interfaces web sencillas) que usan cardiólogos y gestores cada día. Desplegar y operar esas herramientas en servidores del hospital (Docker, Linux): instalación, usuarios, incidencias y nuevas versiones. Integrar modelos de lenguaje (LLM) en los flujos de trabajo: lectura de informes clínicos, apoyo al informe de alta, transcripción de consultas, anonimización. Montar motores de indicadores de calidad asistencial basados en las guías de la Sociedad Europea de Cardiología, con cuadros de mando y alertas. Trabajar con Informática y Protección de Datos para que todo cumpla con la seguridad y la normativa. Un día cualquiera 8:00. Revisas los registros del pipeline nocturno y las incidencias que han dejado los usuarios de nuestras herramientas. 9:30. Te sientas con un cardiólogo para entender qué necesita antes de programarlo: qué datos, de qué sistema y para qué decisión clínica. 11:00. Programas. Por ejemplo, un conector que recibe mensajes HL7 del hospital, los normaliza y los carga en nuestra base de datos, con sus tests. 13:00. Reunión corta del IA Lab: qué ha avanzado cada proyecto, qué está bloqueado y qué toca presentar al jefe de servicio. 14:00. Despliegas una nueva versión de una herramienta en el servidor y avisas a sus usuarios de lo que cambia. 15:00. Te vas a casa. La tarde es tuya. Qué buscamos Grado en Ingeniería Informática y máster (o formación afín: Telecomunicación, Ingeniería Biomédica, Ciencia de Datos, o Matemáticas y Física con un perfil fuerte de programación). Python avanzado y buenas prácticas de desarrollo: Git, tests y código legible. SQL y bases de datos relacionales (PostgreSQL o similar). Experiencia construyendo pipelines de datos (ETL) y APIs (FastAPI, Flask o similar). Soltura con Docker y Linux. Experiencia integrando modelos de lenguaje (LLM) vía API en aplicaciones reales. Valoraremos Interoperabilidad sanitaria (HL7, FHIR, CIE-10) e historia clínica electrónica. Machine learning (scikit-learn, PyTorch) y estadística. Frontend sencillo (React, Streamlit), cuadros de mando (Power BI) y Power Platform. Seguridad, anonimización de datos y RGPD. Proyectos propios o un GitHub del que estés orgulloso/a. Qué ofrecemos 34.000 € brutos anuales. Jornada completa de 8:00 a 15:00, presencial en el Hospital Clínico San Carlos. Impacto directo en pacientes, con datos clínicos reales que muy pocas empresas tienen. Un equipo joven y cercano, donde tus ideas llegan rápido a la práctica. Participación en publicaciones científicas y congresos de cardiología. Aprender medicina de la mano de cardiólogos y aplicar la IA de verdad. Cómo inscribirte Envía tu CV y una carta de motivación a través de LinkedIn (puedes juntarlos en un mismo PDF). En la carta, cuéntanos por qué te interesa este puesto y qué proyecto tuyo te enorgullece más. Si tienes un repositorio, inclúyelo: nos dice más que cualquier título. Recibimos solicitudes hasta el domingo 25 de octubre.

items.desc: Vos missions au quotidien Vous êtes passionné par l’ingénierie logicielle ? Vous aimerez intervenir sur des projets stratégiques dans une équipe projet constituée de développeurs ? Concrètement, vous serez amené à : Participer à la conception et au développement de modèles d'IA et de machine learning pour l'application STAR Analyser des données complexes liées à la trésorerie pour en extraire des insights pertinents Collaborer avec les équipes techniques et métiers pour comprendre les besoins spécifiques à la gestion de la trésorerie Contribuer à la mise en place de solutions IA visant à améliorer l'efficacité et la précision des opérations de trésorerie Rédiger des rapports et présenter les résultats des analyses Utiliser les outils de Continuous Delivery mis à disposition des projets IT Durée du stage : 6 mois. Et si c’était vous ? Vous préparez un Bac+5 en Université ou Ecole d'ingénieur Vous avez des connaissances en machine learning, deep learning et traitement de données Vous maîtrisez les outils de programmation (Python, R, etc.) et les bibliothèques d'IA (TensorFlow, PyTorch, etc.) Vous avez la capacité à travailler en équipe et à communiquer efficacement Vous etes curieux, autonome et avez le sens de l'initiative Vous êtes force de proposition et effectuez de la veille technologique You’re fluent in english ? Vous êtes le candidat idéal ! Plus qu’un poste, un tremplin Rejoignez-nous pour faire grandir vos ambitions ! Dès votre arrivée, vous serez intégré dans nos équipes et apprendrez chaque jour aux côtés de nos experts qui vous accompagneront dans vos missions. Progressivement, vous gagnerez en autonomie sur vos projets pour faire de cette expérience un vrai accélérateur de carrière. Vous découvrirez également toute la diversité de nos métiers, dans un secteur qui évolue et innove en permanence. A la fin de vos études, diverses opportunités pourront s’offrir à vous, en France et à l’international. Pourquoi nous choisir ? Offre variée de restaurants d’entreprise et de cafétérias à tarifs compétitifs ainsi que des titres restaurants dématérialisés quand vous êtes en télétravail Créer, oser, innover, entreprendre font partie de notre ADN. Si vous aussi vous souhaitez être dans l’action, évoluer dans un environnement stimulant et bienveillant, vous sentir utile au quotidien et développer ou renforcer votre expertise, nous sommes faits pour nous rencontrer ! Vous hésitez encore ? Sachez que nos collaborateurs peuvent s’engager quelques jours par an pour des actions de solidarité sur leur temps de travail : parrainer des personnes en difficulté dans leur orientation ou leur insertion professionnelle, participer à l’éducation financière de jeunes en apprentissage ou encore partager leurs compétences avec une association. Les formats d’engagement sont multiples.

items.desc: Craft: Data, Analytics & Strategy Job Description: PM Growth Analytics – Data Scientist, Marketing Measurement & Insights We are looking for a Data Scientist to join Growth Analytics in a hands-on role focused on understanding the true value of Performance Marketing. You will combine experimentation, modelling, and business analysis to evaluate marketing effectiveness, explain performance, and translate findings into clear recommendations that guide investment decisions. This role sits at the intersection of measurement, analytics, and business decision-making. It is suited to someone with solid analytical foundations, strong commercial curiosity, and the ambition to grow into a Senior Data Scientist. You will take ownership of defined analytical projects, with support from experienced colleagues on more complex methodological and strategic questions, and build increasing independence and influence. Your work will span incrementality testing, marketing mix modelling (MMM), and understanding why realised returns differ from predictions. You will work closely with buying teams, analysts, and technical partners to connect evidence across measurement approaches and help assess Performance Marketing alongside the wider marketing mix. A sister team focuses on model training infrastructure and production pipelines; your focus will be on analytical rigour, interpretation, and applying findings to business decisions. Your Role Within Our Kingdom Connect Measurement to Business Value: You will translate analytical findings into practical recommendations on marketing investment, campaign optimisation, and performance expectations. You will work with stakeholders to connect marketing outcomes to player behaviour and revenue, and follow through to understand whether recommendations improve decisions. Deliver Marketing Measurement: You will design and analyse incrementality tests and contribute to MMM and other causal analyses, selecting appropriate approaches with guidance where needed. You will own defined projects from the initial business question through analysis, interpretation, and stakeholder readout. Explain Business Performance: You will investigate where and why ROI is over- or under-predicted, distinguishing changes in player value, campaign mix, measurement assumptions, and underlying business performance. You will help stakeholders understand whether a gap calls for action, further investigation, or more time to gather evidence. Turn Evidence into Decision Frameworks: You will help translate experiment and model outputs into calibration inputs, performance benchmarks, and repeatable analytical tools. You will bring together evidence from incrementality, attribution, and MMM to support planning and evaluate Performance Marketing within the wider marketing mix. Bridge Business and Technical Questions: You will work with marketing stakeholders to frame actionable questions and with technical partners to define data and analytical requirements. You will help ensure measurement outputs are interpreted correctly and used effectively in day-to-day decisions. Communicate Clearly and Improve Our Approach: You will explain findings, assumptions, and uncertainty to technical and non-technical audiences. You will challenge inconsistencies, identify opportunities to improve existing approaches, and take on broader ownership as your expertise develops. Skills To Create Thrills Education: Degree in Statistics, Economics, Data Science, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience. Experience: Hands-on experience in data science, analytics, experimentation, or marketing measurement, with examples of taking an analytical question through to a useful business recommendation. Statistical Foundations: A solid understanding of statistical modelling, hypothesis testing, experimentation, and the distinction between correlation and causation. Practical experience with at least one relevant measurement approach and an interest in developing broader expertise. Execution: Able to independently deliver well-scoped analytical work, validate results, and manage priorities. Comfortable working through ambiguity while recognising when to seek input or challenge the original question. Commercial Mindset: Curious about what drives business performance and able to connect analytical results to investment choices, expected returns, and practical actions. Technical Skills: Proficiency in Python or R and SQL, with experience working with complex datasets and producing clear, reproducible analyses. Communication: Able to explain complex findings in accessible language, make recommendations supported by evidence, and communicate uncertainty without losing the practical message. Judgement and Growth: Thoughtful about assumptions, data quality, and methodological limitations. Receptive to feedback, quick to learn, and ready to develop towards broader project ownership and greater influence over …

items.desc: Craft: Data, Analytics & Strategy Job Description: PM Growth Analytics – Data Scientist, Marketing Measurement & Insights We are looking for a Data Scientist to join Growth Analytics in a hands-on role focused on understanding the true value of Performance Marketing. You will combine experimentation, modelling, and business analysis to evaluate marketing effectiveness, explain performance, and translate findings into clear recommendations that guide investment decisions. This role sits at the intersection of measurement, analytics, and business decision-making. It is suited to someone with solid analytical foundations, strong commercial curiosity, and the ambition to grow into a Senior Data Scientist. You will take ownership of defined analytical projects, with support from experienced colleagues on more complex methodological and strategic questions, and build increasing independence and influence. Your work will span incrementality testing, marketing mix modelling (MMM), and understanding why realised returns differ from predictions. You will work closely with buying teams, analysts, and technical partners to connect evidence across measurement approaches and help assess Performance Marketing alongside the wider marketing mix. A sister team focuses on model training infrastructure and production pipelines; your focus will be on analytical rigour, interpretation, and applying findings to business decisions. Your Role Within Our Kingdom Connect Measurement to Business Value: You will translate analytical findings into practical recommendations on marketing investment, campaign optimisation, and performance expectations. You will work with stakeholders to connect marketing outcomes to player behaviour and revenue, and follow through to understand whether recommendations improve decisions. Deliver Marketing Measurement: You will design and analyse incrementality tests and contribute to MMM and other causal analyses, selecting appropriate approaches with guidance where needed. You will own defined projects from the initial business question through analysis, interpretation, and stakeholder readout. Explain Business Performance: You will investigate where and why ROI is over- or under-predicted, distinguishing changes in player value, campaign mix, measurement assumptions, and underlying business performance. You will help stakeholders understand whether a gap calls for action, further investigation, or more time to gather evidence. Turn Evidence into Decision Frameworks: You will help translate experiment and model outputs into calibration inputs, performance benchmarks, and repeatable analytical tools. You will bring together evidence from incrementality, attribution, and MMM to support planning and evaluate Performance Marketing within the wider marketing mix. Bridge Business and Technical Questions: You will work with marketing stakeholders to frame actionable questions and with technical partners to define data and analytical requirements. You will help ensure measurement outputs are interpreted correctly and used effectively in day-to-day decisions. Communicate Clearly and Improve Our Approach: You will explain findings, assumptions, and uncertainty to technical and non-technical audiences. You will challenge inconsistencies, identify opportunities to improve existing approaches, and take on broader ownership as your expertise develops. Skills To Create Thrills Education: Degree in Statistics, Economics, Data Science, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience. Experience: Hands-on experience in data science, analytics, experimentation, or marketing measurement, with examples of taking an analytical question through to a useful business recommendation. Statistical Foundations: A solid understanding of statistical modelling, hypothesis testing, experimentation, and the distinction between correlation and causation. Practical experience with at least one relevant measurement approach and an interest in developing broader expertise. Execution: Able to independently deliver well-scoped analytical work, validate results, and manage priorities. Comfortable working through ambiguity while recognising when to seek input or challenge the original question. Commercial Mindset: Curious about what drives business performance and able to connect analytical results to investment choices, expected returns, and practical actions. Technical Skills: Proficiency in Python or R and SQL, with experience working with complex datasets and producing clear, reproducible analyses. Communication: Able to explain complex findings in accessible language, make recommendations supported by evidence, and communicate uncertainty without losing the practical message. Judgement and Growth: Thoughtful about assumptions, data quality, and methodological limitations. Receptive to feedback, quick to learn, and ready to develop towards broader project ownership and greater influence over …

Job Description: 
 Your impact 
 Are you ready to launch your career and make an impact on real-world projects from day one?
 At Leonardo, we’re looking for graduates who want to be part of something extraordinary—shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety.
 We are committed to developing our graduates into leading technical or business professionals, and as such we will also support you through your preferred route for professional development We are looking for Graduate Systems Engineers to join our team in Edinburgh.
 Our 18 Month Graduate Engineering Programme 
 Our Graduate Programmes give you the opportunity to work on exciting and challenging projects alongside subject matter experts.
On joining, you will receive a starting salary of £34,000 per annum , plus a £1,000 welcome bonus. You’ll also be eligible for a £1,000 exit bonus upon successful completion of the programme. In addition, you may be eligible for a Temporary Accommodation Allowance (TAA), subject to specific criteria.
 We encourage you to spend at least three days each week on site to integrate with your team and maximise your learning experience.
 As a Graduate Systems Engineer you will: 
 Systems Engineers are involved in all aspects of design and development, from initial product design through to in-service support.
 They look at the big picture, determine how the system needs to operate and collaborate to produce the required overall operational behaviours. They also dive into the deepest level of detail – taking the system piece-by-piece and defining its design to the finest point. Our Systems Engineers can also actively engage in Research and Development, developing new concepts and conducting fundamental research into our future technologies.
 As a Graduate Systems Engineer, you will work on real engineering problems within either the Radar or the Advanced Targeting business area. You will have the opportunity to be involved in supporting a wide range of tasks across multiple projects/products, such as:
 The radar for the Typhoon fighter jet
 The radar for the SAAB Gripen fighter
 Our family of Surveillance AESA (Active Electronically Scanned Array) radars
 An IRCM (Infra-Red Counter Measures) system
 Our laser target designator or laser ranging systems
 Key Responsibility Areas 
 Requirements capture, design documentation, verification and validation
 Algorithm design and test
 Performance modelling; building physics-based models to test our designs through computer simulation
 Data analysis; end-to-end systems analysis using synthetic and ‘real world’ data
 Applied research; from product improvements to blue-sky thinking
 You will join a dynamic and innovative team who will provide day-to-day guidance and on-the job training, introducing you to systems engineering processes, methods, technology and tools. You will also receive targeted training, developing the engineering skills and necessary domain knowledge required to achieve technical excellence and be a successful Systems Engineer.
 What you’ll bring 
 All of our roles require (a) a minimum of a 2:2 Bachelors/Integrated Master’s degree, or (b) a higher degree, such as a MSc or PhD in a STEM related subject.
 In addition to this, we would be interested in hearing from you if you have experience in:
 Coding/programming.
 Relevant project work and/or placements in industry.
 Solving problems as part of a team
 Applying your science and technology knowledge to solve a real-world problem
 Security Clearance 
 Many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations. As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years. 
 For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV). As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment. 
 To be eligible for National Security Vetting at SC level, applicants will generally be expected to have continuously resided in the UK for the previous five years. For DV clearance, this is typically ten years. In some circumstances, time spent overseas may be accepted, with additional overseas checks. Additional vetting requirements may apply upon appointment.
