PhD fellow in Molecular biology, Biotechnology and Genomics - IT | Lifetech 
 PhD fellow in Molecular biology, Biotechnology and Genomics 
 Italy 
 IIT invites excellent candidates to apply to its PhD program organized in collaboration with the Open University; this international PhD program confers Doctorates in Health, Sustainable and Human Technologies .
 In order to be admitted into the ARC program, the minimum requirements are
 a Masters-level degree, which broadly corresponds to a 4/5-year undergraduate MSc/MChem/Meng-style degree or to a postgraduate Masters in the British system, or to a second level University degree in Italy;
 a grade corresponding to an upper second class (2.1) or a merit in the UK system or 100/110 in the Italian system. Candidates with lower grades but redeeming features (publications, specific expertise) are requested to contact the potential supervisors before applying;
 where English is not the applicant’s first language, a valid IELTS (International English Language Testing System) certificate. The minimum acceptable score is an overall 6.5, with no less than 6.0 in any of the four categories
 One PhD fellow position will be available from 1st of January 2027 in the Non-coding Genomics research Line led by Stefano Gustincich .
 Title of the project : The SINEUPOME . 
 Background : SINEUPs are a class of natural and synthetic antisense long non-coding RNAs that selectively increase the translation of a target mRNA without altering its transcription or stability. They were discovered through the mouse antisense Uchl1 transcript (Carrieri et al., Nature 2012), whose activity depends on an embedded inverted SINEB2 repeat, the origin of the name.
 SINEUPs have a modular architecture. A binding domain, antisense to the 5′ region of the target mRNA (typically overlapping the start codon), confers specificity. An effector domain, containing the inverted SINEB2 element or minimal functional fragments of it, drives translational enhancement. Swapping the binding domain lets SINEUPs be designed against virtually any gene of interest.
 Their effect is moderate (about 1.5- to 3-fold protein increase) and stays within physiological ranges. This makes them attractive for haploinsufficiency disorders and other conditions caused by insufficient protein dosage. They are also useful for biotechnological protein production. They can be delivered as plasmids, viral vectors such as AAV, or synthetic RNA.
 Description: 
 Rationale . Only a handful of natural SINEUPs are known, yet inverted SINE elements are abundant in antisense transcripts across mammals. A systematic analysis would reveal how widespread translational enhancement by antisense lncRNAs really is.
 Aim 1 – Computational catalogue. Mine CAGE (FANTOM5/6), total RNA-seq and nanopore long-read datasets from human, mouse and non-model mammals to annotate lncRNAs with an embedded inverted SINE (SINEB2, MIR, Alu, FLAM).
 Aim 2 – PARIS analysis. Identify lncRNA/mRNA pairs in PARIS data from a diverse array of dataset. List which candidate SINEUPs from Aim 1 are part of the duplex.
 Aim 3 – Functional validation. Test 50–100 top SINEUP candidates in HEK293 and neuronal cells, measuring protein over mRNA ratio of the targets by western blot, qRT-PCR and polysome profiling.
 Impact . A validated atlas of natural SINEUPs and their targets, plus rules linking sequence architecture to activity, would provide both a new layer of post-transcriptional gene regulation and design principles for synthetic SINEUP therapeutics.

This is a specialist Quantitative Developer role. Like all our Quantitative Developers, you will work alongside
items.desc: We tackle the most complex problems in quantitative finance, by bringing scientific clarity to financial complexity. From our London HQ, we unite world-class researchers and engineers in an environment that values deep exploration and methodical execution, because the best ideas take time to evolve. Together we're building a world-class platform to amplify our teams' most powerful ideas. As part of our engineering team, you'll shape the platforms and tools that drive high-impact research, designing systems that scale, accelerate discovery and support innovation across the firm. Take the next step in your career. The role G-Research is investing in how we apply large language models (LLMs) and other Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques across the firm. We are looking for an exceptional NLP Performance Engineer to join our NLP Engineering team and take ownership of large-scale LLM inference performance. This is a specialist Quantitative Developer role. Like all our Quantitative Developers, you will work alongside researchers to bring their ideas to life, with a particular focus on maximising the performance of LLMs. This is a hands-on, high-impact role. You will design and implement techniques that improve the performance, cost-efficiency and capabilities of inference workloads on cutting-edge compute infrastructure, enabling researchers and engineers to make the best use of current and future systems. Working closely with research teams and infrastructure engineers, you will profile and analyse workloads, eliminate bottlenecks and develop reference solutions. Your work will help shape the tooling and infrastructure that underpins our NLP capabilities. Key responsibilities of the role include: Profiling, benchmarking and optimising large-scale LLM inference workloads across our compute infrastructure Ensuring efficient deployment of the latest models across a range of GPU architectures, adapting the inference stack as hardware evolves Designing and implementing inference optimisations while maintaining output quality Developing reference implementations, libraries and tooling to improve the efficiency and reliability of NLP workloads Collaborating with researchers, senior stakeholders and engineers to design optimised solutions Working with systems, architecture and platform teams to evolve the compute stack and influence long-term platform decisions Who are we looking for? We're looking for an engineer who combines deep knowledge of LLM inference with strong software engineering skills and a scientific approach to performance. The ideal candidate will have the following skills and experience: A Bachelor’s, Master’s or PhD in computer science, or equivalent experience Proven experience profiling, benchmarking and optimising large-scale LLM inference workloads A scientific, evidence-led approach to performance optimisation, using rigorous benchmarking and reproducible measurement Deep understanding of transformer inference, including prefill versus decode, KV-cache behaviour, attention variants and performance bottlenecks Hands-on experience with LLM serving frameworks such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM or TGI, and the PyTorch ecosystem Experience with inference optimisation techniques, including quantisation, speculative decoding and model parallelism across modern GPU architectures Strong software engineering skills, including Python, CUDA and building reliable systems for machine learning workloads Strong communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across research, infrastructure and engineering teams Why join us? Highly competitive compensation plus annual discretionary bonus Lunch provided (via Just Eat for Business ) and dedicated barista bar 35 days’ annual leave 9% company pension contributions Informal dress code and excellent work/life balance Comprehensive healthcare and life assurance Cycle-to-work scheme Monthly company events

items.desc: Who are we? Tripledot Studios is one of the largest independent mobile games companies in the world. We are a multi-award-winning organisation, with a global 2,500+ strong team across 12 studios. Our expanded portfolio includes some of the biggest titles in mobile gaming, collectively reaching top chart positions around the world and engaging over 25 million daily active users. Tripledot’s guiding principle is that when people love what they do, what they do will be loved by others. We’re building a company we’re proud of. One filled with driven, incredibly smart and detail-orientated people, who LOVE making games. Our ambition is to be the most successful games company in the world, and we’re just getting started. The role is working within our studio: Tripledot Games About Tripledot Games Tripledot Games is a leading developer and publisher of casual and puzzle games, with a strong presence in London, Warsaw, and Barcelona. The studio is responsible for multiple top 10 titles, including Woodoku, Woodoku Blast, Solitaire, and TripleTile. Our best-in-class data-driven approach spans the entire lifecycle from publishing to machine learning puzzle levels, helping us make fast, smart decisions at every stage of development. We are also one of the largest IAA operators worldwide. Tripledot Games is a diverse and collaborative studio, home to people from over 36 nationalities. We take pride in our craftsmanship, strong focus on outcomes, and continuous improvement, building high-quality, scalable games that players around the world love. Role Overview As a Data Scientist in our Experimentation team, you will help deliver and improve Tripledot’s company-wide experimentation analysis platform. Working closely with Data Engineering, you will define the statistical logic and methodologies behind platform features, build prototypes in Python, and ensure the platform produces accurate, reliable results for product teams across our games portfolio. Your initial focus will include hands-on quality assurance: running independent analyses, comparing results with platform outputs, investigating discrepancies, and validating features and metrics. This offers the opportunity to develop deep expertise in experimentation and A/B testing across a sophisticated internal platform. As the platform evolves, the role will expand into more advanced statistical and machine learning work that delivers value across the business. Key Responsibilities Define statistical logic, calculation methods, and detailed requirements for experimentation platform features. Prototype statistical methodologies and analyses in Python before implementation. Partner closely with Data Engineers as they develop and improve the experimentation platform. Perform thorough data and feature QA by independently calculating results and comparing them with platform outputs. Investigate discrepancies, identify root causes, and help ensure metrics and analyses are accurate and reliable. Explore opportunities to automate QA processes and improve the efficiency and quality of validation. Build a deep understanding of experimentation methodologies, including A/B testing, monitoring, segmentation, and analysis. Collaborate with BI, Machine Learning, product teams, and other stakeholders to understand requests and shape effective solutions. Contribute to future statistical, algorithmic, and machine learning initiatives as the team’s priorities evolve. Skills, Knowledge and Expertise 3-5 years of professional experience as a Data Scientist or in a closely related role Strong Python skills, including the ability to prototype analyses and write clear, reliable scripts. Solid knowledge of statistics and standard statistical methodologies. Practical understanding of experimentation and A/B testing, including how metrics and results should be calculated and validated. Familiarity with machine learning methods and the ability to apply relevant approaches when needed. Excellent attention to detail and a disciplined approach to repetitive or methodical QA work. Strong problem-solving skills, with the initiative to propose creative solutions and process improvements. Clear communication skills and the ability to explain analytical methods, results, and rationale. Experience with experimentation platforms or high-volume digital products, such as gaming, e-commerce, or ride-hailing, would be valuable. Ability to critically evaluate and validate AI-generated code, analyses, or modelling suggestions to ensure correctness and reproducibility. Experience using AI-assisted tools (e.g. code assistants or analytical copilots) to accelerate data exploration, research prototyping, and development workflows while maintaining scientific and statistical rigor. Interest in exploring AI-driven approaches that improve experimentation platforms, developer productivity, or data science research workflows. Working at Tripledot 25 days paid holiday in addition to bank holidays to relax and refresh …

items.title: INGENIEUR INFORMATIQUE en ROBOTIQUE d' EMBALLAGE - TRAITEMENT D'IMAGE - INTELLIGENCE ARTIFICIELLE - AUTOMATISME
items.card: Vos missions principales : Il développe des logiciels : * de pilotage et de contrôle de caméras de vision industrielle, 2D et 3D, interfacées en GigE et USB3 ; * de Traitement de l’Image pour extraire des critères de taille, d’orientation (poire, avocat), de texture et de coloration sur des images de fruits et légumes, avec une librairie telle que OpenCV ; * d’entrainement de modèles/réseaux-de-neurones
items.desc: Vous recherchez un emploi dans une entreprise internationale, dynamique et à la pointe de la technologie ? MAF RODA est un groupe international, spécialisé dans la conception et fabrication de projets clé en main de calibrage et de conditionnement destinés au secteur des fruits et légumes. La capacité de MAF RODA à innover grâce à une politique d’investissement en R&D ambitieuse (robotique d’emballage ; …), un réseau international et un service après–vente de proximité, fait de lui le leader mondial dans son secteur d’activité. Le groupe est actuellement représenté par 1200 salariés et une dizaine de sites de production dans le monde, dont 200 ingénieurs répartis sur 6 bureaux d’études. Dans le cadre d'un renforcement de nos équipes, nous recherchons pour notre siège basé à Montauban (Région Occitanie) un(e) : INGENIEUR INFORMATIQUE en ROBOTIQUE d' EMBALLAGE – TRAITEMENT D’IMAGES – INTELLIGENCE ARTIFICIELLE – AUTOMATISME Au sein de l’équipe informatique, vous développez des applications logicielles appliquées à la robotique industrielle, intégrant du traitement de l'image, de l'intelligence artificielle dans l’OS Windows avec l’IDE Visual Studio et la plateforme .NET (C#), des algorithmes et Interfaces Homme-Machine avancées structurées (WPF : XAML, MVVM), en utilisant GitHub pour le Versioning. Afin de concevoir et de réaliser une machine robotisée, vous collaborez avec différents collègues de divers bureaux d’études de l’entreprise : mécanique, électricité, automatisme, électronique, informatique, vision. Vos missions principales : Il développe des logiciels : * de pilotage et de contrôle de caméras de vision industrielle, 2D et 3D, interfacées en GigE et USB3 ; * de Traitement de l’Image pour extraire des critères de taille, d’orientation (poire, avocat), de texture et de coloration sur des images de fruits et légumes, avec une librairie telle que OpenCV ; * d’entrainement de modèles/réseaux-de-neurones d’Intelligence Artificielle appliqués sur des images de fruits et légumes labélisées pour détecter, segmenter et classifier leurs propriétés naturelles intrinsèques (pomme : pédoncule/calyx ; en fruits à noyaux : pédoncule/mucron/suture ; orange et clémentine : pédoncule, ..) ; * d’intégration de modèles/réseaux-de-neurones entrainés d’Intelligence Artificielle, avec une librairie telle que Pytorch ; * s'exécutant sur CPU et GPU * d’échange de données avec des automates programmables industriels, qui pilotent des robots : Cartésiens, Parallèle/Delta, … * de pilotage de moteurs, tels que des moteurs Pas à Pas ; * en utilisant la gestion de Bases de Données, tel que MongoDB ; Le Développeur Informatique en Robotique d'Emballage est ainsi amené à : * traduire en spécifications informatiques un besoin de robotisation d’un process ; * étudier la faisabilité technique d’une proposition ; * élaborer et mettre à jour la documentation des machines ; * apporter son appui aux équipes de montage en coopérant à la mise au point. A cette occasion, il vérifie les capacités de sa solution en lien avec les process définis. Il peut être amené à intervenir, à distance ou en présentiel, en support à toute filiale du groupe. Votre profil : Vous avez des compétences en Programmation informatique (C# ou Java ou C++, Python), Statistiques, Mathématiques, Algorithmie. Maîtrise de l’Anglais indispensable, Espagnol ou Allemand appréciés. Force de proposition, vous êtes passionné(e) par votre métier et aimez le travail en équipe. Votre esprit critique vous sera également nécessaire pour mener à bien les missions confiées. Vous avez de la curiosité pour les nouvelles technologies en général. Vous êtes également capable de vous engager sur le respect d’un délai à une date souhaitée. Le poste est basé à Montauban (82) et nécessite des déplacements en France et à l’étranger. Débutant accepté, formation assurée au poste et à nos techniques. Rémunération : fixe + intéressement/participation + mutuelle+ avantages CSE. Merci d’adresser LM + CV + prétentions salariales par mail recrutement_ea@maf-france.com

items.desc: About Voodoo Voodoo is a consumer tech company founded in Paris in 2013, with one mission: entertain the world. Today we are 1,000 people, generating $1b+ in annual revenue, profitably. Our games and apps have passed 7 billion downloads and reach 200 million+ active users every month, making Voodoo the #3 mobile publisher worldwide in downloads, after Google and Meta. We were backed by Goldman Sachs, Tencent and GBL along the way. Team Blitz is a gaming platform launched by Voodoo in 2021, allowing players to compete on mobile games for real cash prizes (head-up, tournaments, leagues, etc.). It is leveraging Voodoo's unique game portfolio to engage users in a fun and rewarding way. Role This role sits at the intersection of the Data and Gaming teams. You'll be the analytical partner to game designers and product managers, owning the measurement and tuning of the games themselves — from difficulty and game parameters to matchmaking fairness and the in-game economy. Your work directly shapes what players experience and how the games perform. Missions Own the A/B testing cycle for games and game parameters — designing experiments, validating changes, and reading out results that drive core KPIs (engagement, RTP, rake, fairness, retention). Analyze and calibrate game parameters — difficulty, scoring, completion rates, seed selection, and payout structures — to hit target player experience and economic goals. Translate analyses into clear, actionable recommendations that shape game design and the product roadmap. Build simulations and prototypes to pressure-test parameter and economy changes before rollout, then monitor them live once shipped. Collaborate closely with game designers and engineers to embed data-driven decisions across the full game lifecycle. Build and maintain dashboards and reports that keep the Gaming and Data teams aligned on critical game and economy metrics. Profile 3+ years in analytical roles, ideally within gaming or a data-intensive product environment, comfortable working directly with product and design teams. Skilled in SQL and Python; experience with large, complex datasets. Strong grasp of A/B testing and statistical methods. Comfortable with simulation and modeling to reason about game parameters, difficulty, and game economy outcomes. Thrives in a fast-paced environment with rapid iteration. Player-first mindset with genuine curiosity about games, player behavior, and game balance. Benefits Competitive salary based on experience Swile Lunch voucher Gymlib (100% covered by Voodoo) Premium healthcare coverage with SideCare, 100% covered for you and your family Wellness activities in our Paris office Remote days on Fridays

items.desc: We help the world run better At SAP, we keep it simple: you bring your best to us, and we'll bring out the best in you. We're builders touching over 20 industries and 80% of global commerce, and we need your unique talents to help shape what's next. The work is challenging – but it matters. You'll find a place where you can be yourself, prioritize your wellbeing, and truly belong. What's in it for you? Constant learning, skill growth, great benefits, and a team that wants you to grow and succeed. What you`ll do: At SAP’s Business AI Research, we are exploring the next frontier of AI methods on structured business data – graphs, tables, time series, and more. Foundation Models on Structured Data, like SAP-RPT-1, have ushered in the GenAI era for business relevant scenarios – scenarios that have so far been addressed with classical, often tree-based methods. Now, we are taking the next step. We collaborate with our existing applied research teams in creating novel benchmarks for business problems and the development of novel architectures and models, with the goal to publish benchmarks and models at scientific conferences and in the open-source community. We are working jointly with our academic partners to create ever better means of solving real business problems. The Role Contribute to pioneering technical advances to the field of foundation models on structured data, as well as exploring world models for solving business problems. Execute scientific experiments on internal as well as public data. Enable large scale access to business data and model training in a research driven environment. Develop evaluation frameworks and benchmark suites, driving internal and external exploration of novel tasks Collaborate closely with various domain specialists and data owners to understand how business data can be used for foundation model training. Develop new training and benchmark datasets, bringing together rich semantic context with large scale business data. Make critical design decisions regarding the selection and implementation of underlying technologies. Make models and frameworks available to the open source community. What you bring: PhD or Master’s degree in computer science, artificial intelligence, physics, mathematics or other relevant disciplines. 5+ years of professional experience with Machine Learning on Structured Data, and its application in a business context. Important: Good knowledge of SAP data and SAP applications: Their data models and business objects. Not just the extraction interfaces but down to table level. Some experience in training foundation models at scale is a plus. Experience in Data Engineering with a hands-on approach to solving data challenges. Fluent in Python and the ability to convert your ideas into productive code. Developer experience with any SAP Application and its underlying data models is a plus. Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively in cross-cultural teams. Meet your team: SAP's AI organization is dedicated to seamlessly infusing AI into all enterprise applications, enabling customers, partners, and developers to enhance business processes and generate remarkable business value. Join our international AI team where innovation thrives, opportunities for personal development abound, and exceptional colleagues collaborate globally. #SAPBusinessAICareers Bring out your best SAP innovations help more than four hundred thousand customers worldwide work together more efficiently and use business insight more effectively. Originally known for leadership in enterprise resource planning (ERP) software, SAP has evolved to become a market leader in end-to-end business application software and related services for database, analytics, intelligent technologies, and experience management. As a cloud company with two hundred million users and more than one hundred thousand employees worldwide, we are purpose-driven and future-focused, with a highly collaborative team ethic and commitment to personal development. Whether connecting global industries, people, or platforms, we help ensure every challenge gets the solution it deserves. At SAP, you can bring out your best. We win with inclusion SAP’s culture of inclusion, focus on health and well-being, and flexible working models help ensure that everyone – regardless of background – feels included and can run at their best. At SAP, we believe we are made stronger by the unique capabilities and qualities that each person brings to our company, and we invest in our employees to inspire confidence and help everyone realize their full potential. We ultimately believe in unleashing all talent and creating a better world. SAP is committed to the values of Equal Employment Opportunity and provides accessibility accommodations to applicants with physical and/or mental disabilities. If you are interested in applying for employment with SAP and are in need of accommodation or special assistance …

items.desc: Turn computational work from your own engineering research into paid evaluation tasks for AI models. Open to research-track Bachelor's students, Master's and PhD students, postdocs, and recent graduates. AfterQuery is building a network of researchers to author and validate research-grade scientific-computing tasks for AI models. A strong task is a real piece of computational work from your own research, something you've actually run and debugged: a finite-element or CFD solver, a reaction-engineering model, a physiological model, or a structural or electromagnetic simulation you implemented and validated. Each task has a main problem, a few connected subproblems, a Python reference solution, and tests that check the result. The difficulty should come from the engineering science itself, not from withheld information. We're looking for researchers in: computational mechanics and finite-element methods; computational fluid dynamics; aerospace numerical modeling; chemical and reaction engineering; biomedical and physiological modeling; civil and structural computational mechanics; environmental modeling; and computational electromagnetics. Requirements Education: A Bachelor's student on a research track or with research experience (such as an REU, a thesis, or an RA or lab role), a Master's or PhD student, a postdoc, or a recent graduate in mechanical, aerospace, chemical, biomedical, civil, environmental, or electrical engineering with a computational focus. Technical: Hands-on experience writing your own code, preferably Python, to implement or validate engineering models and solvers. Using commercial software (such as ANSYS, COMSOL, or Abaqus) without your own code isn't enough. Work authorization: Must be able to work as an independent contractor without visa sponsorship. Students on F-1 visas (including OPT/CPT) are not eligible. Contract and pay Flexible, independent-contractor work: $200 per approved task, about 2 hours each, with no cap on how many tasks you take on. Tasks go through review, and you may also review other experts' tasks against a short rubric. All accepted experts undergo standard background and identity verification. This is flexible, task-based work with no fixed weekly schedule Preferred Qualifications Research experience developing finite-element, CFD, or other numerical solvers Public code, a thesis, or papers that show your computational work Prior experience in data annotation, data labeling, or AI/ML evaluation work Why apply Work on your own schedule: task-based, not a fixed hourly commitment Contribute directly to how AI models are evaluated on real, expert-level scientific work Paid, flexible work: $200 per approved task (about 2 hours each), no cap on how many you take on

items.desc: Position description Category Thermohydraulics and fluid mechanics Contract Internship Job title Development of Machine Learning Models for Critical Heat Flux predictions H/F Subject Development of Machine Learning Models for Critical Heat Flux predictions Contract duration (months) 6 Job description The Critical Heat Flux (CHF) is a physical phenomenon that may cause the deterioration of the heat transfer in the core of nuclear reactors, potentially leading to core damage. Its accurate prediction is therefore a crucial issue in nuclear reactor safety. The internship deals with the prediction of the CHF through the development of machine learning techniques and the quantification of the associated uncertainty. It will be realized in the framework of an international OECD/NEA project on the development and application of artificial intelligence methodologies for nuclear engineering. Within this framework, the intern will: Perform a preliminary literature review on the topic and get familiar with the previous works performed at CEA, based on experimental data in tubes with uniform axial heat flux profiles Analyse the new experimental CHF database (e.g., tube with non-uniform heat flux, rod-bundle, rectangular channel, …) to understand the physical phenomenon and to verify the coherence and exploitability of the experimental data. Perform an initial assessment of previously developed machine learning models to the new database. Develop transfer learning to predict as accurately as possible the CHF for the new experiments. If time allows it, investigate the explainability issue and quantify the uncertainty of the models developed during the internship applying different state-of-the-art methodologies such as conformal prediction, hierarchical models and other coverage-driven techniques. Present and discuss the work during technical meetings and write a final report. Applicant Profile The ideal candidate is a MSc. student (in French system: M2 level or Ecole d’ingénieur) who has a good knowledge of artificial intelligence and neural networks with an interest in fluid mechanics. Knowledge of the physics processes underlying the CHF phenomenon will be considered a plus. Good skills in Python coding and code management are required. We welcome previous experience with any major deep learning framework (PyTorch, JAX, Tensorflow) and with uncertainty quantification approaches. Given the international context of the OECD/NEA project, fluency in English is considered necessary (French will be considered a plus). Position location Site Saclay Job location France, Ile-de-France Location Saclay Candidate criteria Prepared diploma Bac+5 - Diplôme École d'ingénieurs PhD opportunity Non Requester Position start date 01/02/2027 General information Organisation The French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission (CEA) is a key player in research, development and innovation in four main areas : defence and security, nuclear energy (fission and fusion), technological research for industry, fundamental research in the physical sciences and life sciences. Drawing on its widely acknowledged expertise, and thanks to its 16000 technicians, engineers, researchers and staff, the CEA actively participates in collaborative projects with a large number of academic and industrial partners. The CEA is established in ten centers spread throughout France Reference 2026-42162 Description de l'unité The internship will be conducted at the Department of Thermal-hydraulics and Fluid dynamics (STMF – Service de Thermohydraulique et de Mécanique de Fluide) within the Energy Division (DES - Direction des Énergies). The department develops and qualifies the simulation tools for the design and the safety analysis of the French nuclear power systems, such as the system thermal-hydraulic code CATHARE. These studies are performed within the framework of internal CEA projects or in collaboration with several industrial partners (e.g., EDF, Framatome and TechnicAtome) and international partners. The internship is in collaboration with the Department of Software Engineering and for Simulation (SGLS - Service de Génie Logiciel pour la Simulation).

items.desc: Summary You will become part of the newly established AI Threat Research and AI Conversation Security team within the Technology Division in Bratislava. As a founding member, you have a unique opportunity to shape the team's direction and methodology from the ground up. The team researches attacks against conversational AI systems — probing and breaking them to understand how adversaries exploit large language models. Job Description Beyond research, the team designs and implements detection mechanisms and translates these defenses into shipping products across endpoint, cloud, and standalone form factors. As a Conversational AI Security Engineer, you bridge adversarial research and production engineering — building detection mechanisms to defend conversational AI systems and shipping those defenses as products. Your work spans the full lifecycle, from breaking models to running detection in production. About The Role Research attacks against conversational AI systems — exploring, probing, and breaking them to discover vulnerabilities before adversaries do. Design and propose mitigations, protections, and detection strategies based on findings from adversarial research. Build a multilayered detection core, combining different approaches to identify malicious prompts and attempts to manipulate AI systems. Productize detection capabilities — packaging and deploying them across endpoint, cloud, and standalone environments. Collaborate with the broader threat detection department, product teams, and endpoint teams to integrate defenses into shipping security solutions. Evaluate and experiment with open-source and proprietary AI tooling to stay current with the rapidly evolving attack surface. Shape the team's technical direction and methodology as a founding member, with the opportunity to grow into a Team Lead role over time. Essential Requirements Strong software engineering background — ability to build production systems, not just prototypes. Proficiency in Python for building detection and security tooling. Understanding of how large language models work and how they can be manipulated or attacked, including prompt injection, jailbreaking, and adversarial inputs. Ability to work independently in a newly forming team with minimal defined processes. Desirable Requirements Experience with machine learning and AI, including fine-tuning and deploying language models. C++ for performance-critical detection components. Background in cybersecurity or threat research. Technologies Python, C++, PyTorch, TensorFlow, Hugging Face, scikit-learn, vLLM, Ollama, ONNX, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, Hadoop, Spark, Kafka, OpenClaw, OpenCode, Git, JIRA, Confluence Compensation Basic wage component (brutto): from 2800 EUR/m. (brutto) * The final basic wage component can be increased accordingly to individual skills and experience of the selected candidate. * Performance bonus 2 times per year up to 10% of the basic salary paid for the evaluation period(usually 6 months). #medior At ESET, diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) are integral to our corporate culture. items.desc: Starting date: 16/10/2026Job Reference 446_26_ES_AC_RE2Position Research Engineer on atmospheric composition forecasts and reanalyses (RE2)Closing Date Monday, 19 October, ****Reference: 446_26_ES_AC_RE2Job title: Research Engineer on atmospheric composition forecasts and reanalyses (RE2)About BSCThe Barcelona Supercomputing Center - Centro Nacional de Supercomputación (BSC-CNS) is the leading supercomputing center in Spain. It houses MareNostrum, one of the most powerful supercomputers in Europe, was a founding and hosting member of the former European HPC infrastructure PRACE (Partnership for Advanced Computing in Europe), and is now hosting entity for EuroHPC JU, the Joint Undertaking that leads large-scale investments and HPC provision in Europe. The mission of BSC is to research, develop and manage information technologies in order to facilitate scientific progress. BSC combines HPC service provision and R&D into both computer and computational science (life, earth and engineering sciences) under one roof, and currently has over **** staff from 60 countries.Look At The BSC ExperienceBSC-CNS YouTube ChannelLet's stay connected with BSC Folks! We are particularly interested for this role in the strengths and lived experiences of women and underrepresented groups to help us avoid perpetuating biases and oversights in science and IT research. In instances of equal merit, the incorporation of the under-represented sex will be favoured.We promote Equity, Diversity and Inclusion, fostering an environment where each and every one of us is appreciated for who we are, regardless of our differences.If you consider that you do not meet all the requirements, we encourage you to continue applying for the job offer. We value diversity of experiences and skills, and you could bring unique perspectives to our team.Context And MissionWe are looking for an experienced and enthusiastic research engineer to join the Atmospheric Composition (AC) group within the Earth Sciences department at the BSC-CNS. The AC group is currently composed of about 50 people among researchers, engineers and students of different nationalities. It aims at better understanding and predicting the spatio-temporal variations of atmospheric pollutants along with their effects upon air quality, weather and climate. This is addressed through the continuous development and application of numerical models over multiple scales, from weather to climate and from global to urban scales.The AC group develops and maintains its own forecast model MONARCH, which is a coupled meteorological-chemistry model that can be run at global and regional scales to simulate gaseous chemistry and aerosols plus their feedbacks on radiation. MONARCH is also coupled to a data assimilation scheme for gases and aerosols that is used to initialize forecasts or produce reanalyses of the atmospheric composition. The AC group operates several operational forecasting systems in the framework of the World Meteorological Organization Sand and Dust Storm Advisory System (SDS-WAS, ), the Copernicus atmospheric monitoring services (CAMS, ), the Spanish air quality forecasting system CALIOPE (), and the International Cooperative for Aerosols Predictions (ICAP). The successful candidate will join the Data Assimilation Forecasting and Application team of the AC group and will play a key coordinating role in the production and continuous improvement of the team's operational forecasting and reanalysis systems. The activities will be carried out mainly in the framework of the Copernicus CAMS2_40bis international project, with contributions to the CAMS2_82bis project and to the activities of the Barcelona Dust Regional Center (BDRC). The candidate will work in a highly collaborative environment, with tight links with researchers and engineers in the AC group. The candidate will have the opportunity to follow multiple training activities, including those aimed at improving coding and data analysis, project writing abilities, or project management. All this will be implemented via the formal courses organized by the Education and Training team and Human Resources, and the participation in the regular seminars organized by the department.Key DutiesManage the team's technical activities within CAMS2_40bis and its contributions to CAMS2_82bis and the BDRC, including planning, follow-up of tasks and milestones, and reporting.Coordinate the preparation and timely delivery of project deliverables, and represent the team in international project meetings.Coordinate the upgrades of the production systems: define and evaluate target model configurations, organize the e-suite experiments, and ensure successful operational deployments.Coordinate the production of atmospheric composition reanalyses, from planning and set-up to monitoring, validation and dissemination.Oversee the overall quality assurance of the forecast and reanalysis products, including routine evaluation against in-situ and satellite …

items.desc: About Mistral Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. The Role As a Research Software Engineer on the Sandboxes team, you will design, build, and operate the platform that runs isolated environments for untrusted code at massive scale. Our work spans distributed systems, low-level virtualization, and product-minded platform design. Engineers on this team move between deep infrastructure work and understanding how researchers actually use the platform. This is a software engineering role, not an ML research role. You do not need prior ML experience; what matters is writing clean, reliable systems code that scales. You will join a small, senior team where the wrong hire is worse than no hire. What You Will Do Design, build, and operate the sandboxing platform that runs untrusted code at scale across multiple Kubernetes clusters, from our own bare metal data centers to hyperscalers. Develop the sandbox runtime leveraging Firecracker, enabling fast startup, snapshotting, and efficient scheduling without blocking expensive hardware. Obsess over performance and latency optimisation allowing us to reach millions of concurrent sandboxes. Write robust, well-tested systems code in Rust and Python; review code, CI/CD, and observability across the platform. Own cross-cluster networking, security boundaries, isolation guarantees and monitoring for suspicious activity. Collaborate with researchers and ML engineers who use sandboxes for synthetic data generation and RL training, turning their needs into platform features. What We're Looking For A strong background in software engineering and distributed systems, with experience building and operating large-scale infrastructure. Deep expertise in at least one of: Kubernetes and cluster operations, cross-cluster networking, observability, or low-level virtualization. Fluency in Python or Rust; comfortable writing systems code where performance and security matter. Strong software-design instincts: modular code, testing, CI/CD, observability, and a bias for reliability. A self-starter who learns fast. Core skills matter more than specific tools — we value meta-learning ability and motivation highly. Low-ego, collaborative, and comfortable with ambiguity in a small, high-ownership team. Nice-to-haves Experience with Firecracker, microVMs, or similar virtualization technologies. Product-mindedness: understanding of how sandboxes are used for synthetic data generation or RL training. Experience with GPU clusters, CUDA, or ML workloads. Prior SRE or platform engineering experience at scale. Open-source contributions or widely used internal tools. What we offer We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks. For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page. Privacy Policy Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy.

Backed by global expertise and a commitment to service that feels different, we’re focused on making insurance simpler, faster, and more responsive. Shape The Future We’re leading a transformation in insurance helping people, businesses and society prosper in good times and be resilient in bad times. When you join us, you’re not just taking a job, you’re stepping into a career where you can make a real difference. Grow With Us We’re customer-driven, community-focused, and committed to helping our people grow. Whether you’re early in your journey or bringing years of experience, we’ll support you with the tools, flexibility, and opportunities to thrive. Win As a Team We’re looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to help build and run production-ready ML systems that make a real impact across the business. You’ll work closely with Data Scientists and engineering teams, shaping the ML roadmap, developing scalable solutions, and driving innovation while growing your career. You’ll Make An Impact By Office location – London or Horsham, 3 days a week. Build and automate ML pipelines for feature engineering, model training, and model scoring using Python, PySpark, Databricks, and MLflow. Productionise Data Science models, converting notebooks into modular, tested, production-ready code. Deploy models into batch and real-time environments, managing versioning, promotion, rollback, and scheduled workflows via MLflow and APIs. Implement monitoring and observability, including data and model drift detection, performance alerts, logging, and automated retraining. Collaborate with Data Engineering and Platform teams on CI/CD integration, pipeline performance, compute optimisation, and secure deployment patterns. Maintain engineering standards, ensuring high-quality testing, documentation, code quality, reproducibility, and operational reliability. Your Skills And Experience Experience with ML platforms including Databricks, MLflow, Delta Lake, and cloud environments. Proficient in Python, PySpark, and SQL, following production coding best practices. Understanding of data, distributed ML pipelines, and model deployment patterns, including monitoring, drift detection, and lifecycle operations. Exposure to CI/CD, containerisation, and API integration, with the ability to build scalable, production-ready ML systems. Comfortable working technically while communicating effectively with Data Scientists, stakeholders, and cross-functional teams. Why You’ll Love It Here Being part of our team means you’ll have the support and freedom to bring your best self to work each day. As a permanent member, here’s what you can look forward to Annual discretionary bonus Up to 11% pension contributions Hybrid working + flexible hours 25 days annual leave + bank holidays + buy/sell options Health & wellbeing + virtual GP Career development and mentoring Inclusive culture + employee networks Share investment options Our DEI Commitment We celebrate individuality and believe our differences make us stronger. items.desc: Description Role Title: Research Associate in Sensor Development & Electronic Device Characterisation Grade and Salary: Grade 7, £38,448 - £48,337 per annum FTE and working pattern: Full-time (35hrs per week) Fixed Term until 31st March 2027. Purpose of Role Applications are invited for a five-month Research Associate position at Heriot-Watt University to support an interdisciplinary ARIA-funded research programme developing highly miniaturised sensing and wireless technologies for bio-inspired aerial platforms. The project is a collaboration between Heriot-Watt University and the University of Edinburgh and brings together expertise in sensing, functional materials, electronic systems, microdevices, wireless technologies and bio-inspired engineering. The successful applicant will contribute to two equally important experimental activities within the project: Chemiluminescent sensor development and characterisation - This will include preparation and evaluation of candidate sensing materials, development of optical measurement methods, and assessment of temperature and relative-humidity response, repeatability and stability. Electronic device and high-frequency/RF characterisation - This will include development of suitable measurement arrangements for externally fabricated micro- and nanoscale devices, acquisition and analysis of electrical signals, and evaluation of device performance within the wider electronic and wireless system. The position therefore requires an interdisciplinary experimental researcher with practical experience spanning both sensor/materials development and electronic or high-frequency characterisation. The successful candidate will develop experimental methods, establish and troubleshoot measurement systems, analyse results and contribute to technical decisions across both workstreams. Fabrication of the micro- and nanoscale electronic devices will be undertaken by specialist external facilities. The focus of this appointment is experimental development, characterisation and validation rather than cleanroom fabrication. Given the short duration of the appointment, we are particularly interested in candidates with strong practical laboratory skills who can work independently, adapt quickly to new techniques and deliver experimental results within a defined project timescale. Key Duties And Responsibilities Chemiluminescent Sensor Development and Characterisation Prepare, refine and evaluate candidate chemiluminescent sensing materials and formulations in collaboration with the project team. Develop experimental methods to quantify sensor response under controlled temperature and relative-humidity conditions. Characterise sensor sensitivity, repeatability, variability, response behaviour and stability using appropriate reference measurements. Compare candidate formulations and sensor configurations and identify promising approaches for further development. Establish and use suitable optical measurement methods for quantitative sensor evaluation. Analyse results, identify experimental limitations and provide recommendations for subsequent sensor development. Electronic Device and High-Frequency/RF Characterisation Develop and implement experimental procedures for the electrical and high-frequency/RF characterisation of externally fabricated micro- and nanoscale electronic devices. Establish suitable test arrangements and interfaces between devices and electronic measurement equipment. Acquire and analyse transient and high-frequency electrical signals using appropriate laboratory instrumentation. Characterise device performance, repeatability and device-to-device variability, and compare different device designs or fabrication variants. Identify and minimise measurement artefacts associated with noise, grounding, shielding, bandwidth and parasitic effects. Support evaluation of signal detectability and device performance within the wider electronic and wireless system. Activities Across Both Research Strands Analyse experimental data using MATLAB, Python or equivalent computational tools. Develop appropriate quantitative methods for comparing experimental results. Maintain clear and accurate laboratory records and prepare concise technical reports. Provide technical feedback to project collaborators and external partners and contribute to decisions on subsequent experimental iterations. Develop appropriate risk assessments and COSHH documentation and work within established laboratory health and safety procedures. Present research findings and experimental plans at project meetings and contribute to reports, publications and presentations. Work effectively with researchers at Heriot-Watt University, the University of Edinburgh and …

Job Description: 
 An opportunity for a Manufacturing Engineering Business Methods Engineer - Data Analytics & Foundations has arisen within Airbus Operations, Getafe (Madrid).
 The selected candidate will join the Central Manufacturing Engineering Work Preparation (OMMD) team within the Airbus Production System Efficiency organization. Responsible for Work Preparation processes, methods, tools, and competencies across all Airbus plants, Final Assembly Lines (FALs), and aircraft programs, our department focuses on deploying efficient production solutions to enable industrial excellence and support company profitability.
 The jobholder will reinforce our team by leading transformational digital projects targeting the Manufacturing Engineering Work Preparation community, leveraging Data Analytics, Automation, and Artificial Intelligence to improve decision-making and operational efficiency.
 RESPONSIBILITIES 
 The main tasks of the jobholder will be:
 Lead digital transformation projects by deploying unified platforms (e.g., MEGA) to streamline end-to-end Preparation Dossier creation (PFMEA, Routing, SOI, Work Order Release) across plants and FALs.
 Define and set the ME Data Analytics Strategy for the department while acting as the Data Custodian and main link to Data Governance teams.
 Drive process automation initiatives through the deployment of RPA, Machine Learning, and Artificial Intelligence solutions within the Work Preparation perimeter.
 Ensure compliance and governance by enforcing Airbus Export Control Regulations through specialized digital tools (e.g., tagging tools) and maintaining data consistency.
 Provide technical expertise and change management to local/transnational teams through digital coaching, communication, and facilitation.
 Support end-to-end data integration across business objects (SOI, BoM, Routing, Drawing) across all aircraft programs and shop floor guidance functions.
 SKILLS 
 Is your profile aligned to the following list of skills? Apply! We are looking forward to knowing you:
 Education: 5-year degree (Master's or equivalent) in Mechanical Engineering, IT, or a related engineering field.
 Experience: Hands-on experience in Manufacturing Engineering Work Preparation activities, along with proven project leadership and change management experience.
 Technical knowledge: Expertise in Palantir Foundry (Skywise) or programming, strong knowledge of Artificial Intelligence foundations, and deep understanding of ME Work Preparation end-to-end data flows.
 Languages: English at a negotiation level.
 Soft skills: Excellent stakeholder management, strong negotiation and communication skills, ability to work in a transnational environment, and availability to travel.
 Valuable / Nice to have: Master’s degree in Data Analytics, Digital Transformation, or AI; knowledge of AWS, GCP, RPA, Machine Learning, Airbus Export Control Regulations; and proficiency in French, German, or Spanish.

 At Airbus we are focused on our employees and their welfare. Take a look at some of our social benefits:
 Vacation days plus additional days-off along the year.

 Benefits such as life insurance, health insurance, employee stock options, retirement plan, or study grants.

Location: Bristol, UK 
 Start date: September 2027
 Application deadline : Midnight, 29th November 2026 
 We encourage you to apply early, as we may close applications before the advertised deadline. 
 The Graduate Programme at Graphcore
 Join Graphcore in a permanent role and start your career with two years of hands-on learning. From day one, you’ll be trusted to take ownership, share your ideas and help shape what we’re creating. You’ll tackle challenging problems alongside a team who support your development and are as excited about your success as you are.
 What you’ll work on
 Put your design skills to work on clearer ways for people to understand complex AI workloads. 
 In Graphcore’s UX team, you’ll help shape software used to understand and optimise workloads running on our hardware. Your work will make technical workflows easier to navigate and turn complex system behaviour into clear user experiences. 
 With support from senior designers, you’ll create wireframes, high-fidelity designs and research materials. You’ll also help run usability studies, analyse findings and maintain our research repository, using what you learn to improve designs. 
 Your team and support 
 The UX team works closely with engineers and product managers throughout the development lifecycle. Design decisions are shaped by user insight, technical constraints and clear evidence. 
 Your manager, Lucy, will work with you to build your skills, make time for learning and shape your career. Her favourite part of leadership is helping talented, driven people turn ideas into action, with the support and space to do their best work. You’ll also have a buddy to help you settle in, alongside a team of experienced designers keen to share what they know and help you develop. 
 Josh recently joined us as a graduate and is confident, he’ll have discovered all the best lunch spots near the office by the time you arrive. He’s looking forward to sharing his favourites with you! 
 You’ll contribute to Decagon, our design library, and help keep research insights useful and easy to find. The work moves from discovery to design, testing and iteration, and you will build confidence and take ownership of defined tasks. 
 You’ll be encouraged to ask questions, challenge existing approaches and share ideas for making things better. We’ll support you to take responsibility for your work and speak up when you spot a problem or need help. Thoughtful discussion and clear communication help us learn from each other and improve our designs. 
 How you’ll learn and grow 
 During the two-year programme, you’ll build skills across user experience (UX), user interface (UI) design, research and design systems through real product work. 
 Creating designs and helping run usability studies will give you practical experience of exploring user needs, testing ideas and turning findings into improvements. Contributing to Decagon will help you understand how a shared design library supports consistent interfaces. 
 Working with senior designers, engineers and product managers will help you explain your design decisions, respond to feedback and understand how user needs and technical constraints shape a product. 
 What we’re looking for 
 A degree in UX, Interaction Design, Human–Computer Interaction (HCI), Graphic Design or a related discipline 
 UX/UI design experience and a portfolio demonstrating your UX thinking, design process and visual skills 
 Proficiency in design tools such as Figma or Adobe XD 
 Strong communication and collaboration skills, with an interest in designing for complex, technical or business-to-business (B2B) software products 
 Your experience can come from academic or personal projects, internships or placements. In your portfolio, show the problem you explored, how you approached it, the design decisions you made and what you learned.

 Flexible working: Balance your work and personal life with greater flexibility
 Retirement planning support: Up to 5% matched pension
 Phantom equity: Share in Graphcore’s success
 Workplace experience: Enjoy thoughtfully designed office spaces for collaboration, with free food and an on-site barista to support your day
 Peace of mind protection: Income protection and life assurance to provide financial security for you and your loved ones
 Electric Vehicle Scheme: Choose an electric vehicle and lease it through salary sacrifice
 Flexible benefits: Tailor your benefits package with a choice of additional options, including private medical insurance and dental cover
 Optional benefits: Dental cover, health cash plan, private medical insurance, cycle to work scheme, give as you earn

items.desc:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. We work with customer executives, product and engineering teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works.

Production-ready deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere.

About the Role

As an Applied AI Engineer you will partner directly with leading organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that deliver measurable business outcomes. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from use-case selection and architecture through prototyping, evaluation, production launch, and scale.

You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact—not simply activity or successful demonstrations.

This is a rare opportunity to work on consequential real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI’s products evolve.

This role is based in Paris. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees

In this role, you will:

 - Partner directly with enterprise and digital native customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria.

 - Design, build, and deploy AI systems that solve important customer problems and produce measurable business outcomes.

 - Work hands-on in code to build prototypes, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, integrations, and production accelerators.

 - Make sound technical decisions across models, agents, retrieval, tools, data, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance.

 - Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers toward resolution.

 - Help customers progress from promising prototypes to reliable production systems, sustained adoption, and scaled impact.

 - Partner closely with customer engineering teams and OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and go-to-market teams, translating deployment experience into high-signal product feedback.

 - Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have a demonstrated track record of designing, building, and delivering AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, product engineering or technical consulting.

 - Are fluent in both French and English

 - Can point to substantial personal contributions in code, architecture, evaluation, debugging, or engineering of production systems—not only program or stakeholder management.

 - Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working across an AI application stack; experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable.

 - Understand how to evaluate AI systems systematically using representative data, graders, production signals, and human judgment.

 - Have navigated enterprise production requirements such as integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost.

 - Can connect technical decisions to customer workflows, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.

 - Communicate with clarity and credibility across hands-on engineers, technical leaders, security teams, product leaders, and executives.

 - Bring high agency, strong technical judgment, and end-to-end ownership in ambiguous environments.

 - Learn quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and collaborate with humility; experience in a particular industry or with OpenAI products is not required.



About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. items.desc:
ABOUT ELEVENLABS

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

 - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

 - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

 - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.




HOW WE WORK

 - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

 - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

 - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

 - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

 - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

 - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

 - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

 - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

 - Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

 - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Every model we train runs on infrastructure this role owns. We operate NVIDIA GPU clusters across bare metal and rented capacity, and we're looking for an engineer to join our small research infrastructure team and make that compute fast, reliable, and boring - in the best sense. When the clusters just work, research moves faster. Your impact is measured directly in training throughput and researcher velocity.



This is a builder-operator role with real breadth: one week you're writing automation that eliminates a whole class of manual work, the next you're benchmarking a new provider's InfiniBand fabric or on-site bringing new hardware online. You'll have unusual scope and autonomy - we're a lean team where decisions are made by the people closest to the problem.




WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

 - Operate and improve our GPU fleet end to end: provisioning, scheduling, monitoring, upgrades, capacity planning

 - Build automation that keeps the fleet healthy without human intervention — node health checks, automated draining and remediation, burn-in pipelines for new capacity

 - Own the stack beneath the training code: OS images, NVIDIA drivers, CUDA, container runtimes, NCCL, high-speed networking (InfiniBand/RoCE)

 - Run and tune job scheduling (Slurm or similar) so researchers get compute fairly and fast

 - Build and maintain high-performance storage for datasets and checkpoints

 - Hunt down performance problems: stragglers, degraded links, thermal issues, flaky GPUs — and fix the class of problem, not just the instance

 - Evaluate rented GPU capacity: benchmark it, validate it, hold providers to their SLAs

 - Hands-on hardware work when it's needed: racking, cabling, diagnostics, coordinating with datacenter staff and vendors

 - Keep clusters secure by default: access control, network isolation, secrets




REQUIREMENTS

 - Have run large-scale Linux server or GPU environments in production and enjoy both building and operating

 - Know the NVIDIA stack well — drivers, CUDA, NCCL, DCGM — or have deep systems experience and learn hardware stacks fast

 - Are comfortable with bare-metal environments, server hardware, and high-speed networking

 - Write solid automation in Python and/or Bash, with IaC tools like Ansible or Terraform

 - Are happy digging into noisy data (metrics, …

items.desc: Job Specs Job Name Experienced - Digital Regulation & AI Governance Location Roma Business Area RISK, REGULATORY & FORENSIC Seniority Experienced Business Function STRATEGY, RISK & TRANSACTIONS ADVISORY What impact will you make? Experienced Digital Regulation & AI Governance Siamo alla ricerca di un/una Senior Consultant – Digital Regulation & AI Governance da inserire nella divisione Strategy, Risk & Transactions Advisory di Deloitte, con sede a Roma e modalità di lavoro ibrida (hybrid working). Il nostro team affianca organizzazioni pubbliche e private, in Italia e a livello internazionale, nell’interpretazione e nell’applicazione delle normative europee e nazionali in ambito digitale, degli standard internazionali ISO e dei principi di etica e responsabilità tecnologica. Trasformiamo i requisiti normativi in soluzioni concrete di governance, compliance e gestione dei rischi, supportando i clienti nell’adozione responsabile dell’intelligenza artificiale e delle tecnologie digitali. In particolare, accompagniamo le organizzazioni nella definizione e nell’attuazione di modelli di governance. Le nostre attività contribuiscono inoltre alla trasformazione digitale in ambiti quali la sicurezza delle informazioni, i servizi cloud, la gestione dell’intelligenza artificiale e la continuità operativa. Your Role La risorsa Experienced verrà inserita in un team di lavoro e si occuperà di: Valutare l’impatto delle normative digitali europee e nazionali, tra cui l’EU AI Act, la Legge 132/2025, le Linee Guida AgID per l’IA nella PA, il GDPR, il Data Act, la direttiva NIS2 etc., traducendo i requisiti di conformità in priorità operative e piani d’azione concreti. Progettare modelli di governance dell’intelligenza artificiale e valutare i casi d’uso dell’IA, i rischi e le misure di protezione, anche nell’ambito delle Pubbliche Amministrazioni e dei servizi pubblici digitali. Supportare i clienti nell’implementazione e nel miglioramento dei sistemi di gestione basati sugli standard ISO (es. ISO 27001, ISO 27017, ISO 27018, ISO 27701, ISO 31000, ISO 20000-1, ISO 42001), attraverso gap analysis, definizione dei controlli, attuazione dei sistemi, preparazione agli audit di terza parteetc. Integrare i requisiti normativi e di governance nei progetti di trasformazione digitale, cybersicurezza, servizi cloud, protezione dei dati e resilienza operativa. Collaborare con team legali, compliance, risk management, IT e business per sviluppare policy, modelli di governance e procedure operative. Gestire specifiche linee di attività progettuali e le relazioni con i clienti, realizzando valutazioni, workshop, raccomandazioni e presentazioni rivolte al management. Contribuire alla preparazione di proposte progettuali e allo sviluppo di metodologie e strumenti, affiancando e supportando la crescita dei colleghi più junior. What We Offer La retribuzione prevista per questa posizione è compresa tra EUR 37.500 e EUR 41.000 lordi annui per il grade Senior Consultant in applicazione del CCNL Terziario Distribuzione e Servizi. La definizione del compenso specifico, inclusi eventuali elementi variabili (come MBO) o benefit accessori, dipenderà dalla valutazione del profilo rispetto ai requisiti della posizione Winning Requirements Formazione: laurea magistrale in Giurisprudenza, Economia, Scienze Politiche, Politiche Pubbliche, Ingegneria, Informatica, Sicurezza delle Informazioni o discipline affini. Esperienza professionale: almeno 3 anni di esperienza nella consulenza direzionale, nella regolamentazione digitale, nella governance tecnologica o dell’IA, nella cybersicurezza, nella gestione dei rischi o nella compliance. Conoscenza normativa e competenze di governance: solida conoscenza della regolamentazione digitale europea e della governance dell’intelligenza artificiale, preferibilmente anche in relazione ai casi d’uso dell’IA nella Pubblica Amministrazione. items.desc: About Mercor Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents. Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices. Mercor AI Research Fund Grants: Economics of AI One of the biggest challenges facing the industry today is determining whether frontier AI is capable enough to deliver value in real-world settings. A model can perform well on benchmarks and still struggle in production. That’s why investing in research, realistic evaluations, and robust verification is critical. Mercor is seeking to fund AI research on the economic impacts of AI. This is separate from the Mercor Research Fellowship, which funds individual experts (apply HERE), our $5m of safety funding awards (apply HERE), and our funding of benchmarking research. The grant supports: The time of experts from Mercor's platform Researcher hours API costs Stipends for event and conference attendance Budget Categories Applications are grouped into three budget tiers. Please state your tier clearly in your application and ensure your overall budget ask falls within it: Tier 1: under $50,000 : Suited to focused, well-scoped projects such as pilot studies, evaluations, replications, or extensions of existing work. These applications undergo a streamlined review. Tier 2: under $200,000 : Suited to substantial projects requiring dedicated personnel time, meaningful compute, or data collection. Reviewed with proportionally greater attention to the budget breakdown and implementation plan. Tier 3: under $500,000 : Reserved for ambitious, multi-component research programs. These applications receive the highest level of scrutiny: reviewers will expect a detailed justification of each spend category, a clear account of team capacity to execute at this scale, and milestones against which progress can be assessed. The level of review scrutiny scales with the size of the ask, so applicants should request the smallest budget that credibly supports the proposed work. Research Agenda We are interested in submissions in the following area: 1. Measuring AI’s impact on labor How should we measure AI’s effect on real economic and labor outcomes — and what methodologies are up to the task? To what extent do benchmark scores map onto real economic outcomes? What is the right methodology for measuring AI’s impact on labor outcomes (employment, wages, task composition)? How does occupational exposure to AI evolve over time, and how can novel datasets improve its measurement? 2. Human–AI collaboration and productivity How do humans actually work with AI systems, and when does that collaboration make them more productive? What is the efficiency gain of human experts when paired with AI models, and under what conditions? How can we measure the “review cost” that model outputs impose on humans — the time and effort spent checking, correcting, and verifying AI work? Which collaboration patterns improve output quality rather than merely output volume? 3. Enterprise adoption and returns What does AI adoption look like inside organizations, and what returns does it generate? How are organizations actually using AI, and how is that usage changing? How can the effect of AI and agent deployments be measured causally, rather than through self-report or correlation? What are the right enterprise-level variables for quantifying AI-driven productivity gains? Eligibility Researchers at universities and non-profit research organizations, as well as public benefit corporations and small startups (<20 people) that do not sell AI training data. Awards are made to the researcher’s institution. Applicants must be based in the United States or the United Kingdom We expect grantees to publish a paper, an open dataset, a public methodology, or a tool the field can use, released under an open license that permits commercial use. Timeline Application deadline: November 27, 2026, 11:59 PM PT (UTC 8) Notification to applicants: by December 18, 2026 Late or incomplete applications will not be reviewed. All applicants will be notified of the outcome whether or not they are shortlisted. How to apply We invite interested researchers …
