items.desc: Are you an experienced Data Engineer with deep expertise in enterprise data warehouse design and data modelling, preferably with experience in Data Vault 2.0? Join us in transforming our existing GCP data platform into an advanced enterprise data warehouse that reliably integrates diverse data sources and helps shape the future of finance. SEB is more than a bank. We are a technology-driven financial institution where everything starts from our customer needs and business outcomes. Cloud, AI, automation and modern engineering are natural parts of how we build, operate and continuously improve our technology platforms. From core banking platforms to hybrid and multi-cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, platform engineering, AI-enabled operations and automation, we offer a broad tech landscape and many paths to grow. Together, we are shaping secure, responsible and future-proof solutions for our customers and society. Are you ready to take on a new challenge? About the role You will play a key role in transforming SEB’s Finance & Risk Data Platform into a modern, scalable, and audit-ready enterprise data warehouse. This is a hands-on data engineering role with a particular focus on enterprise data modelling. As part of the FR360 Data Platform team, you will help establish a data architecture that enables reliable integration at enterprise scale while meeting the high standards of a regulated banking environment. Your primary focus will be designing and implementing robust data models that support business reporting, regulatory requirements, historical data management, and data governance. You will work closely with data engineers, architects, business stakeholders, and Finance & Risk specialists to ensure that data is accurate, traceable, and fit for purposes. Key responsibilities include: Take end-to-end responsibility for data modelling, from source analysis to the design and implementation of target data models. Use SQL and other analytical techniques to understand source data structures, content, relationships, keys, grain, and data quality. Design target data models using scalable and maintainable patterns based on Data Vault 2.0 principles and methodologies. Define and promote standards for historical data management, auditability, lineage, metadata management, and data quality. Build and optimise ELT processes using Google Cloud Platform technologies, including BigQuery, Cloud Composer, dbt, and Dataform. Drive best practices in data modelling, warehouse design, and engineering excellence across the team. You will share responsibility for the team’s day-to-day data engineering work while taking a leading role in data modelling, data governance, and data engineering standards. To thrive in this role, we believe you have: Deep expertise in data modelling and enterprise data warehouse design. Proven hands-on experience delivering data models end to end, from requirements gathering and source analysis through conceptual and logical modelling to physical design and production implementation. A track record of building scalable data platforms that integrate large numbers of heterogeneous source systems. Hands-on experience building and maintaining ELT pipelines and data integration solutions. A strong ability to balance business requirements, regulatory expectations, and long-term maintainability. Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to translate complex requirements into practical data solutions covering data structures, semantics, keys, and data quality. Strong SQL and Python skills. Experience using AI-powered tools to improve engineering, operations or automation workflows, either professionally or through personal projects. It is beneficial if you also have: Experience in banking, finance, or another regulated industry. Hands-on experience with Data Vault 2.0 modelling principles and implementation. Familiarity with GCP services and tools such as BigQuery, Cloud Composer, Apache Airflow, Dataform, and dbt, or with comparable cloud data platforms. Knowledge of data governance, regulatory reporting, or frameworks such as BCBS 239. What we offer Agile and modern ways of working. A flat hierarchy and an open environment where ideas, opinions, and different points of view are welcomed. Extensive training and learning opportunities. The opportunity to work for an innovative company at the forefront of technology. A hybrid working model, with the possibility of working remotely up to two days per week. Do you want to be part of SEB? We believe that inclusion and diversity are crucial to our future success. We strive to foster an inclusive, value-driven culture in which employees feel valued, respected, and involved, regardless of who they are, what they believe, or where they come from. We review applications continuously, so please submit your application through the link in this advertisement as soon as possible, and no later than 15 November 2026 . Vi välkomnar en mångfald av sökande med olika bakgrund och vi ser fram emot din ansökan. Om oss Vi på Plikt- och prövningsverket arbetar för att göra Sveriges säkrare. Vår huvuduppgift är att mönstra, skriva in till grundutbildningen och registerföra personal i krigsorganisationen. Vi gör också tester och bedömningar åt andra myndigheter, till exempel Polisen och Försvarshögskolan. Kort sagt: vi ser till att rätt personer hamnar på rätt plats i totalförsvaret. Möt några av våra medarbetare – på vår webbplats hittar du filmer och intervjuer med några av oss! Därför tänker vi nytt och använder den senaste tekniken för att förenkla och förbättra, utveckla och leverera it-tjänsterna för den svenska socialförsäkringen. Välkommen till en av Sveriges största IT-avdelningar. It-utvecklingsenheterna i Luleå och Kalix befinner sig i en spännande utvecklingsfas och utökar nu verksamheten. Här utvecklar och förvaltar vi samhällsviktiga IT-lösningar inom bland annat arbetsmarknadsstöd, pension, externt informationsutbyte och datahantering. På våra kontor arbetar drygt 100 medarbetare, varav majoriteten är systemutvecklare. Du får arbeta med komplexa system i nära samarbete med erfarna kollegor i agila team. Tekniskt ansvar, kvalitet, säkerhet och automatisering är centrala delar av vardagen och du får möjlighet att påverka lösningar som används av stora delar av samhället varje dag. Systemutveckling, Java, backend, testare och systemanalytiker Vi söker nu fler kollegor till våra agila DevOps-team. Vårt uppdrag är att utveckla och förvalta samhällsviktiga system som ska vara tillförlitliga, säkra och användbara. För att lyckas med detta behöver vi stärka upp med flera kompetenser. Som systemutvecklare hos oss arbetar du med hela kedjan från kravanalys och utveckling till test, förvaltning och observerbarhet. Samtidigt finns möjlighet att fördjupa sig inom särskilda områden där vi har särskilt behov. Nedan kan du läsa mer om de kompetenser vi nu söker: Systemutveckling i Java: Vi söker systemutvecklare med tyngdpunkt inom backend och Java. Du arbetar med utveckling och förvaltning av komplexa system och är delaktig från analys och design till implementation, test och driftsättning. Vi ser gärna att du har förståelse för hela utvecklingskedjan och kan se hur kod, test, integration, infrastruktur och drift hänger ihop. Arbetet innebär att utveckla och förvalta system med höga krav på prestanda och robusthet. Teknisk test: Vi söker erfaren tekniska testare som kan ta ansvar för kvalitetssäkring av komplexa system. Du planerar, genomför och utvecklar tester och bidrar till att identifiera risker och fel tidigt i utvecklingsprocessen. Arbetet omfattar både automatiserade och manuella tester. Du har god teknisk förståelse och kan bedöma hur olika delar av ett system samverkar. Erfarenhet av testautomation och utveckling av testmetoder är värdefullt. Systemanalytiker: Vi söker erfaren systemanalytiker som kan analysera komplexa behov och problem och omsätta dem till tydliga krav och tekniska lösningar. Du arbetar nära verksamhet och IT och skapar struktur och förståelse mellan olika perspektiv. Rollen innebär att analysera behov och krav, förstå komplexa system och ta fram lösningsunderlag som kan omsättas av DevOps-teamen. Du samarbetar nära systemutvecklare, testare och andra kompetenser i den agila utvecklingsmiljön. Tjänsten innebär att du hanterar sekretessbelagda uppgifter vilket ställer höga krav på rätt hantering. Därför är det viktigt att du som ska arbeta hos oss har högt säkerhetsmedvetande. Det är ett jobb för dig som vill vara med och ta ansvar. Vi söker dig som har högskoleexamen eller erfarenheter och kvalifikationer som kan prövas likvärdiga har specialistkompetens inom systemutveckling inom Java, test, systemanalys agerar på eget initiativ och tar ansvar för att nå goda resultat samarbetar effektivt med andra för att nå gemensamma mål har ett systematiskt och noggrant arbetssätt kan förstå och analysera komplexa frågor har god kommunikativ förmåga, i tal och skrift har goda kunskaper i svenska, i tal och skrift. Det är meriterande om du har har erfarenhet av DevOps, Confluence, Bitbucket, Gitea, SQL, Linux har erfarenhet av microtjänstlösningar i OpenShift och Kubernetes har erfarenhet av agilt arbetssätt har erfarenhet av arbete i stor it-organisation har erfarenhet av arbete inom offentlig verksamhet. Vi lägger stor vikt vid dina personliga egenskaper. Övrigt Ett flertal tjänster, tillsvidare heltid, med tillträde enligt överenskommelse. Provanställning kan bli aktuellt. Vissa anställningar hos oss innebär deltagande i säkerhetskänslig verksamhet. För att bli anställd i en sådan tjänst krävs godkänd säkerhetsprövning enligt säkerhetsskyddslagen (2018:585). I enlighet med Försäkringskassans riktlinje för säkerhet genomförs bakgrundskontroller i denna rekrytering. Möjlighet till distansarbete finns om arbetet tillåter. I den här rekryteringen kan arbetspsykologiska test användas som en del i urvalsarbetet. Placeringsort: Luleå. Vill du veta mer om Försäkringskassan som arbetsgivare? items.desc: Systemutvecklare - fler lediga tjänster Din profil och bakgrund Du är civilingenjör, högskoleingenjör eller motsvarande. Du har intresse och erfarenhet inom några av dessa områden: Utveckling i C# Utveckling av Windowsklienter i utvecklingsplattformen .NET Utveckling av 3D verktyg mot Autodesk Revit eller andra AutoDesk produkter Utveckling med erfarenhet av ODA (Open Design Alliance) Erfarenhet av Revit & BIM: Avancerad geometrihantering via Revit API samt integrationer med Autodesk Forma. (ACC) BIM/arkitektur/konstruktion kunskap är meriterande Erfarenhet av Microsoft Visual Studio och Team Foundation Server är meriterande Databasdesign och -programmering mot relationsdatabaser Hos oss får du möjligheten att utvecklas och bli en expert inom C#, .NET och Maui. Vi genomför flera interna Coding Dojos och interna utvecklingsdagar där vi tävlar i kreativitet. Allt för att skapa en miljö där vi alla fortsätter att utvecklas till experter inom våra områden. Vi ser gärna att du är innovativ, gillar problemlösning och trivs bra med att arbeta i grupp. Stor vikt kommer att läggas vid personlig lämplighet. Eftersom vi är en global produktleverantör är det viktigt att du behärskar svenska och engelska, såväl i tal som i skrift. Om Ides Ides är ett svenskt mjukvaruföretag i tillväxt. Vi utvecklar och levererar lösningar för teknisk information och anläggningsdata – från idé till underhåll. Hos oss har du stora möjligheter att utvecklas och att påverka såväl dina egna arbetsuppgifter som resultat för företaget. Vi bedriver IT-utveckling på aktuella plattformar såsom C#, .NET, AutoCAD, Oracle, SQL Server, Maui m.m. Vi är ett modernt företag bestående av trevliga arbetskamrater i trivsamma lokaler. Vårt huvudkontor är centralt beläget i Linköping, bara ett par hundra meter från tågstationen. Vi har också kontor i Västerås, Karlstad, Göteborg och Shanghai, Kina. Ansökan och kontaktinformation Skicka in ditt personliga brev och CV till: jobs@idesglobal.com Märk ansökan med ”Systemutvecklare3D”.

items.desc: Join us in pioneering breakthroughs in healthcare. For everyone. Everywhere. Sustainably. Our inspiring and caring environment forms a global community that celebrates diversity and individuality. We encourage you to step beyond your comfort zone, offering resources and flexibility to foster your professional and personal growth, all while valuing your unique contributions. Together, we can beat cancer. At Varian, we bring together the worlds’ best talent to realize our vision of a world without fear of cancer. Together, we work passionately to develop and deliver easy-to-use, efficient oncology solutions. If you want to be part of this important mission, we want to hear from you. This role location is Denmark, but we will accept applications from any NRB listed country, please ensure you have the right to work and meet the criteria. Role Responsibilities: Consulting & Pre-Sales - Support sales teams and customers in identifying customer specific interoperability solutions. Draft a detailed solution proposal. Ensure feasibility. Project Management - Scope, plan and monitor implementation in an international environment. Follow deadlines agreed. Developing - Technically develop, implement, test and accept interface solutions following communication standards in health care (e.g. HL7, FHIR, Dicom, API, etc). Where required, develop customer specific software features. Support: Maintain and support customers and their interface solutions in production Mentoring: Share experience and support other team members Skills & Experience Required: Solid knowledge and professional experience in information technology. Solid scripting skills (e.g. TSQL, Java Script, VB, etc) Solid understanding of interoperability in health care including common standard (e.g. HL7, Dicom, FHIR) Solid project management skills Able to handle difficult internal and external customer situations including troubleshooting Associate degree or Bachelor degree in Computer Science or equivalent skills. Solid knowledge of technical writing / communication. Solid English skills (EU B2) Fighting cancer calls for big ideas . We envision a world without fear of cancer. Achieving this vision takes dedication and commitment from all of us, every single day. That's why we celebrate and value the distinctly beautiful and intersectional identities of each of our employees. We are a mirror of our patient-base, which allows us to innovate. Big ideas come from everywhere, and the best ideas are fostered by our unique individual experiences. At Varian, we encourage you to bring your whole self to work and believe your bold and authentic perspective will help to power more victories over cancer. #LI-REMOTE #LI-OSI Who we are : We are a team of more than 72,000 highly dedicated Healthineers in more than 70 countries. As a leader in medical technology, we constantly push the boundaries to create better outcomes and experiences for patients, no matter where they live or what health issues they are facing. Our portfolio is crucial for clinical decision-making and treatment pathways. How we work : When you join Siemens Healthineers, you become one in a global team of scientists, clinicians, developers, researchers, professionals, and skilled specialists, who believe in each individual’s potential to contribute with diverse ideas. We are from different backgrounds, cultures, religions, political and/or sexual orientations, and work together, to fight the world’s most threatening diseases and enable access to care, united by one purpose: to pioneer breakthroughs in healthcare. For everyone. Everywhere. Sustainably. To find out more about Healthineers’ specific businesses, please visit our company page here. As an equal opportunity employer, we welcome applications from individuals with disabilities. Data Privacy : We care about your data privacy and take compliance with GDPR as well as other data protection legislation seriously. For this reason, we ask you not to send us your CV or resume by email. We ask instead that you create a profile where you can upload your CV. Setting up a profile also lets us know you are interested in career opportunities with us and makes it easy for us to send you an alert when relevant positions become open. Register here to get started. Beware of Job Scams: Please beware of potentially fraudulent job postings or suspicious recruiting activity by persons that are currently posing as Siemens Healthineers recruiters/employees. These scammers may attempt to collect your confidential personal or financial information. If you are concerned that an offer of employment with Siemens Healthineers might be a scam or that the recruiter is not legitimate, please verify by searching for the posting on the Siemens Healthineers career site. To all recruitment agencies : Siemens Healthineers does not accept agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to our jobs alias, employees, or any other company location. PostNord, the leading supplier of communication and logistics solutions in the Nordic region, is searching a talented System Architect to join our ongoing transformation journey. items.desc: Due to internal promotion, we are now looking for a Medical Advisor to join our team! Bring your scientific expertise to a role where your insights, relationships, and ideas can help shape oncology care in Sweden. As a trusted scientific partner to healthcare professionals, you will focus on solid tumours, particularly gynaecological oncology, with the potential to expand into other tumour areas as our pipeline evolves. You will connect emerging evidence with clinical needs, turn insights into medical strategy, and collaborate with internal teams and external experts to advance patient care. If you are curious, collaborative, and motivated to make a meaningful impact, this is an opportunity to grow your expertise while uniting science, technology, and talent to get ahead of disease together. We create a place where people can grow, be their best, be safe, and feel welcome, valued and included. Discover more about our company wide benefits and life at GSK on our webpage Life at GSK | GSK In this role you will Build and strengthen trusted, peer-to-peer scientific relationships with oncology healthcare professionals and key stakeholders in solid tumours, with a particular focus on gynaecological oncology. Lead balanced, evidence-based scientific exchange, translating complex and emerging data into clear discussions that support informed clinical decisions and patient care. Identify unmet clinical needs, gather and document actionable insights, and translate them into recommendations for medical strategy. Contribute to clinical development by identifying and qualifying potential investigators and clinical sites. Represent GSK at scientific meetings, congresses, and expert forums, fostering scientific dialogue and bringing relevant knowledge back to the organisation. Partner with cross-functional colleagues on approved scientific education, medical projects and initiatives that address clinical needs. Why you? Basic Qualifications & Skills: We are looking for professionals with these required skills to achieve our goals: Advanced degree in medicine, pharmacy, life sciences or a related field, such as MD, PhD, PharmD or equivalent. Pharmaceutical-industry experience in Medical Affairs, Medical Science Liaison or a related scientific role. Strong knowledge of solid-tumour oncology clinical practice, treatment options and the evolving treatment landscape. Ability to make complex scientific information clear, relevant, and engaging for healthcare professionals. Demonstrated experience in building trusted, peer-to-peer relationships with oncology experts and healthcare teams. Ability to work independently, take initiative, and organise priorities effectively while complying with relevant regulations and standards. Fluent in Swedish and English both written and spoken. Preferred Qualifications & Skills: Please note the following skills are not necessary, just preferred, if you do not have them, please still apply: Clinical experience in oncology or direct patient care environments related to solid tumours, preferably gynecological cancer. Experience supporting clinical trials, investigator-initiated studies, or real-world evidence projects. Familiarity with the Swedish healthcare system, including hospitals and reimbursement processes. At Stegra, we’re building an impact-driven, sustainable company - and we need a diverse, inclusive team to make it happen. If you share our passion but don’t meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might be the perfect fit for this role, or another as we grow. At Stegra, we’re not just building a plant, we’re proving that sustainable industry is possible. And to do that, we need people like you. Join a team where safety comes first. Where we support each other, learn as we go, and make space for everyone to grow and contribute. This is your chance to be part of something big - while being closer to nature and leading a balanced, purposeful life. What you’ll do Right now, we are looking for a Digital Workplace Technician for our Digital Workplace team . This is a temporary 12-month assignment. As a Digital Workplace Technician at Stegra, you’ll help colleagues with everyday digital workplace questions and issues. This is a one-year contract where you’ll provide on-site and remote support, follow established processes, and build your experience with workplace tools and user support. Specific to this role, the day-to-day tasks will include the following, but as we are a growing company with few silos between teams, other tasks may be included as well. Provide in-person and remote support through Digi Bars (onsite support points), Slack, and ticketing systems. Help troubleshoot common issues with Microsoft 365, Slack, Zoom, Windows, macOS, devices, and user access, escalating issues when needed. Support onboarding and offboarding tasks, such as preparing devices and setting up user accounts. Follow existing support processes and help keep user guides, FAQs, and other support materials up to date. Contribute to self-service materials and simple workflow improvements with guidance from the team. Identify recurring support questions and share them with the team. Help prepare and share short digital tips or walkthroughs for colleagues. Learn about AI capabilities relevant to digital workplace support and share potential use cases with the team. What you’ll bring You’re curious and believe that real progress happens when we work together. You’re not afraid to challenge old ways of thinking - and you treat others with respect while doing it. At Stegra, we value people who take initiative, build trust, and help create a workplace where everyone can do their best. Who we think you are You have an interest in IT support, workplace technology, and helping people solve everyday problems. You communicate clearly and patiently, and enjoy working with colleagues. You’re comfortable providing direct support on-site as well as remotely. You have some familiarity with tools such as Microsoft 365, Slack, Zoom, Windows, or macOS. You’re organized, willing to follow established processes, and know when to ask for help or escalate an issue. You’re curious and willing to learn new tools and ways of working. It’s a bonus if you have Experience in a service or support role, or through a student project. An interest in writing clear instructions or maintaining user documentation. Basic familiarity with scripting, automation, or no-code tools. Benefits at Stegra At Stegra, you’ll join a company where your work has real impact on the climate, the industry, and future generations. We’re building a culture rooted in safety, trust, and inclusion, where people feel supported to grow and thrive. You’ll receive fair, competitive compensation aligned with collective agreements, along with benefits like up to 30 days of paid vacation, occupational pension, parental benefits, and insurance. If you need support with relocation or immigration, our relocation department will help guide you through the process, whether it’s permits, housing or other practical matters. You can also enjoy perks like subsidized gym memberships and bike leases, plus the everyday benefits of life closer to nature. Read more about Benefits at Stegra here. This is Stegra Stegra is on a mission to change the global steel industry by producing green hydrogen, iron, and steel - with the goal of eliminating CO₂ emissions. Instead of coal, we use green hydrogen and fossil-free electricity, meaning our primary emissions will be water and heat. By 2030, our ambition is to produce 5 million tonnes of green steel annually in our fully integrated, digitized, and sustainable plant in Boden, Northern Sweden - currently under construction. But this is just the beginning. Our expertise in green hydrogen will enable us to decarbonize industries beyond steel, paving the way for a cleaner future. Our Boden Site Our Boden site is located just west of Boden City, right in the heart of a growing green industrial hub in Northern Sweden. It’s where we’re building one of the world’s most modern, sustainable steel plants—designed with safety, efficiency, and …

As a UX Designer you will: Participate in all design stages from concept to final hand-off to engineering Develop original ideas that bring simplicity and user friendliness to complex design roadblocks Discuss designs and key milestone deliverables with peers and executive level stakeholders Perform user research and evaluate user feedback Prepare wireframes٫ storyboards٫ user flows٫ process flows and site maps to effectively communicate interaction and design ideas Stay up to date with the latest UI trends٫ techniques٫ and technologies We are looking for someone with: 2+ years’ experience of working in a Product or UX Designer position Profound UX design skills with a solid portfolio of design projects Strong team player abilities and presentation skills Experience designing user flows and intuitive end-to-end experiences Good understanding of user needs, behaviours, and system interactions Ability to translate complex requirements into clear, user-centred solutions Experience working with design systems and established UI patterns Solid experience working with Figma Good understanding of working in an Agile/Scrum development process Personal qualities: Curious and proactive, with a collaborative and solution-oriented mindset Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment and adapting to changing priorities Strong focus on delivering real value Good written and verbal English, in addition to Finnish, Norwegian or Swedish AI knowledge requirement AI literacy is expected for this role. You will be comfortable using approved AI tools to improve quality and productivity in everyday work (e.g., drafting, summarising, analysing, and automating routine tasks). You can write clear prompts/instructions, critically evaluate and validate AI outputs, and apply sound judgement when results are incomplete, biased, or incorrect. You understand and follow company policies and applicable legal/regulatory requirements for confidentiality, privacy, security, and responsible AI use (including not sharing sensitive data in unapproved tools). What’s in it for you? With us, you will be part of the important and meaningful work of developing solutions used in healthcare organizations. You have an important mission to make a difference that really matters. In addition, as a company we offer you professional growth, open and friendly culture, and an outstanding work-life balance! We believe that our organizational culture is an important part of enabling you to be successful. We provide a flexible hybrid work model as part of our culture and way of working. Finally, we also believe in curiosity and learning as a lifestyle. We want to encourage you to keep up that curiosity and deepen your knowledge on topics you’re interested in. For example, we host a ‘Keep Learning Week’ twice a year, a week where everyone at Tieto has the possibility to join different training courses in a truly global setting. items.desc: Company Description At lastminute.com, we live for the holidays. We are the European Travel-Tech leader in Dynamic Holiday Packages. With technology, we turn spontaneous thoughts into meaningful experiences, helping people travel the world Job Description The setup Job Title: Administrative B2B Specialist Working model: Hybrid Team: Partnership Location: Chiasso, Switzerland Contract: Fixed term (1 year) - full-time (36 hours/week) Travel time required: None / Minimal We are looking for an Administrative B2B Specialist to join the Partnership team at lastminute.com, a dynamic global company of 1,200 people powering millions of holiday journeys. The Partnership team manages a growing portfolio of B2B partners, and we need a person who becomes their administrative point of reference: someone who understands how our partnership business works, with its flows and specificities, and the ability to translate business and Finance needs into functional requirements and use cases for Tech teams. Good project management skills, including dependency analysis and coordination across processes, systems and teams. Sitting between the Partnership and the Administration & Finance teams, you will make sure that our partners' sales are correctly reconciled, invoiced and covered, bringing the needs of the team and of our partners to Finance, and Finance's requirements back to the team. You will own your tasks end to end with autonomy, and you will use data tools and AI smartly to make our current processes faster and more reliable. If you are precise with numbers, curious about how a business works behind the scenes and keen to improve the way things are done, keep reading! Key Responsibilities Be the contact point of the Partnership team with the Administration team, and Administrative department of partners, for all administrative tasks, and the administrative reference for our partners. Work closely with the Partnership team to learn the business flows and each partner's specificities, and represent the needs of the team and of the partners with Finance Verify on a monthly basis, using Excel, the sales data communicated by the partners against the data in the company systems, investigating and aligning any discrepancies. Provide the Administration team, on a monthly basis, with the data needed to issue accounting documents to the relevant partners, taking full end-to-end responsibility to ensure all internal and partner administrative steps are completed and numbers are properly reconciled. Create and manage Purchase Orders to cover the team's payable invoices. Manage the assigned tasks autonomously, from start to finish, meeting monthly deadlines. Propose and implement improvements to the current flows, also leveraging AI tools and automation to optimize activities. Qualifications Essential Excellent Excel skills (VLOOKUP, pivot tables, etc.). Confident, everyday use of AI tools to speed up analysis and routine tasks, with the curiosity to find new use cases. At least 3 years of office work experience in administrative tasks. Knowledge of administrative and accounting concepts (invoices, credit notes, purchase orders) . Languages: excellent written and spoken English. Italian is considered a welcome plus. University Degree required; a degree in Economics is considered a plus. High level of accuracy and attention to detail. Autonomy and proactivity in managing assigned tasks, with a problem-solving mindset. Good interpersonal skills and excellent ability to work in a team. Ability to work in a developing environment, whose dynamics and guidelines can change very quickly. Additional Information How we work together: An inclusive, friendly, and international environment (you’ll be working with colleagues from +10 countries and over 48 nationalities) Shorter working week (36h as full time), with a half working day on Fridays Flexible start and end of the working day Possibility to work from anywhere for a period of time per year defined according to local regulations How we learn together: Fri-Yays: half a day on Friday morning with a no-meeting mandate and dedicated to deep work, personal growth, learning and training and/or focus time. Professional and managerial skills development training paths, access to e-learning platforms and to our internal platform offering bespoke training content Other perks: 2 paid days off per year for volunteering purposes Occasional social events to foster connections among colleagues Travel industry discounts and flash exclusive staff fares We support our employees through life’s significant moments with leave options (e.g., parental responsibilities, marriages, bereavements, relocations, etc.) in line with local laws. Wish you were here? We do, too!

The Maison Louis Vuitton makes a promise to every of its customers: all of them, no matter the reason for their visit, should be cherished, encouraged to be themselves and a trusty relationship should be created. As the professional in charge of Stock, you will ensure a smooth product flow from delivery to client, in line with the standards of the Brand. Job responsibilities Manage product receipt and restocking operations, as well as the sales plan Effectively manage stock levels by coordinating with the supply chain Ensure efficient organisation of the back-of-house area Manage product transfers Monitor logistics KPIs and contribute to the store’s performance targets Manage inventory Implement new processes/projects relating to logistics and the organisation of the back-of-house Provide sales support and customer service Profile Your strenghts : Good knowledge of stock/supply chain processes Able to work in a fast-paced environment Strong hands-on mindset Retail operational skills Solution and results oriented Integrity and trust Proactive with good team spirit and able to take initiatives Computer skills Fluency in German/Swiss-German and English knowledge LOUIS VUITTON MAISON Founded in Paris in 1854, Louis Vuitton perpetuates the ambitious vision of its namesake. From his origins as a master trunk maker, manufacturing boxes used to pack both everyday objects as well as voluminous wardrobes, Louis Vuitton and his successors introduced numerous innovations including the advent of the flat-top trunk, lightweight canvas, signature patterns, and the tumbler lock. Today, Louis Vuitton’s legacy is expressed through its rigorous spirit of innovation, the boldness of its creations and an uncompromising demand for excellence.

items.desc: Applications are invited for this fixed term, full time role as Medical Laboratory Assistant (MLA) in the specimen reception section for the South East Haematological Malignancy Diagnostic Service (SE-HMDS) at King’s College Hospital. The reception is integral to the SE-HMDS, acting as a central sample receipt point for the four key laboratories that make up the SE-HMDS plus the clinically lead morphology service. The most important part of the role will be sample handling and electronic logging of the samples received. The SE-HMDS reception also contribute to the preparation, maintenance, operation and quality assurance of laboratory equipment. Training and development is a key focus at Synnovis and this is an excellent opportunity to enhance skills and knowledge in a specialist department environment. There is also a keen interest in Research & Development within the departments that is supported by various funds and collaborators as we endeavour to provide a leading and fit-for-purpose service to our patients. There is culture of continuous quality improvement that applies to both staff and departmental development. This is a great opportunity to work amongst a team of dedicated and patient focused individuals and enhance administrative, communication and data/sample handling skills. The successful candidate will be a team player and will be working closely with the laboratories, scientific and clinical staff. They must have excellent attention to detail and be able to accurately and efficiently transfer data on to electronic systems. Effective communication skills with all levels of staff, internal and external users is essential. There is a variety of laboratory information management systems (LIMS) in use within the laboratories, candidates must have good IT skills, and prior experience of various forms of LIMS is beneficial. The role largely involves accurate transfer of clinical information and specimen prioritisation with the requirement for good medical/scientific literacy skills. Working knowledge of the Health & Safety requirements of handling biological materials is desirable and experience in the preparation of blood and bone marrow slides would be of additional benefit. The SE-HMDS is a regional centre for diagnostic services, providing UKAS accredited Immunophenotyping, Morphology, Cytogenetic, Molecular Diagnostic and Histopathology services covering most of Southeast England. There has been a steady rise in referrals to the SE-HMDS, from clinicians who require increasingly sophisticated and accurate haematological investigations, for diagnosis and disease monitoring. As a member of the SE-HMDS reception, you are the essential first and last points of contact for patient specimens and results, with service quality, a key focus throughout. As an essential part of the SE-HMDS, the reception team also have access to a number of developmental activities including clinical presentations, webinars and integrated departmental training sessions for haematological malignancies. Here you can learn more about the various departments, investigations and the patients that we serve. The SE-HMDS reception area acts as a central location for receipt of samples, performing pre and post analytical procedures and other support for the five areas that make up SE-HMDS: Immunophenotyping, Morphology, Cytogenetics, Laboratory Molecular Haemato-Oncology and Histopathology. The post holder will work as a member of the support staff to assist SE-HMDS in the appropriate handling, receipt and distribution of specimens. The main responsibility of the post holder will be to perform the electronic receipt, data management and quality assurance of specimens, as well as preparation, maintenance, operation and quality assurance of laboratory slide staining equipment. Concentration, attention to detail and accurate transcription of data are essential skills to these processes and form the greater part of the working day. Good IT and typing skills are required to perform this role and training will be provided for the use of the various and bespoke LIMS. The post holder will offer a helpful and professional service to all visitors and enquiries from a broad spectrum of service users under the direction of qualified laboratory staff and where appropriate will assist in the collection and compilation of data for management purposes. It will be essential that the post hold can follow written and verbal instructions as directed by the supervisor, senior scientists, operational and quality leads or head or section. Prioritisation and time management skills are required for time sensitive tests and urgency of clinical investigations within a busy environment. Once competence in tasks is achieved members of the team are also required to assist in the training of others whilst maintaining and promoting safe working practises. The post holder must be able to effectively and appropriately communicate within the reception team, the …

items.desc: You will support the Biomedical Scientists by performing a wide variety of laboratory tasks. Duties vary between departments which include the sorting, preparation, processing and handling of blood, urine, tissue and bodily fluids. You should have an interest in science, be self-confident and motivated. You must possess a wide range of skills demonstrating good numeracy and literacy, a high standard of verbal and written English, keyboard data entry skills and attention to detail. You will also be required to sit or stand for extended periods of time whilst preparing samples and inputting data, therefore the ability to multi-task and work flexibly are essential. Your shifts will be set within a 24/7 shift system and there will be a requirement to work nights, weekends and bank holidays on rotation with other team members NB HCPC portfolios cannot be supported in this area as there is insufficient exposure to the main Laboratory. Your duties will include: Sample preparation - Identification checks & barcode labelling Data entry - Inputting patient data onto the laboratory computer system Reception duties - Face to face and telephone queries from service users Housekeeping duties Participate in quality & audit work Closing Date: 2 November 2026 Interview Date: 14 November 2026 Candidates who have applied for this vacancy within the last 3 months and were unsuccessful at any stage of the recruitment process should not reapply unless you can demonstrate additional relevant skills, qualifications or experience acquired since your previous application.' In return we will offer: Development opportunities, both professional and leadership development On-going support from recruitment to when you join our team and beyond. Staff benefits including employee assistance programme, discounted gym membership, onsite fitness classes, car schemes Key Facts: We see on average 4810 OP appointments a day. We are the 4 th busiest Trauma & Orthopaedic outpatients department in England – an average of 2077 per week. The position is available full time, starting in January 2027 (or as soon as possible thereafter, with flexibility to start earlier). Molecular glues are an emerging class of
items.desc: Job number NAT02293 Faculties Faculty of Natural Sciences Departments Department of Chemistry Salary or Salary range £48,246 - £58,318 per annum Location/campus White City Campus - On site only Contract type work pattern Full time - Fixed term Posting End Date 18 Nov 2026 About the role We are seeking a talented technician to join the team in the group of Professor Ed Tate at Imperial College London. This role will support the production and characterisation of recombinant proteins for molecular glue discovery. The position is available full time, starting in January 2027 (or as soon as possible thereafter, with flexibility to start earlier). Molecular glues are an emerging class of small molecules which induce or stabilise protein-protein interactions, creating new opportunities to modulate biological processes and tackle ‘undruggable’ targets through induced proximity. Despite growing interest in the field, there remain limited approaches for the systematic discovery of molecular glues. As a result, there is a need for scalable and generalisable molecular glue discovery platforms that enable target proteins and compound libraries to be screened across the proteome. To support these efforts, we are establishing workflows for the production and characterisation of recombinant proteins for use in proteomic, biochemical, biophysical and cell-based assays. The successful candidate will play a central role in generating high-quality protein reagents and supporting downstream studies that underpin molecular glue discovery. What you would be doing Your role will focus on the expression, purification and characterisation of recombinant proteins using mammalian cell expression to support molecular glue discovery projects. You may also contribute to the development of biochemical or biophysical assays using these proteins. You will be contributing to a dynamic and ambitious research programme, working in a multidisciplinary team spanning chemical biology, proteomics and medicinal chemistry. In addition to your core activities, you will support the day-to-day running of the laboratory. This includes maintaining equipment, purchasing and organising consumables, disposal of biohazard and chemical waste, participating in laboratory duty rotas, and providing introductory training for new users. The Tate group is culturally diverse and highly multidisciplinary, with project teams encompassing scientists at all levels of experience and from a variety of backgrounds (chemical biology, cell biology, proteomics, cancer biology, drug discovery, etc.). Technicians are expected to engage in the various projects across the Tate group and offer support on an ad-hoc basis as required outside of their core projects. We are looking for candidates who can thrive in this dynamic and creative environment and take optimal advantage of the many training opportunities it provides. What we are looking for Essential criteria for the role include: A minimum of a BSc and/or MSc qualification in biochemistry, chemical biology, biotechnology, or a closely related field, or an equivalent level of professional qualifications and experience. Experience with mammalian cell culture, protein purification and characterisation Knowledge of, data analysis, and safe laboratory working practices. Desirable experience for this role includes one or more of the following: experience with HEK293, Expi293 or related mammalian expression systems; biochemical or biophysical assay development; experience with plate-based assays; experience of ternary-complex formation assays; relevant laboratory management; knowledge of the molecular glue field. What we can offer you Working within the Tate group would give you the opportunity to work with >60 scientists at all levels from undergraduates to postdoctoral researchers with our state-of-the-art labs in West London, including the Agilent Measurement Suite and Imperial Drug Discovery Hub. You will be joining a team with an excellent track record in the areas of molecular glues and induced proximity mechanisms (https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c12299; https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c01420; The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity. Grow your career: Gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 39 days off a year and generous pension schemes). Further information Starting in January 2027 (or as soon as possible thereafter). Full time, fixed term, for up to 24 months in the first instance. items.desc: Job Introduction Scientist Analytical Chemistry Hoddesdon Pharmaron is a global CRO helping pharma and biotech companies bring new therapies to life. With over 25,000 employees worldwide across 23 locations in the US, UK and China, we support drug discovery through to manufacturing with fully integrated, high-quality services. We’re proud of the impact we make and just last year, we supported over 780 discovery projects, 1,000+ CMC programmes, and 1,000+ clinical trials across all phases. Our teams are involved in everything from small molecules to biologics and gene therapies, and we work with more than 3,000 global customers. To learn more, visit www.pharmaron.com. Is this you? Do you love getting hands-on with HPLC and seeing your results move a project forward? Are you keen to build your analytical skills in a fast-paced, GMP environment alongside experienced scientists? If so, we’d love to hear from you. We’re looking for a Scientist in Analytical Chemistry with solid HPLC experience, ideally alongside GC, SFC, NMR or other techniques used to characterise APIs. You’ll support our chemistry projects, help develop and validate analytical methods, contribute to the characterisation of Starting Materials, Intermediates and APIs, and work closely with our Process Chemistry colleagues. What’s in it for you at Pharmaron A vibrant, dynamic place to work: we’re a highly specialised, growing company in a critical sector of the economy. Our future is strong and exciting, and you can be part of it. Room to grow: our rapid growth means more opportunities for you to learn, develop and progress faster. A team that has your back: we support each other and enjoy what we do. After all, you spend about a third of your time here! What you’ll bring A BSc (Hons) or MSc in Analytical Chemistry or Chemistry Relevant experience in an Analytical Chemistry laboratory Significant expertise in HPLC and/or UPLC methods Hands-on experience and up-to-date knowledge of other analytical methodologies Experience working to GLP and GMP What you’ll be doing Analysing APIs, Intermediates, Starting Materials and Raw Materials using HPLC and other analytical methods Delivering your assigned tasks to tight deadlines Stepping in to learn new techniques whenever a project needs it Solving scientific problems as they arise Working effectively in a GMP laboratory Who we are “We are a dynamic, fast-growing company, with an enviable reputation for leading edge science, offering contract research services to some of the world’s leading pharmaceutical companies, solving what were believed to be unsolvable scientific challenges.” We relentlessly push the boundaries of scientific excellence to deliver solutions for our clients, always ethically and with integrity. We take pride in our professionalism and in giving our very best every time. Where you’ll work Picture yourself on our Hoddesdon campus in Hertfordshire: several purpose-built scientific and administrative buildings, a dedicated conference area and more than 5,000 m² of premier R&D space. It’s home to established Process Chemistry, Analytical Chemistry, Product Development and Drug Discovery teams, with state-of-the-art GMP facilities for API development, Oral Solid Dose manufacture, formulation development and process chemistry. It’s a highly supportive, team-focused environment where you can develop and fulfil your true potential. Your team Our Analytical Chemistry team supports other chemistry functions and our science partners with advanced analytical solutions that help move medicines to market. Here you’ll: Gain exposure to a wide range of modern techniques, including UHPLC, NMR and GC-MS Experience both early- and late-phase pharmaceutical development Apply your problem-solving skills across a wide variety of R&D projects Contribute to the development and validation of modern methods for testing raw materials, intermediates, APIs and material characterisation Explore further opportunities in polymorph screening, crystallisation optimisation and pre-formulation development What we offer A competitive salary and a progressive, comprehensive benefits package A state-of-the-art working environment on site Real growth and development, including funding for relevant training programmes Salary Competitive Frequency Annual Job Reference ukpharmaron/TP/141/781 Contract Type Permanent Contract Closing Date No expiry date Job Category Scientific (Analytical Chemistry) Division Process Chemistry Location Hoddesdon, United Kingdom Posted on 15 October, 2026

items.desc: We are looking to recruit an experienced Cardiac Physiologist/Clinical Scientist in Echocardiography. The post is a fixed term 22-month contract funded as part of a research study funded through commercial partnership with Edwards. The successful candidate will assist in the development and delivery of an electronic fast track referral pathway across Cheshire and Merseyside for patients with severe aortic stenosis. The candidate will assist in the Standardisation of diagnostic and triage protocols for suspected AS to support the implementation of the pathway and enhance the identification of symptomatic and asymptomatic patients with severe AS by strengthening regional collaboration across NHS partners. The cardiac physiologist will be based at Liverpool Heart and Chest Hospital and will be expected to provide hands on echocardiography support and educational support across multiple hospital sites; there will be an innovative element to this post. Main duties of the job Provide specialised technical expertise to the area of echocardiography. Provide specialised technical expertise in diagnosis of valvular heart disease, particularly aortic stenosis Provide independent outreach Provide direct point of communication and liaison between regional echo services and LHCH structural valve service Provide close collaboration with TAVI specialist nurses and medical teams. Demonstrates empathy when dealing with patients in distressing conditions. Independently interprets results and provides factual reports for highly specialised diagnostic cardiac investigations Communicates effectively and advises both clinical and non-clinical staff regarding outcomes of diagnostic investigations. Undertakes supervision & training for Clinical staff, Trainee Cardiac Physiologists and other allied health professionals. Within their designated area assists the lead physiologist in implementing departmental strategies to ensure continuing development of patient-focused services in line with activity targets and the requirements of the Directorate. Assists lead physiologist in monitoring and maintaining quality of services within designated section. Ensures that individual own level of practice is kept up to date. Demonstrates active participation in clinical audit, and R&D activities. Has awareness of future implications for development of current Cardiology As the largest single site specialist heart and chest hospital in the UK, we, at Liverpool Heart and Chest Hospital, have a clear vision 'to be the best cardiothoracic integrated healthcare organisation'. We are a resilient, vibrant, and creative borough in the heart of London, with strong, diverse communities and a powerful set of shared values. Over the past twenty years, the Council has built up first-class services, outstanding public infrastructure, and a reputation for excellence, innovation, and ambition. We are leading the way on essential work such as our fight for equity in Hackney with a particular focus on becoming an actively anti-racist borough. But the work doesn’t stop there, we are proactive in our approach to bringing fairness to all aspects of life including gender, neurodiversity and across the poverty divide. Our Adult Social Care vision is that “We want you to achieve what matters to you, in partnership with our communities in Hackney. Where you need support, together we can find a solution that keeps you safe, well and independent.” We have an ambition to make a step-change in how we prevent, reduce and delay the development of social care needs, working collaboratively across the council, and with our partners in health, and the voluntary, community and faith sector in order to achieve this. Our Public Health Service plays a vital role in this mission. Together, we’re passionate about improving the health and wellbeing of our communities in Hackney. We work collaboratively and creatively to address health inequalities and create a healthier future for all. You can find out more about how we work in Adult Social Care, and how it is changing, by reading our annual report and three year plan at https://www.hackney.gov.uk/health-and-social-care/adult-social-care/adult-social-care-annual-reports-and-strategies. If you would like to find out more information about public health in the City and Hackney, please visit the Hackney and City of London Health and Wellbeing Profiles website at https://cityhackneyhealth.org.uk/ and the services recruitment page at https://recruitment.hackney.gov.uk/the-public-health-team/. As a Public Health Analyst working within our Adult Social Care transformation programme, you will play a critical role in applying analytical skills to prevent, reduce, and delay the development of social care needs, address health inequalities, and build good health in all of Hackney’s communities. This role will join the team on a fixed term contract for 2 years and will be focussed exclusively on the Adult Social Care “Understanding demand and maximising prevention” programme. The programme covers a range of different initiatives that cut across the whole health and social care system; including changes to how we provide holistic support to people approaching social care for the first time, how we ensure people remain stable while waiting for an assessment or a review, and how we support those with the most complex needs to keep them well. As well as delivering partnership projects, the programme supports culture change within individual teams, ensuring all staff have the capability, motivation and opportunity to work preventatively on a day to day basis. The role will sit within the Public Health Intelligence Team (PHIT), which supports strategic planning and service development across Hackney and the City of London. This ensures the postholder will have appropriate analytical line management, professional support, and quality assurance, while maintaining clear accountability to the Adult Social Care prevention programme for delivery of the agreed project objectives. In this role you will be responsible for the end-to-end delivery of analytical projects that help the department to understand and model social care demand, and embed a population health management approach within Adult Social Care. You will transform complex datasets into actionable insight using tools such as Tableau, Python, and Google Workspace. This will include analysing demographic, health and service data, delivering all stages of the evaluation cycle, analysing quantitative and qualitative data and preparing reports for a range of stakeholders, use of machine learning and development of predictive models, and developing a longer term model of demand for Adult Social Care. You will also provide expert analytical advice, contribute to evidence-based planning and evaluation and help build data and insight capability across the wider ASC Transformation service. You will lead on specific work areas and collaborate with colleagues across and beyond the organisation to make best use of analytical and data resources, ensuring insight is co-produced, ethical, secure and impactful. items.desc: About Us Flok Jobs is on a mission to fix hospitality hiring for good. We're building the UK's first direct, real time platform connecting hospitality venues with verified, flexible staff. No agencies, no fees, no nonsense. Founded on more than 25 years of hands on hospitality and recruitment industry experience, Flok is solving a problem that touches a multi billion pound industry and has never been properly solved. We're not just an idea on a slide deck. We already have real traction, an active investment pipeline, and a founding technical team with over 30 years of combined development experience between them, including a CTO with more than 20 years of enterprise technology leadership. We're small right now, but we're going big. As we head towards launch with genuine momentum behind us, there's real room for the right person to step in, make their mark, and grow with us as the business scales. This role could suit someone fresh out of university looking for their first real opportunity to make an impact, or a more experienced developer looking for genuine ownership and influence at an early stage company. What matters most to us is attitude, curiosity and the willingness to learn and grow. Experience level is secondary to that. Important. Please Read Before Applying This role has two distinct stages, and because we're building Flok the right way, with honesty and respect for the people who join us, we want to be completely upfront about both before you apply. Stage 1 (unpaid, up to 4 to 6 weeks) An initial period working directly with our Director, CTO and wider team, including one of our existing developers, to help get Flok ready for launch. From the moment you start, your input matters. You'll be involved in real discussions, technical decisions and product priorities alongside a team that already brings decades of hospitality, recruitment and software development experience to the table. This period is unpaid. There is no guaranteed minimum number of hours, and either side can end the arrangement at any time. Stage 2 (paid and/or equity, ongoing) At the end of Stage 1, we'll have an honest conversation about where the business is at and what we can offer. Depending on our position at that point, including funding and investment progress, this could be A wage, or Equity in the business, or A combination of both, or Equity initially, with a wage introduced as the business grows Given the traction and investment conversations already underway, we expect to be in a genuinely stronger position by the end of Stage 1 than many early stage startups. We know unpaid stages can raise legitimate concerns, so here's what we commit to. You'll work directly with the Director, CTO and team, not sit on the sidelines, as your contribution and input will matter from day one. At the end of Stage 1, we'll give you a clear, honest answer about what we can offer, with real feedback either way. We won't ask for more time or scope than we agree upfront. No unpaid overtime, no scope creep. If we're not able to offer a wage or equity at that point, we'll tell you clearly, rather than leaving it vague. This arrangement will only suit candidates who are able to take on unpaid work for this initial period. If that doesn't work for your circumstances, we completely understand, and we'd encourage you to look at paid roles elsewhere with no hard feelings. Why Now Is a Great Time to Join This isn't a startup starting from zero. It's a business built on more than 25 years of hospitality and recruitment expertise, backed by a technical team with over 30 years of development experience between them, and with real momentum and investment interest already in motion. Joining now means getting in ahead of the crowd, while the business is still small enough that every person genuinely shapes what Flok becomes. Whether you're a graduate looking to prove yourself on a real product from day one, or a more established developer who wants meaningful ownership instead of being one voice among many, this is a chance to be part of decisions that actually matter, not just execute someone else's roadmap. Working Arrangement We're based out of our Loughborough office. Hybrid working is available, as some of our existing team already work this way. We ask that you're able to come into the office regularly enough to stay closely connected with the Director and CTO, given the collaborative, fast moving nature of a pre launch startup with real deadlines ahead. items.desc: In a nutshell, we’re all about making great wine better, for everyone. We partner directly with the world’s best independent winemakers to bring our members better-quality wine for a better price. No thirsty middlemen as far as the eye can see. It’s a different way of doing things, sure. But it works. We’re one of the UK’s favourite wine clubs, shipping over 1 million (!) cases a year to curious wine lovers. And with an ambitious road ahead, we’ve got no plans on plugging the cork on growth. Our global team (we have offices in the US and Australia, too) is entrepreneurial by nature, obsessive about customer experience and driven by performance. All things that make Naked a great place to grow both personally and professionally. And yes, we like wine. A lot – we even have a wine fridge in the office. It takes a village to run Naked. That’s why we’re always on the lookout for eager talent to join the bunch. And now, our Planning team is looking for a Supply Network Planning Analyst to be part of the fun. As our Supply Network Planning Analyst, you will design, build, and maintain the decision-making tools that guide how stock moves through our supply network across two key markets, the US and AUS. Focused on execution, allocation, and systems optimisation, you will engineer spreadsheet models and GEM workflows to determine exact stock movements, optimise production timing and protect shelf-life viability. Serving as the primary collaborative bridge to our Commercial team in the US, you will provide clear visibility into stock availability, campaign readiness, and potential fulfilment risks. So if you’re keen to help us connect more wine lovers with talented winemakers, there’s a Naked welcome pack with your name on it. Together, we’ll take Naked Wines to the next level – and share our not-so-well-kept secret with the world. Build clear visibility models: Engineer dynamic spreadsheet models to project inventory levels, track stock aging, and mitigate shelf-life expiration risks. Guide risk management: Proactively identify potential network bottlenecks, delayed arrivals, or stockouts, and collaborate on mitigation options to keep operations flowing smoothly. Ensure campaign readiness: Monitor stock allocation progress so the exact right inventory is positioned in the right place, at the right time, to support key sales and marketing initiatives. What you'll bring Advanced Google Sheets capability: A deep understanding of system architecture, complex formulas, and array functions to build robust operational tools. Operational system design skills: A strong background in building decision-making tools that translate logistical data into actionable insights. We don't compete with AI model providers, we orchestrate them: every major voice, music and sound model, working together in one production engine. The world's largest agencies, publishers and platforms, including Omnicom, Publicis, Dentsu, Bloomberg, Global and Acast, use AudioStack to produce anything from a single radio spot to thousands of hyperlocal ad variants in days rather than weeks. About the role Every ad, voiceover and audiobook we deliver depends on the infrastructure underneath it. We're looking for an Infrastructure Engineer to co-own that foundation alongside our infrastructure lead, keeping it secure, reliable and cost-effective as we grow. You'll join a small, collaborative engineering team and work with engineers across the company. We are looking for a mid or senior engineer with real ownership, and you'll have support from our tech and infrastructure leads as you take responsibilities across infrastructure, site reliability and devops. Location: London, hybrid (2 days a week in the office) Level: Mid to Senior Level What you'll do Infrastructure Maintain and improve our AWS infrastructure through Terraform - including our Kubernetes (EKS) clusters, RDS databases, networking and our ad-tech VAST servers. Write runbooks and documentation so infrastructure knowledge is shared across the team. Site reliability (SRE) Look after our observability stack (Grafana, Prometheus, CloudWatch, Logfire) and the alerts that tell us when something's wrong. Join our on-call rotation to help us meet our enterprise SLAs, and carry out maintenance with zero or planned downtime. Help improve how we handle and learn from incidents. Provide tooling that let teams spin up prototypes and automations fast. Be a go-to person for infrastructure and platform questions across engineering. Practical knowledge of networking and security: VPCs, DNS, load balancers, TLS and least-privilege access. Comfort writing Python and working with Git, and curiosity about AI coding tools. DevOps knowledge on how to build or improve CI/CD pipelines and developer tooling. Experience with Auth0 or OAuth, RDS operations, or SOC2 audits. Not sure you tick every box? Please apply anyway. Skills come from many places, we value transferable experience. Benefits What we offer Stock options. Hybrid working with flexible hours. The chance to shape the culture and engineering practices of a growing company. An international team across London, Barcelona and New York. Dog-friendly offices (Swanson and Bernie say hello). Our process: a 30-minute intro call, a technical conversation with our infrastructure lead, then an in-person interview in London. Our commitment to inclusion: to build audio that works for everyone, we need a team with different perspectives, experiences and backgrounds. We welcome applications regardless of race, religion, colour, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age or disability, and especially encourage people from groups underrepresented in tech. If you need any adjustments to apply or interview, or would like to talk about flexible working, just let us know. It won't affect your application.

items.desc: Specialism Software Engineering, AI/ML, Data Job type Permanent Location London Salary £100,000 - £140,000 per annum There are a lot of AI startups out there right now, all claiming they're doing something different. But how many are actually building technology that businesses genuinely need? This company is taking an interesting approach to that. They're focused on industries where people are still spending ridiculous amounts of time working through documents, managing spreadsheets, processing emails and dealing with admin that really shouldn't need so much human involvement. The aim is to change that by building AI powered systems that take on the repetitive work and make these processes far more efficient. And that's where you come in. They're looking for a Founding Forward Deployed Engineer to join a small engineering team and help turn some pretty complicated business problems into working software. You will be getting close to the problems themselves, understanding how things currently work and figuring out where AI can actually make a difference. It's a hands on engineering role, where you'll be working across AI, backend systems, integrations, data and whatever else is needed to get something working. There won't always be a clear brief or someone telling you exactly how to approach a problem, so you'll need to be comfortable figuring things out for yourself. The good thing is, you'll actually get to see what happens when your work goes live. You're not spending months building something without knowing whether it's going to be useful. It's still early days, but there's a clear plan for where they want to take the business, along with the investment and backing to make it happen. The engineering team is small, which means you'll be working closely with senior technical leadership, having a say in how things are built and taking on far more responsibility than you would in a larger company. There's also meaningful equity on offer, so you'll have a stake in what you're helping to create. It's not going to suit everyone. There's a lot to figure out, things will change quickly and some weeks will be pretty demanding. But if you like the idea of joining something early, getting stuck into difficult engineering problems and having the freedom to build things your way, there's a lot to like here. What are they looking for? A strong software engineer who's comfortable working across the stack and isn't restricted to one language. Someone who's already built and shipped AI applications into production. Experience working in environments where you've had to take ownership and figure things out without much hand nholding. An interest in building products from scratch and solving problems that don't always have an obvious answer. You don't need to have 'Forward Deployed Engineer' on your CV. What's more important is that you enjoy getting close to the problem, working out what needs building and then actually building it. If this sounds like something you'd be interested in hearing more about, apply below. Leah Smith Talent Consultant 07527938219

As a Platform Engineer, you’ll play a vital role in designing, automating and optimising secure, cloud-native platforms that enable critical operations. You’ll take ownership of complex engineering challenges, apply creative thinking to improve performance and resilience, and collaborate with talented teams to deliver solutions that make a real difference. Working in an agile, supportive environment, you’ll have the opportunity to develop your expertise, influence technical decisions and contribute to high-impact programmes that help protect the UK’s digital future. Engineer & Integrate: Develop and configure infrastructure, networking and Linux-based systems, ensuring seamless integration across platform components. Innovate & Improve: Apply modern DevOps practices, infrastructure automation and cloud-native technologies to continuously enhance engineering capabilities. Collaborate & Contribute: Work closely with software engineers, architects and delivery teams in an agile environment, sharing knowledge and contributing to technical decisions. Required qualifications to be successful in this role To succeed in this role, you should have strong hands-on experience in Kubernetes and platform engineering, combined with a practical understanding of DevOps, automation and cloud-native technologies. You'll be comfortable working with Linux-based infrastructure, diagnosing complex technical challenges and contributing to secure, resilient solutions. We’re looking for someone who takes ownership, approaches problems creatively and thrives in a collaborative engineering environment where continuous learning and improvement are encouraged. Essential skills and experience: Kubernetes: Strong hands-on experience deploying, managing, troubleshooting and optimising Kubernetes clusters and containerised workloads. This is a key requirement. Platform Engineering: Proven experience designing, building and supporting reliable, scalable cloud-native platforms. DevOps & CI/CD: Practical experience with GitLab, CI/CD pipelines and modern DevOps tooling. items.desc: Description About Bright Software Group At Bright, we are powering the digital practice of tomorrow – today. We deliver products that help accountants, payroll bureaus, and businesses across the UK and Ireland work smarter and win more. Our innovative solutions and outstanding customer experiences enable our customers to run their businesses efficiently and serve their customers brilliantly. We believe understanding is the difference between working and winning. The Role We are looking for a proactive Software Engineer to strengthen the backend of the TimeKeeper platform. The role is Python-led, covering the services, APIs and data layer behind our web and mobile applications, and working closely with engineers across the stack. It suits an engineer who enjoys solving problems across a varied technology stack and picks up new tools quickly. Proficiency in every technology listed below is not expected; being proactive and keen to learn is what matters most. What You'll Do Design, build and maintain backend services in Python (Flask) that power the TimeKeeper platform Develop and improve APIs, data models and Postgres queries, with a focus on reliability and performance Shape features based on customer and team feedback, and deliver them alongside the web and mobile teams Write automated tests, investigate issues and fix bugs Review pull requests and share knowledge with the wider team Contribute to infrastructure and deployment work across AWS, Terraform and Redis Prioritise and manage multiple tasks, delivering on time and picking up new topics as needed Build strong working relationships and contribute positively to the team What We're Looking For Essential Minimum 4 years of professional experience as a Software Engineer, with a strong backend focus Professional experience building and maintaining backend services and APIs in Python Working knowledge of SQL and relational databases Experience writing automated tests and reviewing code Comfortable working alongside AI tools; curious about how technology can make you better at your job Nice to Have Experience with Python frameworks and libraries such as Flask, Django or SQLAlchemy Relevant AWS infrastructure experience, including Infrastructure as Code (Terraform) Experience with Postgres and Redis in production Familiarity with React or React Native, enough to work effectively with front-end colleagues Bachelor's or higher degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering or a related field The Technology Stack • Python (Flask) – Backend services • Postgres – Database • Redis – Application cache layer • AWS – Infrastructure • Terraform – Infrastructure as Code • React – Web application • React Native – Mobile application Don’t worry if you aren’t proficient in all of these, the main thing is you are proactive and able to pick new things up. Working At Bright Bright builds software that genuinely makes people's working lives easier. That matters — and you'll never have to apologise for what you're selling. But honestly, the first thing people mention is the culture. It's collaborative, it's human, and we're not a small company anymore, but it still feels like one — in the best way. People are genuinely looked after here — that's not just something we say. You get real autonomy to learn, grow, and make an impact. And right now is a genuinely exciting time to join. We're growing fast, investing heavily in AI, and that creates real opportunity — for the business and for the people in it. It's a place where curious people thrive. About Bright Software Group Bright is built around brilliant people doing brilliant work, and we invest in making sure the environment matches that ambition. You’ll have genuine flexibility in how you work, backed by modern practices that adapt to how work actually gets done today. We recognise and celebrate strong performance, support your wellbeing, and give you real opportunities to grow, not just in role, but in career. We’re proud of the culture we’ve built. It’s high-trust, high-expectation, and focused on doing great work. That’s Bright
