items.desc: Azure Cloud Architect At UBDS, we help organisations transform through cloud, cyber security, AI and digital innovation. This is a hands-on architecture role with a strong focus on Microsoft Azure, cloud infrastructure, storage and automation. You will work closely with engineering, security and delivery teams to design and implement cloud solutions, providing technical leadership while remaining actively involved in development, configuration and deployment activities. What You'll Do Design and deliver secure, scalable and resilient cloud architecture using Microsoft Azure. Support the migration and modernisation of on-premise file services and storage into Azure. Design hybrid cloud environments, including connectivity between on-premise infrastructure and Azure. Provide architectural guidance and hands-on engineering support to Cloud and DevOps teams. Develop and maintain Infrastructure as Code and automated deployment solutions. Support scripting, development and automation using PowerShell, Python or similar technologies. Design and implement CI/CD pipelines and deployment processes using Azure DevOps or equivalent tooling. Produce architecture documentation, technical designs and implementation guidance. Engage with customers and stakeholders to translate business and technical requirements into effective cloud solutions. What We're Looking For Strong experience designing and delivering Microsoft Azure cloud architecture. Proven experience as an Azure Architect, Cloud Architect, Technical Architect or senior Cloud Engineer. Strong understanding of Azure infrastructure, including compute, networking, storage and identity. Hands-on experience with Azure Files, Azure Storage and hybrid file-sharing solutions. Our services include street outreach, assessment hubs, supported accommodation, and tenancy support, helping people move off the streets and into safe, secure housing. We take a person-centred, trauma-informed approach, building trust and supporting people to achieve long-term stability and independence. A home is the foundation for everything. Join SPEAR’s Housing First team in Wandsworth and help people who’ve experienced rough sleeping to secure and keep a safe, permanent place to live. At SPEAR, you’ll be part of a friendly, skilled charity team dedicated to ending homelessness. We offer comprehensive training, opportunities to progress, and strong wellbeing support—so you can thrive while helping others do the same. The Role In this crucial role, your focus will be on the service delivery of SPEAR’s Housing First model. You will work with staff and management teams to deliver this innovative model of housing society’s most vulnerable people, helping us drive forward a collective vision of inclusion and participation across the organisation. Housing First is a SPEAR service that provides independent tenancies with registered social landlords via the council nomination process and intensive personalised support to rough sleepers who have not progressed through any supported accommodation pathway. Our Values Everything we do is guided by our values. We're looking for people who are: Collaborative Aspirational Respectful Determined Visionary If these values resonate with you, we'd love to hear from you. About You You’ll bring experience of supporting people affected by homelessness or other complex challenges, plus the empathy, resilience and practical skills to make a lasting impact. You’ll know how to build rapport, plan support, and work collaboratively with housing and health services. You will build trusting relationships and provide flexible and one-to-one support. You will work in partnership with the London Borough of Wandsworth and local agencies to help people stay housed, improve their wellbeing and help them feel part of the community. You'll respond to changing priorities and manage situations as they arise, making sure services reach those who need them most. Your Benefits Generous holiday – 26 days plus public holidays, rising by up to five extra days with length of service Wellbeing & EAP – 24/7 Employee Assistance Programme with free counselling, money, and legal advice Health support – Occupational health service and free annual eye test (with contribution towards glasses if required) Cycle to Work – Save on a new bike and accessories through salary sacrifice Season ticket loan – Interest-free loan for annual travel passes Moving house day – Extra day’s leave when you move home Financial security – Life assurance (4x salary) and interest-free emergency staff loan Family-friendly policies – Enhanced maternity and adoption pay, plus flexible working options Career development – Ongoing training, learning, and progression opportunities Blue Light Card – Discounts across a wide range of shops, restaurants, and services At SPEAR, we welcome and encourage applications from everyone, regardless of age, disability, gender, ethnicity, religion and sexual orientation. We are facing diverse problems, so we need diverse people to tackle them. So, if you’re seeking your next challenge as a Housing First Worker, please apply . Medina Healthcare is unique, we are partnered with Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, which is one of the largest Community and Mental Health Trusts
items.desc: The closing date is 31st Dec 2026 Job summary Medina Healthcare are looking for a Salaried GP to join our ever expanding team. You will be part of a dynamic team responsible for providing sustainable, population-based health and social care, while ensuring our patients are seen in a timely manner by the most appropriate clinician within the Extended Primary Care Team. Medina Healthcare is unique, we are partnered with Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, which is one of the largest Community and Mental Health Trusts in the UK. Main duties, tasks & skills required Main Duties Of The Role: In general, the post-holder will be expected to undertake all the normal duties and responsibilities associated with a GP working within primary care including: Making professionally autonomous decisions in relation to presenting problems, Consults with patients in the surgery and during home visits or via telephone or on-line mechanisms. Undertakes triage calls, triage visits, checking and signing of repeat prescriptions, Screening patients for disease risk factors and early signs of illness In consultation with patients and in line with current Practice disease management protocols, develop care plans for health, Provide counselling and health education as necessary. Admits or discharges patients to and from caseload and refers them to other care providers internally and externally as appropriate, Complies with all relevant clinical governance and Practice policies and protocols. Assist in the establishment of appropriate systems to manage common chronic medical conditions, Record clear and contemporaneous consultation notes to agreed standards. Provide active input to the wider Primary healthcare team in the process of health needs research/base line data collection/clinical audit. Complies with and issues computer-generated acute and repeat prescriptions, prescribing in accordance with the Practice/Trust/ICB prescribing formulary, and meets professional learning and CPD requirements. About us Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust provides joined-up mental and physical healthcare for around two million people across our communities. With over 13,000 staff working in the community and local hospitals, we deliver care at every stage of life, helping people live their best and healthiest lives. Our mental health services include community-based support and early intervention in psychosis (EIP) for both adults and young people, alongside a network of specialist inpatient wards covering forensic, learning disability, eating disorder and older person's care. We deliver extensive physical health services too, from urgent community response teams helping frail and older patients remain safely at home, to hospitals at home teams providing acute-level care in familiar surroundings. Our neurological services offer rehabilitation and treatment for conditions including Multiple Sclerosis, Parkinson's Disease, Motor Neurone Disease, Head Injury, Cerebral Palsy and Stroke. Across Hampshire, our community hospitals provide inpatient rehabilitation as a step down from acute care, and our dedicated teams also staff Treetops Sexual Assault Referral Centre in Portsmouth, offering expert, compassionate support. Everything we do is underpinned by our CARE values of compassion, accountability, respect and excellence Job description Further information about the Trust and this role can be found on the Job Description and Person Specification document attached. The Trust will seek to resolve this issue wherever possible. We are happy to talk Flexible Working - all requests for flexible working options can be discussed as part of the interview process. items.desc: At Expedia Group, we help travelers explore the world, one journey at a time. As a global travel company powered by passionate people, trusted partnerships, and leading technology, we connect travelers, partners, and advertisers through our consumer brands, B2B network, and travel advertising business. Here, you'll do meaningful work that helps millions of people discover, book, and experience travel with more ease, confidence, and joy. Our five Behaviors-Traveler First, Think Big, Operate with Excellence, Ownership Mindset, and Succeed Together-help foster a supportive environment where people can grow their careers and have the flexibility, benefits, and support to do their best work. Join us and build for travelers everywhere. What you’ll do ICM platform configuration and solution delivery Translate incentive-plan requirements, terms and conditions, and business rules into effective ICM platform configurations. Own or contribute to functional design, configuration, testing, deployment, and post-release validation for new plans, plan changes, and enhancements. Document calculation logic, data flows, configuration decisions, dependencies, and operational procedures. Identify opportunities to use ICM platform capabilities, best practices, and approved AI tools to improve reliability, scalability, and user experience. Use AI-assisted approaches to accelerate requirements analysis, configuration drafting, reuse of proven patterns, identification of edge cases, and preparation of configuration documentation; validate all AI-generated outputs against approved requirements and controls. Data integrations and data quality Own or support data integrations into the ICM platform from HR, attainment, and other operational data sources. Monitor data loads and investigate failures, missing records, mapping issues, and data-quality exceptions. Partner with Analytics, Data/Engineering, and HR Operations to validate source data and reconcile discrepancies. Use SQL to inspect, validate, and troubleshoot data across multiple sources. Testing, release management, and controls Create and maintain test plans, test cases, test scripts, regression coverage, and release evidence. Use AI-supported QA to compare requirements with configurations, expand test coverage, identify inconsistencies, summarize test results, and highlight likely regression risks, with human review before release decisions. Validate plan calculations and downstream outputs when configurations change or defects are fixed. Apply disciplined change-management practices, including documentation, approvals, testing, and traceability through the team’s ticketing and backlog processes. Support SOX and audit requirements related to plan configuration, data connections, user access, and change management. Operational support and troubleshooting Support Incentive Operations during payout and accrual cycles, including investigation of calculation errors, data discrepancies, and system issues. Triage production problems, assess impact, coordinate resolution, and communicate status clearly to stakeholders. Work with the ICM platform vendor support team to diagnose critical errors, test fixes, and coordinate safe production rollouts. Use AI-assisted triage and analysis to summarize errors, identify patterns across incidents, develop root-cause hypotheses, and accelerate runbook updates. Help turn recurring incidents into permanent fixes, improved controls, or clearer operating procedures. Access, backlog, and stakeholder management Review and manage user access rights and support license provisioning in the ICM platform. Maintain a prioritized backlog of features, configuration changes, defects, technical debt, and control improvements. Estimate effort, identify dependencies, and communicate timelines and risks for delivery work. Build trusted relationships with technical and non-technical partners, explaining system behavior and trade-offs in a clear, practical way. What we’re looking for Required experience and skills Four or more years of hands-on programming, configuration, or technical administration in an Incentive Compensation Management (ICM) platform such as Captivate IQ, SAP Callidus Commissions, Varicent or comparable platforms. Practical experience configuring calculation logic, testing plan changes, troubleshooting defects, and supporting production releases. Strong SQL skills and experience integrating, validating, or reconciling data from multiple sources. Demonstrated ability to create structured test plans, test cases, test scripts, and regression coverage. Ability to translate business requirements and incentive-plan rules into robust technical solutions. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and investigative skills, with close attention to detail. Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to work effectively across Operations, Analytics, HR, Finance, IT, and vendor teams. items.desc: Job Introduction The National Autistic Society is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of all children and adults who use our services. Successful applicants will be required to complete the relevant safeguarding checks if relevant to their role. Join Us as a Data Support Officer The National Autistic Society helps create a world that works for autistic people and within National Programmes we champion the rights and interests of autistic people and their families, making sure national policies and legislation reflect their needs. We have a rewarding opportunity for a Data Support Officer within the Commercial Development and Support Team. If you share our values and want to make a difference, we’d love to hear from you. About the Team The National Programmes Data Team supports a range of fundraising, marketing and supporter engagement activities across the National Autistic Society. The team is responsible for maintaining the quality, accuracy and security of our CRM systems, supporting data administration processes and helping colleagues access reliable information to support decision making and excellent supporter experiences. About the Role As a Data Support Officer, you will support the administration of routine and scheduled tasks within the National Programmes Data Team. You will help maintain the accuracy and integrity of the National Autistic Society’s CRM database, support fundraising and supporter services activities, and play a key role in the migration from Raiser's Edge to Microsoft Dynamics. This is an excellent opportunity for someone with strong attention to detail and an interest in data management within the charity sector. What You’ll Do Run regular data imports and contact selections to support fundraising and marketing activities. Administer new data briefs and process files received from fundraising agencies. Support donation processing and fundraising administration tasks. Maintain and cleanse CRM records to ensure data quality and accuracy. What We’re Looking For Experience working in a data, supporter services or database administration environment. Experience using CRM systems such as Raiser's Edge or similar databases. Excellent communication, interpersonal and time management skills. Strong attention to detail, accuracy and problem-solving ability. Click here for the Job Description This advert is for a Full Time, fixed-term position at 35 hours per week, until 31/03/2027. This role is Hybrid, with a minimum of 1 day per week in the London Head Office. What we can offer you Pension – Auto-enrolled pension scheme. Annual Leave – 33 days (including public holidays). You can buy or sell leave each year. Training – Great induction and training, including autism training. Discounts – Online staff discount scheme for shopping, cycling, tech, and more (e.g., Asda, Tesco, Nike, Apple). Healthcare – Cash plan for permanent staff. Life Assurance – 2x your base salary. Flexible Benefits – Options like private health, dental insurance, holiday trading, enhanced pension. Support – 24-hour Employee Assistance Programme and counselling. Mindfulness – Free Headspace app for you and up to 3 family/friends. Blue Light Card – Eligibility for discounts. About our application process You will be required to upload your CV. If you are providing a supporting statement, please consider the following: Look at the job description and person specification. Tell us how your skills and experience match the role. Give examples if you can. We might close this job advert early if we get lots of suitable applications. To protect our autistic adults & children at the National Autistic Society, some roles require employees to have a criminal background check. Possession of an Enhanced DBS Check either on the Update Service or conducted within the last 12 months would be preferable but not essential if it's applicable to your role. Applications for this job are sought from anyone who is suitably qualified and experienced for the role but particularly welcome from autistic people. We are an equal opportunities employer and part of the Disability Confident Employer scheme. Important Information Agencies need not apply. Please note the National Autistic Society are unable to provide sponsorship for Visas. The National Autistic Society may use artificial intelligence (AI) to assist our recruitment team with reviewing applications for this role. All application decisions are made by people and are not determined automatically by AI.

items.desc: Starting Salary: £32,000 plus an annual bonus and Benefits Location: Birmingham Duration: 2 Years Closing date: 31st December 2026 - Please note, we may close this advert earlier than advertised if we receive a high volume of applications, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible Are you an ambitious final year undergraduate looking for a unique graduate programme? Imagine contributing to projects that help move millions of people every day? At Siemens Mobility, we're developing innovative transport solutions that are transforming the future of rail and making travel more sustainable. Start your career at the heart of that journey! Join a two-year graduate journey that combines hands-on experience with structured development. Through technical and professional training, graduate workshops, mentoring and leadership exposure, you'll build your skills while working on meaningful projects. You'll collaborate with fellow graduates across the business, present your achievements and deliver a Business Impact Project with real business value, developing the confidence, experience and connections needed to accelerate your career at Siemens Mobility. Siemens Rail Electrification powers electric trains, trams, and metros worldwide by designing, installing, and maintaining all the necessary equipment, like substations and overhead lines. Their work ensures these vehicles get the electricity they need to run safely and efficiently, supporting modern electric transport and helping to reduce its environmental impact. Year 1: Three 4 month rotations across key functions, starting off with 1 month in your home team. Year 2: Transition into your substantive team to develop deeper expertise and to prepare for your role beyond the graduate programme. Note - Some business areas may continue rotations into year 2. Job Purpose: The Protection and Control (P&C) Team within the Electrification Business Unit of Siemens Mobility, Rail Infrastructure are responsible for the development of cutting edge protection and control schemes and the implementation of digital substation solutions to allow the railways in Britain to be safer, greener and more cost effective! We are at the very cutting edge of electrical protection design and you will be working within a dynamic and driven team which delivers electrification on all major UK projects. During your 2-year graduate scheme, you will have the opportunity to gain experience in other teams within the Electrification business unit, previous examples of which have been high voltage design, overhead line design and protection system design. Depending on the placement, you may be working away from your contracted location for a period of up to six months (funded by Siemens). For the duration of the graduate scheme, you will take part in technical and professional training, with technical training delivered by the top engineers in the business over the course of several weeks. During these training weeks you will also have a chance to meet and challenge other early career professionals across Siemens Mobility and discuss different experiences, building connections for your burgeoning career. It is an exciting time to be joining the railway in the UK as new electrification projects are authorised and a new generation of protection and control systems for the electrification network are being developed. Siemens are at the forefront of these new technologies as a manufacturing business giving you the opportunity to learn from the subject experts. The work will include undertaking outline and detailed design of railway electrification systems, initially under the supervision of experienced engineers but rapidly taking on more responsibilities. These projects support the growth and transformation of the railway for a greener future, with typical clients being Network Rail, London Underground and Docklands Light Railway, to name a few. The work involves, site investigations, outline and detailed designs, commissioning support, and liaison with clients, stakeholders, suppliers and external third parties. Knowledge, Skills, Qualifications and Experience: The candidate would be expected to a have strong academic background in engineering, ideally in power distribution. Principal Accountabilities: Undertake all design calculations (from first principles if required) for assigned projects within the Rail Electrification portfolio. Undertake site surveys and produce site reports. Responsible for ensuring that all works are carried out safely. To support all design team members (e,g. Project Engineers, Design / Senior Design Engineers, Engineering and Design Managers etc.), as required, to ensure we deliver an integrated solution for the customer. To positively influence design and construction safety performance and aims for zero accidents (Siemens Zero Harm policy).  In CIS, we deliver Rail Infrastructure systems for customers across the UK and internationally.  Scripting & Automation: Strong programming skills in Python and Shell/Bash; familiarity with package/artifact management (e.g., Artifactory) and containerization (Docker).

 Schimbă lumea de mâine împreună cu noi. 
 Unitatea noastră de afaceri Siemens Motion Control (DI MC) este unul dintre liderii mondiali în furnizarea de produse, sisteme, soluții și servicii în domeniul controlului mișcării. Aceasta include aproximativ 20.000 de angajați și patru segmente de business. Cu locații globale de producție, cercetare și dezvoltare (R&D) și servicii, MC este aproape de clienții săi și activă într-o gamă largă de industrii. 
 În rețeaua noastră de fabrici, Siemens AG dezvoltă și produce motoare electrice pentru piața globală. Clienții noștri țintă activează în domeniul tehnologiei de automatizare, în industria auto și în domeniul intra-logisticii. Pentru a susține creșterea noastră de succes, vom extinde locațiile noastre într-un mod direcționat în următorii ani. Digitalizarea și simulările ne sprijină în planificarea viitorului și în implementare. 
 In prezent cautam noi colegi pe rolul de Failure Room Analysis Technician care sa se alature echipei de Calitate. Vei fi responsabil pentru investigarea și analiza produselor neconforme provenite din producție, reclamații clienți (RMA) sau audituri interne, în vederea identificării modurilor de defectare și a cauzelor rădăcină. Acesta oferă suport tehnic echipelor de Calitate, Producție și Inginerie pentru implementarea acțiunilor corective și preventive. 
 Responsabilități principale: 
 - Recepționează și înregistrează probele trimise pentru analiză. 
 - Efectuează inspecții vizuale, măsurători și teste funcționale asupra produselor neconforme. 
 - Realizează analize de defect folosind echipamente și metode specifice laboratorului. 
 - Identifică și clasifică modurile de defectare. 
 - Colectează și documentează dovezi tehnice (fotografii, măsurători, rapoarte de testare). 
 - Întocmește rapoarte de analiză și concluzii tehnice. 
 - Participă la investigații de tip 8D, 5 Why și Ishikawa. 
 - Colaborează cu departamentele de Calitate, Producție, Inginerie Proces și Logistică pentru identificarea cauzelor rădăcină. 
 - Menține trasabilitatea probelor și arhivarea documentației aferente. 
 - Respectă procedurile de siguranță, calitate și mediu aplicabile în laborator. 
 - Asigură ordinea și buna funcționare a echipamentelor din Failure Analysis Room. 
 Cerințe 
 - Studii medii tehnice sau studii superioare în domeniul tehnic 
 - Experiență în domeniul calității, producției sau analizelor tehnice constituie avantaj. 
 - Experiență în utilizarea echipamentelor de măsurare și testare. 
 Cunoștințe și competențe: 
 - Interpretarea desenelor tehnice și a specificațiilor produselor. 
 - Utilizarea instrumentelor de măsură (șubler, micrometru, comparatoare, multimetru etc.). 
 - Cunoștințe de bază privind metodologiile de rezolvare a problemelor (8D, 5 Why). 
 - Cunoștințe Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint). 
 - Atenție la detalii și gândire analitică. 
 - Abilități de comunicare și lucru în echipă. 
 - Cunoștințe de limba engleză la nivel tehnic. 
 Ce iti oferim: 
 Pe lângă oportunități de muncă atractive, punem un accent deosebit pe un echilibru sănătos între viața profesională și cea personală; învățarea continuă și dezvoltarea angajaților noștri sunt foarte importante pentru noi – credem că acestea sunt cheia succesului nostru.

 Diversitatea la Siemens este sursa noastră de creativitate și inovație. Existența unor tipuri diferite de talente și experiențe ne face mai orientați spre rezultate și mai bine pregătiți să răspundem eficient cerințelor societății. Prin urmare, apreciem candidații care reflectă diversitatea de care ne bucurăm în compania noastră.

items.desc: We're looking for an experienced Applied AI Engineer to join our Growth team and help build operations automation systems for our global mobility platform. If you're excited about applying machine learning to customer support, document verification, and fraud detection challenges across Bolt's 200M+ customers, you'll find plenty of impactful work here. About Us With over 200 million customers across 50+ countries and 850+ cities, Bolt is one of the fastest-growing tech companies in Europe and Africa — powered by 4.5+ million partners on our platform, 4,000+ employees globally. And it's all thanks to our people. We believe in creating an inclusive environment where everyone is welcome, regardless of race, colour, religion, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, age, or ability. Our ultimate goal is to make cities for people, not cars — and we need your help on this mission! About The Role Every new customer and order at Bolt can trigger an operational decision: a refund, a document check, an account review, a ruling in a dispute. Our teams already use AI on top of existing processes to make them faster and more accurate. Many of those processes need a redesign from the ground up, and a design that gets better with every decision it makes. You start with customer support for all users, then move to document verification & fraud detection. After that, any process with high decision volume and a recorded outcome is in scope. You are hands-on. You ship the product and own the result. Main Tasks And Responsibilities Redesign processes. Mine an area's systems of record, interview the people who run it, and decide which steps become software, agents or human checkpoints. Define what great looks like. Turn real cases and human decisions into test sets, and turn every new failure into a regression test. Build checks that are hard to game. Calibrate LLM judges against human labels, keep them apart from programmatic checks, and guard cost and payouts. Run the improvement loop across policies, prompts, tools and models. Add fine-tuning where a better policy is not enough. Own the rollout gates. Decide what ships, run the A/B test, and feed the live result back into the test sets. Codify what works so other teams can run it without you. You are measured on how many decisions you automate while raising their quality. About You You come from software engineering, ML or data science, and you have shipped and operated a system that calls LLMs. You have built an evaluation suite for an LLM or agent system and used it to decide what ships. You have spent dozens of hours in agent traces finding where decisions went wrong, and fixed them. You have designed an LLM judge, measured its agreement with human labels, and fixed it when the two disagreed. You know how verifiers get gamed, and have caught a case of reward hacking in your work. You can design an A/B test, read its result, and explain to an operations lead why the offline tests predicted something different. You know when a rule, a classic ML model or a human beats an LLM, and you can show the cost trade-off. You write clearly in English. Your reports pair a ceiling estimate with a realistic one. Nice To Have Hands-on post-training: RLVR, GRPO or DPO, reward modelling, LoRA etc. Program optimisation frameworks such as GEPA, DSPy or TextGrad. RL environment or gym design with programmatic grading. Operations automation at a marketplace, fintech or trust and safety team. Strong SQL, and comfort working in codebases you did not write. This role is not for you if you want to train frontier models, need a finished spec before you start, or prefer benchmark scores to live results. Why you'll love it here Accelerate your professional growth with unique career opportunities. Enjoy a rewarding salary and stock options, knowing that as Bolt succeeds, so do you. Take care of your physical and mental health with our wellness perks. Celebrate 5 years at Bolt with a 1-month paid sabbatical to recharge. Connect with colleagues at annual company events and smaller team gatherings. Work on-site at our Tallinn HQ, next to the operations and engineering teams whose decisions you automate. Some perks may differ depending on your location and role. At Bolt, using AI daily is a baseline expectation for everyone. If there's a faster, smarter way to do your work, we expect you to find it. You're still responsible for the output, so the standard stays high when using AI tools. Experience is great, but what we really look for is drive, intelligence, and integrity. So even if you don't tick every box, please consider applying! Everyone is welcome Bolt is an equal opportunity employer. items.desc: As we partner with a diverse array of Danish companies operating on a global scale, we navigate industries that must adhere to stringent laws and financial controls, all while delivering exceptional service levels. With over 1,500 dedicated colleagues across Denmark, The Czech Republic, and The Philippines, Aeven is not just a workplace — it's a community united by a common goal: to drive innovation and operational excellence. In Denmark, we boast four state-of-the-art data center facilities, allowing us to leverage advanced technologies and provide robust solutions tailored to our clients' needs. If you’re looking to make an impact in a dynamic environment that values expertise and collaboration, we invite you to explore joining our team at Aeven! About The Role Aeven is currently building a controlled AI platform: a gateway for models and tools, reference RAG and MCP patterns others can reuse, and an organization that builds on that foundation. In this role you will own that technical path from first production platform work to enablement at scale. You will also function as the technical lead for the Aeven AI Gateway and for the first reference RAG pipelines and MCP integrations. You will build and harden shared platform capabilities, then shift toward enabling other teams to adopt them. Production day-to-day operations for the gateway will be run with skilled-up colleagues in the wider organization; you design for that handoff. We offer ownership of a company-wide AI control plane; path from builder to technical enabler, and exposure to on-prem and cloud LLM stacks. Responsibilities: Own the technical direction and delivery of the AI Gateway, including routing, keys and budgets, guardrails, auditability, and OpenAI-compatible upstreams such as on-premises models. Design and ship the first reference RAG pipelines, covering ingestion, retrieval, access-control-aware patterns, and basic evaluation. Deliver the first MCP and tool integrations as reusable patterns rather than one off applications. Partner with Security and platform and network teams on identity, data classification, and production readiness. Write clear runbooks and interfaces so gateway operations can be owned by upskilled teams across the organization rather than requiring a 24/7 CoE pager role. After the first gold paths are established, prioritize enablement through templates, review gates, office hours, and pairing with line-of-business engineers. Challenge “build it for us” requests; default to platform capabilities and reusable patterns unless the Head of AI sponsors a time-boxed proof of concept, typically four to six weeks. Contribute estimates and technical options to the CoE backlog maintained with the AI Operating Lead. Requirements: You care about production systems and operator impact. You ship scalable building blocks and teach others to use them. Must-Have Qualifications: At least five years of software engineering experience with production ownership. Strong Python and/or TypeScript skills, including APIs and system integration. Hands-on LLM application experience, including tool calling, orchestration, and an evaluation mindset. Knowledge of RAG patterns, including chunking, embeddings, vector stores, grounding, and access-control awareness. Experience with API gateways, reverse proxies, or LLM gateways such as LiteLLM or an equivalent platform. Cloud literacy, preferably with Azure, and confidence working with Linux and containers. Clear written and spoken English for design documentation and stakeholder collaboration. Evidence of mentoring or enabling other engineers through reviews, templates, guilds, or pairing. Good-to-Have Qualifications Experience with MCP or a similar tool protocol. Knowledge of Entra ID and enterprise authentication. Experience with observability, including metrics, tracing, and token and cost visibility. Familiarity with Kubernetes or hybrid on-premises GPU inference. Experience in regulated industries such as finance, life sciences, or the public sector. Experience with vector databases or pgvector-style stores and document pipelines over enterprise knowledge bases. items.desc: Permanent position at Twoday | Copenhagen AI Engineer – LLMs and On-Premise AI Do you have hands-on experience building reliable LLM solutions and deploying models in controlled environments? We are looking for an AI Engineer to join Twoday and work on an important digital solution for a Danish public-sector organisation in Aarhus. Your role You will work across the development and operation of LLM-based solutions, with a particular focus on models running on-premise. You will help turn AI concepts into secure, stable and production-ready services. Your responsibilities will include: Developing and integrating LLM-based applications and agents Deploying and operating LLM models in on-premise environments Building RAG solutions, structured workflows and validation layers Improving model reliability through guardrails, testing and monitoring Integrating AI services with existing applications and APIs Working with sensitive data and high requirements for security and traceability What we are looking for Practical experience developing production-ready LLM solutions Strong Python skills and experience with relevant LLM frameworks Experience with RAG, prompt design, tool calling and structured outputs Knowledge of local or self-hosted models and inference infrastructure Experience with Docker, Linux, APIs and CI/CD A pragmatic approach to hallucination reduction, validation and monitoring Fluent Danish and English, both spoken and written Ability to work full time onsite in Aarhus Experience with model fine-tuning, GPU infrastructure, NLP or regulated environments is an advantage. What We Offer You will be permanently employed by Twoday and become part of a strong professional environment within AI and software engineering. Your first assignment will be based onsite with our customer in Aarhus, where you will work closely with both technical specialists and business stakeholders. At Twoday, you will have the opportunity to develop your expertise, share knowledge with experienced colleagues and help create responsible AI solutions that make a real difference. Working at Twoday Twoday is a leading technology consulting company specializing in applied AI and advanced engineering. With around 2,300 experts in AI, data, digital engineering, and cloud engineering, we cut through complexity, remove uncertainty, and prove the value of technology. Our purpose is to create a better tomorrow through AI and technology. We strengthen private and public organizations across energy and utilities, financial services and insurance, industrials and manufacturing, health and life sciences, and government. However, our greatest strength isn't the technology we work with. It's the people behind it. Every day, they bring together expertise, curiosity, and determination to help our customers solve complex challenges and create lasting value. Diversity and inclusion We are committed to building an inclusive and diverse workplace where everyone is treated with respect and has equal opportunities. Our recruitment decisions are based on competencies, experience, and individual merit. Don’t meet all the requirements? Many candidates hesitate to apply unless they meet every qualification. We are looking for people who are engaged, meet most of the criteria, and are motivated to grow in the role. If this role interests you and you believe you could be a good fit, we encourage you to apply.

items.desc: Il nostro cliente : Azienda edile consolidata, attiva nella ristrutturazione, nella manutenzione e nella riqualificazione energetica di edifici residenziali e commerciali. Opera su commesse private e, in parte, su gare pubbliche, con un approccio tecnico e orientato alla qualità dell'esecuzione. Ruolo Ingegnere informatico con esperienza AI, punto di riferimento per progettare e mettere in produzione soluzioni concrete a supporto dell'ufficio tecnico, commerciale e di commessa: dal computo e dal preventivo all'analisi documentale, fino a strumenti GenAI utilizzabili da profili non tecnici. Responsabilità Mappare i processi aziendali (preventivi, capitolati, computi, schede impianto, SAL, assistenza) e individuare use case AI ad alto impatto Sviluppare e integrare soluzioni di machine learning e generative AI su dati tecnici e documentali (offerte, computi, schede prodotto, layout copertura, anagrafiche commessa) Costruire assistenti e workflow su LLM (RAG su documentale interno, draft di preventivi/relazioni, classificazione richieste, supporto all'ufficio tecnico) Collaborare con geometri, preventivisti, commerciali e responsabile di produzione per tradurre esigenze di cantiere e di commessa in strumenti usabili Integrare i modelli con gli applicativi già in uso (gestionale, Excel, cartelle di progetto, eventualmente CRM/ERP) tramite API e automazioni Portare le soluzioni dal prototipo all'uso quotidiano: qualità, tempi di risposta, costi, manutenzione e formazione degli utenti Definire regole minime di qualità dato, privacy e tracciabilità, coerenti con un'impresa edile (commesse, fornitori, clienti) Monitorare adozione ed effetti sul lavoro (tempi di offerta, errori di computo, recupero documentale) Requirements Laurea in Ingegneria Informatica, Informatica o discipline STEM affini Esperienza di almeno 4-6 anni in sviluppo software, di cui almeno 3 su progetti AI/ML o GenAI usati in produzione Ottima padronanza di Python e stack AI di mercato (PyTorch e/o TensorFlow, Hugging Face, Scikit-learn, FastAPI) Esperienza concreta su LLM: RAG su documentale aziendale, prompting, integrazione via API, valutazione della qualità delle risposte Capacità di lavorare su dati "reali" di PMI (file disomogenei, Excel, PDF, disegni, anagrafiche), non solo su dataset di laboratorio Conoscenza di cloud (Azure, AWS o GCP), Docker e integrazioni verso gestionali/ERP Interesse o prima esposizione al mondo edile, impiantistico o energetico (fotovoltaico, computi, capitolati) è un plus decisivo Disponibilità a operare da Pavia, a contatto con ufficio tecnico e commessa; italiano fluente, inglese tecnico Plus: dimestichezza con computi/prezzari, lettura di elaborati CAD, dati di producibilità FV, Power BI o automazioni (n8n/Power Automate). Caratteristiche personali Profilo concreto, poco accademico: sa spiegare l'AI a un capo commessa o a un preventivista e misura il valore in giorni-uomo e qualità dell'offerta, non in paper. È autonomo in una realtà di medio-piccole dimensioni, dove non esiste un team data science strutturato . Curioso verso il mestiere (coperture, tetti, impianti FV), paziente con dati imperfetti, orientato al rilascio di strumenti usabili. Precisione, senso pratico e capacità di stare in squadra con profili tecnici non informatici sono essenziali. Benefits Retribuzione: RAL 50.000-55.000 €, commisurata a esperienza e autonomia.. Contratto a tempo indeterminato, CCNL Edile.

items.desc: Accueil » SYNCHRONIC – Ingénieur IA/Big Data (H/F) SYNCHRONIC – Ingénieur IA/Big Data (H/F) (Franqueville-Saint-Pierre (76), France) A propos de Synchronic SYNCHRONIC, fabricant de solutions de sécurité électronique depuis plus de 30 ans, est une PME reconnue dans son domaine d’activités auprès de ces clients banquiers, industriels et étatiques notamment. Depuis 2020, la société a rejoint CASTEL et le pôle tertiaire du groupe URMET, et fait face à une forte augmentation de son activité. Afin de se structurer, de répondre à l’attente de nos clients et à une activité croissante, nous recrutons un Ingénieur IA/Big Data (H/F). Quelles sont les missions ? Dans Un Pôle De Compétences à Forte Valeurs Ajoutées Au Sein D’un Bureau D’études Pluridisciplinaires De Plus De 20 Développeurs Et Sous La Responsabilité Du Directeur Technique, Vous Êtes Garant(e) Des Outils Nécessaires Au Traitement Des Données Massives Et De La Bonne Intégration De L’Intelligence Artificielle Au Développement Des Solutions De Sûreté Synchronic. Vous Mettez Votre Expertise à Disposition De Nos Équipes Et Vos Missions Sont Les Suivantes Analyser et développer une solution permettant le traitement de volumes importants de nos données en garantissant leur sécurité Concevoir et développer des algorithmes d’IA et d’apprentissage automatique Préconiser l’architecture technique nécessaire aux traitements des algorithmes conçus Collaborer avec les équipes interdisciplinaires pour intégrer des IA dans nos solutions Evaluer et améliorer les performances des modèles d’IA Anticiper les évolutions dans les données et préparer l’architecture de nos solutions à y répondre techniquement Intégrer la sobriété numérique dans la gestion des données en adoptant des pratiques responsables comme l’optimisation de l’infrastructure de stockage et de la puissance de calcul pour réduire la consommation d’énergie, ou la sélection de technologies moins énergivores Participer au respect des normes applicables au sein de l’entreprise dans son périmètre (qualité, sécurité de l’information…), et notamment la norme ISO9001 Assurer une veille technologique pour rester à jour sur les dernières avancées La liste de ces missions est non exhaustive et est susceptible d’évoluer en fonction des besoins du service, de votre polyvalence et de vos compétences en lien avec l’activité. Quel profil recherchons-nous ? Passionné(e) d’informatique, vous êtes dynamique, motivé(e), et avez le sens du travail d’équipe. Votre sens du service, votre rigueur et votre aisance relationnelle associés à votre esprit de méthode, vos qualités rédactionnelles et votre sens de l’innovation vous permettront d’accomplir vos missions avec succès. Aircall’s AI Voice Agent automates routine calls, AI Assist streamlines post-call work, and AI Assist Pro delivers real-time guidance so people can do their best work. The result is higher revenue, faster resolutions, and teams that scale with confidence. Aircall is headquartered in Paris, our European HQ, with a strong North American presence anchored in Seattle, our North American HQ, and teams across Madrid, London, Berlin, San Francisco, New York City, Sydney, and Mexico City. We’ve built a product customers love and a business that’s scaling quickly, backed by world-class investors and driven by rapid AI innovation across multiple product lines. At Aircall, you’ll join a company in motion. We’re ambitious, product-driven, and execution-focused, with visible impact, fast decisions, and real growth. How we work at Aircall : We’re customer-obsessed, data-driven, and focused on delivering meaningful outcomes. We value ownership, continuous learning, and thoughtful speed. If you thrive in a collaborative, fast-moving environment where trust and impact matter, you’ll feel at home here. About The Team Aircall’s Forward Deployed Engineering team connects our innovative AI Agents technology to real-world SMB workflows. We turn possibility into production — delivering automation that improves customer experience, boosts productivity, and unlocks new business value. Working cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Sales, Solutions, and Customer Success, the team ensures every deployment delivers measurable impact. This is a dynamic, hands-on role at the intersection of technical consulting , project leadership , and AI adoption strategy . You don’t need to be a full-time software engineer, but you should be fluent in APIs, very confident managing technical projects, and eager to continuously learn, build, and scale new models that empower both customers and teammates. About The Role As a Forward-Deployed Engineer, you’ll own the end-to-end delivery of technically sound, low-code AI solutions for Aircall customers. You’ll design, implement, and operationalize workflows that connect the AI Agent with CRMs, help desks, and communication tools. You’ll also play a key role in driving team upskilling , building reusable frameworks , and leading cross-functional initiatives that improve how Aircall deploys AI at scale. This is a hands-on role where you’ll translate customer challenges into scalable technical solutions, working directly with Product and Engineering to refine Aircall’s platform and accelerate adoption. Please note, this is not a software engineering role. This is a hybrid, revenue driving role across Solutions Engineering, Software Engineering, Consulting, Professional Services, and Product Ownership What You'll Do Lead customer discovery and design sessions to map business processes, identify automation opportunities, and define solution architecture. Design, build, and deploy integrations using low/no-code platforms (Zapier, Make, n8n, Workato) and CRM automation tools (HubSpot Workflows, Salesforce Flow) with API connectors. Collaborate with Engineering to validate technical feasibility, resolve blockers, and share field learnings that inform product improvements. Configure and optimize the AI Agent — defining intents, prompts, actions, guardrails, and performance metrics. Manage complex, cross-functional deployments — defining timelines, aligning stakeholders, ensuring accountability, and delivering on time and within scope. Create scalable models and reusable frameworks (templates, playbooks, reference architectures) that make future projects faster and more consistent. Champion continuous learning and enablement — train peers, run internal workshops, and document best practices to raise the technical bar across the team. Run global, targeted outbound campaigns within the existing customer base to generate pipeline and accelerate adoption, working closely with the customer marketing team. Collaborate with GTM leadership to embed routines and cadences that drive accountability for new product pipeline, forecast accuracy, and performance tracking. Own regional top-line targets for assigned products (e.g., AI Voice Agent MRR generated per area) by collaborating with AEs and AMs who hold add-on quotas. Act as an internal product owner within the GTM function—defining product-specific MRR strategies, coordinating cross-functional support, and ensuring Aircall delivers the leading AI-enabled communication platform. items.desc: Do you like being ahead of the curve? Do you want to work on developing software for new, market-leading technology? As a Software Developer at Robin Radar, you will do just that! The ideal candidate will have the opportunity to directly work on our software development and will be able to build, adapt, and modify the software of our radar products. To put it in simple terms, you will develop mind-blowing radar tech! Your work will be crucial, as equipping our radars with the best performing software also creates a better functioning product for our customers and increases safety, too. Not only that, but you would be part of an amazing, growing, and agile R&D Software Development Team, reporting to a team lead who is there to support and guide you every step of the way. Responsibilities Design, build, and maintain efficient, reusable, and reliable C++ code with a special focus on complex algorithms. Identify bottlenecks and bugs, and devise solutions to these problems. Help maintain code quality, organization, and automatization. Working with other departments on technical issues including software system design and maintenance. Analyzing information to recommend and plan the installation of new systems or modifications of an existing system. Consulting with engineering staff to evaluate software hardware interfaces and develop specifications and performance requirements. Give direction to software programming and documentation development. Requirements MSc degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field. Minimum of 5 years' experience as a C++ software developer with current knowledge of (advanced) C++ 17/20 standards. Extensive experience developing and deploying software on Linux, with a strong grasp of multithreaded code and real-time environments. Proficiency in Qt and experience with complex algorithms (e.g., image processing or tracking) with real-time performance. Knowledge of PostgreSQL databases, JSON, and XML. Familiarity with low-level hardware interactions and unit testing using GoogleTest. Experience with Bitbucket (or similar), Jira, Qt Creator and CI/CD (Jenkins). Solid understanding of the SDLC and experience in Agile/Scrum environments. Excellent communication in English (Dutch proficiency is a plus). Nice to have Experience with radar systems or a similar industry. Experience with embedded systems design. N.B. All applicants, we realize that this is quite the list and people come with various levels of experience. Don't be afraid to apply even if you feel you don't meet every desired skill. Our mission is a journey and there's plenty to learn on the way! But of course, you should identify with our core values: We trust, We own it & We aim high. Please note: We will request a Certificate of Conduct (VOG) and conduct a background check according to our screening policy. We appreciate your understanding and cooperation in this matter. What's In For You Working for a Great Place to Work® certified company. Comprehensive pension plan. Commuting allowance: our teams work hybrid. 30 days of paid holiday leave (with the possibility to buy 3 additional days). Opportunities to develop your skills even further through training and certifications. High quality laptop/desktop, monitor, headphones, and any other equipment necessary for your role. An international team of 30+ nationalities, full of high performance colleagues you can exchange experiences with and learn from. As well as having a lot of fun in our social events and Friday drinks! Our hiring process First interview: An introductory conversation with our Head of Software and one of the Team Leads to discuss your background, experience and mutual cultural fit. Coding challenge: A practical take-home C++ assignment designed to let you showcase your technical skills on your own time. Final interview: A technical deep-dive with 2 other team members to review your solution. Robin is a technology leader in tracking and classification of small objects. Our mission is to increase the safety of people and wildlife by preventing bird strikes in aviation, reducing the environmental impact of wind farms, and protecting humans and critical infrastructure against drones. We achieve this by combining purpose-built radars with unique software algorithms. This powerful combination allows us to provide actionable information that empowers users to prevent serious incidents. We’re growing. Fast. In fact, we are one of the top 10 fastest‑growing companies in the Netherlands. But despite this growth, we stay true to our core values of trust, ownership and aiming high. At Robin, you don’t join just a team. You join a collective of bright minds driven by the belief that ‘doing things better’ is a continuous challenge. Want to work on next-level radar tech, solve real problems, and never have to pretend your job has meaning? You’ll fit right in, we’re saving you a seat.

items.desc: About The Job You're Considering We’re looking for curious, driven graduates who are excited to kick-start their career in tech and make a real impact from day one. You’ll become part of a high-performing team delivering solutions for one of the UK’s largest public sector organisations - giving you the chance to work on meaningful projects that truly matter. Along the way, you’ll learn from experienced professionals, build in-demand technical skills, and gain hands-on experience with cutting-edge technologies. At Capgemini, we are helping shape a new age of intelligence, partnering with clients across industries to harness AI, technology, and human potential to drive meaningful change. As part of this journey, you’ll join one of our specialist tracks aligned to your interests: Data Engineer: turn data into powerful insights, working with modern analytics tools and cloud platforms to drive smarter, data-led decisions. Software Engineer: bring ideas to life by building scalable, user-focused applications using modern frameworks and full-stack technologies. Platform Engineer: develop and maintain secure, scalable cloud platforms and infrastructure using modern DevOps practices and platform technologies. This is more than just your first job - it’s a chance to grow, innovate, and shape the future of digital solutions, all while accelerating your career in a supportive and dynamic environment. At Capgemini, we are helping shape a new age of intelligence, partnering with clients across industries to harness AI, technology, and human potential to drive meaningful change. If you are successfully offered this position, you will go through a series of pre-employment checks, including: Identity, nationality (single or dual) or immigration status, employment history going back 3 continuous years, and unspent criminal record check (known as Disclosure and Barring Service) This role is based in either Telford or Hove, and you’ll typically be in the office up to 3 days a week, so you’ll need to be within commuting distance of your chosen location. The nature of this role requires you to work on a secure site, if this isn't a suitable location for you, we encourage you to explore our other graduate opportunities with Capgemini, which are available at various locations across the UK. Please also note that the Software Engineer and Platform Engineer pathways are only available at our Telford office, and the Data Engineer pathway is only available at our Hove office. What you will bring To be eligible for this programme, you must have obtained, or be studying towards, a minimum 2:2 degree. If you are currently studying, you must have completed your degree prior to proposed start date. We recognise that mitigating circumstances can have an impact on academic performance. If you have experienced any circumstances that you would like us to take into consideration, please provide details in your application. Additional criteria for each track can be found below. items.card: In this role, you will be responsible for authoring comprehensive Statistical Analysis Plans and executing regulatory-grade programming necessary for Analytical and Clinical Validation. You will work remotely, collaborating with cross-functional teams to ensure compliance with FDA and EMA standards. If you have a passion for applying statistical methods to enhance healthcare technologies, we encourage you to apply.
items.desc: We are seeking a detail-oriented Statistical Programmer to join our team focused on the statistical validation of Digital Health Technologies. In this role, you will be responsible for authoring comprehensive Statistical Analysis Plans and executing regulatory-grade programming necessary for Analytical and Clinical Validation. You will work remotely, collaborating with cross-functional teams to ensure compliance with FDA and EMA standards. If you have a passion for applying statistical methods to enhance healthcare technologies, we encourage you to apply. Your tasks Designing Statistical Analysis Plans for Clinical Validation to assess the Digital Health Technologies' capability in measuring clinically meaningful concepts using appropriate statistical models Selecting and documenting suitable statistical methods and success criteria to meet FDA and EMA validation requirements Writing clean, modular, and well-documented code in Python (or R) to generate necessary datasets and statistical outputs for regulatory submission Implementing software development best practices, including version control and automated testing, to ensure high-quality statistical programming outputs Ensuring compliance with regulatory standards, including 21 CFR Part 11 and Good Clinical Practice (GCP), throughout the statistical validation process Mapping raw and processed DHT data into CDISC-compliant data structures to facilitate efficient FDA review Compiling and structuring statistical reports and validation documentation for regulatory submissions, ensuring audit readiness Requirements Master's or Ph.D. in Biostatistics, Statistics, Data Science, or a related quantitative field Minimum 6 years of experience in statistical programming or data science within the pharmaceutical, medical device, or CRO sectors, with a focus on clinical trial statistics and SAP authoring Advanced proficiency in Python for statistical programming, with a strong understanding of best practices in software development, such as Git and unit testing Expertise in validation statistics and methods for assessing measurement agreement, including Bland-Altman analysis and mixed-effects models Experience preparing statistical evidence for regulatory bodies such as the FDA and EMA, particularly in the context of clinical assessments Advanced level of English Poland as a current place of living Job no. JOB-WP33K Sii ensures that all hiring decisions are made solely on the basis of qualifications and competence. We are committed to equal and fair treatment of all, regardless of legally protected characteristics. At Sii, we promote a diverse and inclusive work environment, in full compliance with applicable anti-discrimination laws. items.card: In this role, you will explore the physics behind the printing process and develop solutions that directly contribute to future products and applications. This is a highly multidisciplinary role where scientific insight is translated
items.desc: About This Vacancy Are you fascinated by the science behind advanced technology? Do you enjoy combining experimentation, data analysis, and physical modelling to solve complex engineering challenges? If so, this could be the perfect opportunity for you. We are looking for a Print Process Developer to join an innovative R&D team developing the next generation of industrial inkjet printing technology. In this role, you will explore the physics behind the printing process and develop solutions that directly contribute to future products and applications. From ink behavior and droplet formation to media interaction and drying processes, you will investigate the fundamental mechanisms that determine print quality and system performance. This is a highly multidisciplinary role where scientific insight is translated into technology that works in real-world printing systems. As a Print Process Developer, you will work on complex technical challenges at the intersection of physics, chemistry, and engineering. Your Responsibilities Will Include Investigating printing phenomena through experiments, measurements, data analysis, and physical modelling. Developing and optimizing print processes involving inks, printheads, media, drying, fixation, and image processing. Translating print-quality challenges and application requirements into physical questions and technical solutions. Designing and executing experiments using laboratory setups and industrial printing systems. Building, validating, and refining physical models to explain and predict process behavior. Analyzing complex datasets and using insights to improve print performance. Collaborating with specialists from multiple disciplines to understand process interactions and trade-offs. Converting scientific knowledge into robust, scalable solutions for future products and applications. You will be part of a multidisciplinary R&D organization where innovation is driven by collaboration. Working alongside physicists, chemists, engineers, software developers, and technology specialists, you will tackle challenges ranging from: Fluid dynamics Droplet generation and jetting behavior Ink-media interactions Drying and fixation processes Print quality optimization Process modelling and validation The unique aspect of this role is that you will not only develop theories and models but also test them directly on experimental setups and real industrial printing systems. What We Expect From You We are looking for a curious and analytical professional who enjoys understanding how complex systems work and translating scientific knowledge into practical solutions. Qualifications BSc, MSc or PhD in Physics, Applied Physics or Chemistry with a strong interest in material science Strong understanding of physical principles and engineering fundamentals. Hands-on experience or affinity with experimental research and measurement techniques. Ability to describe physical behavior through calculations, models, and data analysis. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. A structured approach to investigating and testing hypotheses. Interest in bridging the gap between scientific research and product development. Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively within multidisciplinary teams. Fluent in spoken and written English. What You Can Expect From Us The opportunity to work on cutting-edge inkjet technology within a highly innovative R&D environment. Challenging technical projects that combine physics, experimentation, modelling, and engineering. Collaboration with experienced specialists across multiple disciplines. A culture that encourages curiosity, innovation, and continuous learning. The chance to see your ideas evolve from scientific concepts into technologies used in real-world products. Excellent opportunities for personal and professional development.

items.desc: Over deze vacature Bij TNO zetten we de nieuwste wetenschappelijke inzichten om in innovatieve technologische oplossingen en toepassingen. We ontwerpen en bouwen systemen die gebruikmaken van kwantumeigenschappen en slaan daarmee de brug tussen fundamenteel onderzoek en praktische toepassingen via testfaciliteiten, demonstratoren en productontwikkeling. Voor quantumsensing op basis van Rydberg-atomen bouwen we onze expertise verder op. Jij krijgt daarin een specialistische rol. Je ontwikkelt niet alleen de technologie, maar helpt ook de experimentele infrastructuur opzetten die nodig is om ideeën daadwerkelijk te kunnen bouwen en testen. Daarbij kijk je verder dan het experiment alleen. Je onderzoekt samen met collega's, klanten en partners waar deze technologie kan worden toegepast en helpt de mogelijkheden van Rydberg-quantumsensing zichtbaar en concreet te maken. Wat ga je doen? Je gaat aan de slag binnen de afdeling Quantum Technology van TNO. Hier werk je aan projecten voor klanten én in nauwe samenwerking met partners binnen het Nederlandse en Europese kwantumecosysteem. In deze functie werk je aan het opbouwen van onze kennis en experimentele mogelijkheden rond quantumsensoren op basis van Rydberg-atomen. Je vertaalt wetenschappelijke kennis en concepten naar experimentele ontwerpen en bouwt de opstellingen waarmee we deze in de praktijk kunnen onderzoeken en demonstreren. Dat betekent dat je zelf oplossingen moet ontwerpen en uitwerken. Je bouwt en test experimentele opstellingen en werkt daarbij met optische systemen, elektronica en software. Je draagt bij aan de ontwikkeling van operationele concepten en proof-of-conceptdemonstraties en laat zien hoe de onderliggende meetprincipes in de praktijk kunnen werken. Tegelijk help je het expertisegebied verder te ontwikkelen. Je zoekt actief de verbinding met mogelijke toepassingen en externe partijen en denkt mee over waar deze technologie toegevoegde waarde kan hebben. Je kunt complexe wetenschap begrijpelijk maken voor anderen en krijgt de ruimte om initiatief te nemen in de ontwikkeling van dit nieuwe werkgebied. Zo draag je eraan bij dat nieuwe quantumsensortechnologie niet in het lab blijft, maar wordt vertaald naar toepassingen die relevant zijn voor klanten en uiteindelijk bijdragen aan de veiligheid van Nederland. Wat wij van jou verwachten We zoeken een specialist die graag iets nieuws opbouwt. Je combineert wetenschappelijke diepgang met een praktische instelling. Je vindt het interessant om vanuit een idee of wetenschappelijk concept zelf de stap naar een werkende experimentele opstelling te maken. Je werkt zelfstandig, maar zoekt actief de samenwerking met collega's en externe partijen. Je neemt initiatief, brengt je eigen inhoudelijke perspectief in en kunt tegelijkertijd voortbouwen op de expertise van anderen. Ook vind je het interessant om verder te kijken dan de technologie zelf en mee te denken over nieuwe toepassingen en samenwerkingen. Wat je meebrengt Een master- of promotiediploma (PhD) in Experimentele Natuurkunde, Engineering of een vergelijkbaar vakgebied. Praktische ervaring met het ontwerpen, bouwen en testen van kwantuminstrumentatie, bij voorkeur op basis van Rydberg-atomen. Ervaring met optische systemen en elektronica. Sterke programmeervaardigheden, met name in Python. Het vermogen om wetenschappelijke kennis te vertalen naar experimentele ontwerpen en werkende opstellingen. Initiatief en ondernemerschap om een nieuw expertisegebied verder te helpen ontwikkelen. Het vermogen om verbinding te leggen tussen technologie, mogelijke toepassingen en externe partijen. Goede communicatieve vaardigheden in het Engels. Een zelfstandige en samenwerkingsgerichte manier van werken. Wat wij jou bieden Uitdagend én afwisselend werk met serieuze impact. En volop kansen, want bij TNO heb je grotendeels zelf de regie over je carrière. Naast een bruto (fulltime) maandsalaris tussen € 3500,- en € 5500,- (afhankelijk van je kennis en ervaring), vakantiegeld (8%), een 13de maand (8,33%) en een flexbudget (5,58% + € 180), krijg je alle mogelijkheden om jezelf te ontwikkelen. Daarnaast kun je bij TNO een ‘menu’ aan arbeidsvoorwaarden samenstellen dat bij jouw persoonlijke situatie past. items.desc: About This Position At TNO, we turn the latest scientific insights into innovative technological solutions and applications. We design and build systems that harness quantum properties, bridging the gap between fundamental research and practical applications through test facilities, demonstrators and product development. We are further developing our expertise in quantum sensing based on Rydberg atoms. You will have a specialist role in this field. You will not only develop the technology itself, but also help build the experimental infrastructure needed to turn ideas into systems that can actually be built and tested. Your perspective extends beyond the experiment itself. Together with colleagues, clients and partners, you explore where this technology can be applied and help make the potential of Rydberg quantum sensing tangible and concrete. What will be your role? You will join TNO's Quantum Technology department, working on projects for clients and in close collaboration with partners across the Dutch and European quantum ecosystem. In this role, you will help build our knowledge and experimental capabilities in quantum sensors based on Rydberg atoms. You translate scientific knowledge and concepts into experimental designs and build the setups needed to investigate and demonstrate them in practice. This means developing and working out solutions yourself. You build and test experimental setups using optical systems, electronics and software. You contribute to the development of operational concepts and proof-of-concept demonstrations, showing how the underlying measurement principles can work in practice. At the same time, you help further develop this field of expertise. You actively connect with potential applications and external partners and explore where this technology can add value. You can make complex science understandable to others and have the opportunity to take initiative in developing this new field. In this way, you help ensure that new quantum sensing technology moves beyond the lab and is translated into applications that are relevant to clients and ultimately contribute to the security of the Netherlands. What we expect from you We are looking for a specialist who enjoys building something new. You combine scientific depth with a hands-on mindset and enjoy taking an idea or scientific concept all the way to a working experimental setup. You work independently while actively seeking collaboration with colleagues and external partners. You take initiative, bring your own technical perspective and know how to build on the expertise of others. You are also interested in looking beyond the technology itself and contributing to new applications and collaborations. What you bring A Master's degree or PhD in Experimental Physics, Engineering or a comparable field. Hands-on experience in designing, building and testing quantum instrumentation, preferably based on Rydberg atoms. Experience with optical systems and electronics. Strong programming skills, particularly in Python. The ability to translate scientific knowledge into experimental designs and working setups. Initiative and an entrepreneurial mindset to help develop a new field of expertise. The ability to connect technology with potential applications and external partners. Strong communication skills in English. An independent and collaborative way of working. What you'll get in return Challenging and varied work with a real impact. And plenty of opportunities as, at TNO, you are in charge of shaping your career. We offer a gross monthly salary between €3500,- and € 5500,- (based on your knowledge and experience), 8% holiday pay, a 13th month bonus of 8.33% and a flex budget (5.58% + € 180). In addition, you will be given every opportunity to develop yourself. Perhaps you would like to grow your career in the direction of commerce or consultancy? Or would you like to become a project manager? Immerse yourself in sustainable innovations? Or carve out a career as a technical expert? TNO offers optional employee benefits, enabling you to tailor your benefits package to match your personal situation. You may also expect An extremely professional, innovative working environment where colleagues are leading experts in their field. The opportunity to attend courses, workshops and conferences, and to receive training and coaching based on your needs. 33 days annual leave plus a flexible holiday that can be used on a cultural, religious, or otherwise important day of your choosing (on a full-time basis). An employer working towards a respectful, inclusive, and equitable work environment where every employee can flourish, with various initiatives such as Jong TNO, numerous expertise based guilds, Rainbow Community and Round Tables on diverse inclusion topics. We offer a comprehensive and flexible mobility plan that also includes full compensation for public transportation for commuting and business travel. Great social events with your team …

items.card: vos missions et de trouver pleinement votre place au sein de nos équipes. Ce poste est peut-être fait pour vous. Alors osez vous lancer : cliquez, candidatez !
items.desc: Vous êtes rattaché au groupe Céramiques, Accidents et Modélisation (CAM) de l'ingénierie du combustible de la Business Unit Fuel, dont les activités principales sont de : Définir les exigences de conception et fabrication des céramiques nucléaires et traiter les écarts à celles-ci qui peuvent survenir lors de la fabrication. Participer au développement et à la qualification de nouveaux produits combustibles et justifier leur comportement en réacteur, par exemple les solutions EATF (Enhanced Accident Tolerant Fuel), le combustible TRISO (Tri-Structural Isotropic) ou pour RNR (réacteur à neutrons rapides). Réaliser des études spécifiques, via des outils de modélisation numérique, portant sur le comportement du combustible dans diverses situations. Etudier et justifier le comportement du crayon combustible dans les situations accidentelles. L’équipe CAM souhaite renforcer ses activités portant sur les céramiques nucléaires (UO2, MOX, B4C, SiC, etc.). Ainsi, en tant qu'ingénieur Matériaux Céramiques & Modélisation, vous réaliserez des activités de support à la fabrication des produits céramiques, des étude de R&D sur leurs comportement et propriétés et des travaux de modélisation thermomécanique. Plus précisément, les principales missions qui vous seront confiées sont : Des contributions à la documentation des exigences techniques encadrant la fabrication du combustible (spécification, plan, etc.), à la validation des évolutions des procédés de fabrication (qualification) et la gestion des écarts et anomalies survenant en usine. Des études de R&D, concernant la définition de solutions de combustible innovantes (EATF, combustible RNR ou TRISO, etc.) et visant l'amélioration des connaissances quant au comportement de ces produits. Selon vos prédispositions et motivations, des missions secondaires pourront être confiées: Des simulations numériques du comportement du combustible à l'aide d'outils de calculs scientifiques propres à Framatome ou externes (FEniCS, Cast3M, etc.). Le développement et la validation des outils de calculs et de leur environnement (outils de pré-, post-traitement, automatisation, etc.). Dans ces missions, vous serez en relation avec de nombreux interlocuteurs, en France et à l’international : Les usines de fabrication de combustible de la Direction des Opérations Fuel (DOF) de Framatome et celles des fournisseurs. Les autres services de l’ingénierie du combustible, notamment ceux responsables de la conception du crayon combustible ou de la neutronique. Les clients, les exploitants de réacteurs nucléaires. Profil Vous êtes titulaire d'un diplôme d'ingénieur, d'un équivalent universitaire ou d'un doctorat dans le domaine des Matériaux et/ou de la Mécanique. Idéalement, vous possédez une première expérience dans le domaine des céramiques nucléaires. Pour mener à bien vos activités, vous démontrez : Une bonne connaissance du comportement thermomécanique des matériaux. Une connaissance des céramiques nucléaires sera un atout indéniable. Un bon esprit de synthèse et d’analyse, avec la capacité de faire des recommandations et de prendre des décisions. Une première expérience dans les domaines de la R&D ou du support à la fabrication, démontrant ces aptitudes sera appréciée. Une bonne aptitude rédactionnelle et un niveau d’anglais opérationnel à l’oral comme à l’écrit. En complément, un élargissement des missions est possible, si vous montrez : La maitrise d'outils de calcul par la méthode des éléments finis, tels que FEniCS, ou Cast3m développé par le CEA. La maîtrise des langages de programmation, de manière privilégiée Python et Fortran, et une connaissance des systèmes de gestion de versions tel que Git. Le poste est à pourvoir à Lyon au sein d'un établissement soumis à enquête administrative. Vous ne cochez pas toutes les cases ? Postulez quand même ! Nous croyons autant au potentiel et à la motivation qu’au parcours et aux expériences. Chaque candidature est étudiée avec attention. L’accueil et l’intégration de nos collaborateurs sont au cœur de nos priorités : un accompagnement structuré vous permettra de prendre progressivement en main vos missions et de trouver pleinement votre place au sein de nos équipes. Ce poste est peut-être fait pour vous. Alors osez vous lancer : cliquez, candidatez !

Define scope and methodology of research projects that respond to real-world challenges faced by innovators, industry practitioners, and development actors, while aligning with the strategic objectives of funders and GSMA programmes.
